items.title: NeuralOpt
items.text:
A JAX research package for learned optimization, with replayable interval certification.

Status: alpha research package

NeuralOpt is for research on learned optimizers. In our own pre-registered and exploratory studies (v0.4–v0.7), the learned geometries did not beat validation-tuned fixed or Barzilai–Borwein baselines, and classical L-BFGS outperforms the learned optimizer on the reported benchmarks. See When to use NeuralOpt and the release notes.

NeuralOpt has two independent modes:

  • Learned mode. A compact transformer reads normalized position, gradient, bounds and budget features (and, opt-in, a masked history of evaluated states) and proposes the next step. No conventional optimizer runs during inference, and every objective and gradient evaluation is counted against one budget.
  • Certified mode. Interval branch-and-bound with outward rounding proves global bounds for a restricted expression language. It uses no learned component, and its certificates can be replayed by an independent verifier.

items.title: API reference
items.text: The public API is what neuralopt exports (neuralopt.__all__). Other modules, such as neuralopt.compiled, neuralopt.task_families and neuralopt.fast_training, are research interfaces that may change between minor versions.

items.title: preconditioned_solve
items.text:
preconditioned_solve(objective: Any, x0: Any, bounds: tuple[Any, Any], budget: int, *, theta: Any = None, params: Params | None = None, config: ModelConfig = DEFAULT_CONFIG, model_kind: str = 'transformer', geometry: str = 'learned', structure: str = 'full', fixed_metric_diag: Any = None, preconditioned_step: float | None = None, loop_rule: str = 'halving') -> dict[str, Any]

Run one compiled solve; returns host arrays (see :class:_State) plus status.

items.title: preconditioned_solve_batch
items.text:
preconditioned_solve_batch(objective: Any, thetas: Any, x0: Any, bounds: tuple[Any, Any], budget: int, *, params: Params | None = None, config: ModelConfig = DEFAULT_CONFIG, model_kind: str = 'transformer', geometry: str = 'learned', structure: str = 'full', fixed_metric_diag: Any = None, preconditioned_step: float | None = None, loop_rule: str = 'halving') -> dict[str, Any]

vmap the compiled solve over tasks objective(x, theta_i) of one dimension.

thetas, x0 and both bounds carry a leading task axis. Errors are not raised: inspect status per task (see :data:STATUS_MESSAGES).

items.title: Changelog
items.text: All notable changes to NeuralOpt. Each version has curated release notes; dates are UTC merge dates. Versions before 0.7.0 were tagged retroactively and are not on PyPI.

items.title: Unreleased
items.text: • Nothing yet.

• Track A (speed only, opt-in): preconditioned_engine="compiled" runs the v0.6 loop as one lax.while_loop (float64 parity with the Python loop to 1e-10), with a vmapped batch API; parametric task families and a compiled, batched, NaN-guarded trainer (train_batched, skipped updates counted). Engine and training benchmarks in results/engine-benchmark-v0.7.0.json; Optimistix added to the benchmark extra only.
  • Track B (opt-in, research): Gram-space history model (model_kind="gram", schema gram-v2), opt-in step-acceptance rules (loop_rule), gates 1-2, loop-rule ablation, mask diagnostic, a frozen pre-registration (sha256 recorded) and its training and evaluation infrastructure. Pre-registered result (negative): Stage 1 passed, but gram-full did not beat the untrained BB step on the curvature domain (H1 fails), the reliability guard trips on Rastrigin and Ackley, and the model is far from the oracle-BFGS ceiling. BB stays the bar. Exploratory post-mortem (training and validation tasks only): wider models imitate the oracle better but none performs well in the loop, and A/C gradients reach the heads without a saddle, so the cause is undetermined (leaning optimization signal). By plan gate G7 the line is not expanded.
  • Breaking: minimize(..., preconditioned_engine=...) now defaults to "compiled"; candidate_method="preconditioned" with a host/NumPy gradient= raises a ValueError naming preconditioned_engine="python". The v0.6 reproduction script pins "python" (its sha256 changed; frozen v0.6 results unchanged).
  • Breaking: neuralopt.__version__ comes from the package metadata; pyproject.toml is the single version source (.bumpversion.toml removed).
  • Next direction (2026-11-22): amortized optimization over problem families; learned guidance for certified search is deferred, not cancelled.
  • Release engineering: first PyPI release (trusted publishing), tag-driven GitHub releases, versioned docs (Zensical with its mike fork), curated release notes for every version, git-cliff with conventional PR titles, release-metadata checks on every PR, updated CITATION.cff and .zenodo.json, Citing page and logo.

PRs #7, #8 and the release-engineering PR · release notes

• Add opt-in history-v1 trajectory features (neuralopt.trajectory): a bounded buffer of actually evaluated normalized (u, g_u, f) records, masked secant pairs and twelve scale-invariant curvature/reliability features; versioned checkpoint schema that fails closed, with v0.1--v0.5 checkpoints and outputs pinned by a golden regression test.
  • Add candidate_method="preconditioned", a shared loop charging objective and gradient calls to one budget, and train(objective="history"), its differentiable mirror.
  • Pre-registered multi-seed study with a negative main result: an untrained Barzilai--Borwein step beats every learned arm by about one decade, and attention adds nothing over an MLP (H2). History plus a rejection signal helps over a matched control (H1); under a 3.5x anisotropy cap, learned geometry does not beat the tuned fixed step under the reliability rule (H3). Fixed geometry stays the default.

PR #6 · release notes

• Add scale-aware, bounded diagonal-plus-low-rank geometry while preserving legacy checkpoint behavior.
  • Add diagonal, low-rank, full, FP, and training-budget ablations with disjoint validation tuning and a 30-instance held-out comparison.
  • Reproduce v0.4 exactly and reconcile its pre-review and corrected FP results.
  • Retain the negative result that learned geometry did not beat tuned fixed geometry overall, with family-level failure analysis.

PR #5 · release notes

• Train transformer diagonal-plus-low-rank mobility and mass heads through differentiable overdamped and BAOAB trajectories.
  • Add multi-horizon stochastic regret, stability, fixed compute-cost, robust weak-generator, and optional Gaussian free-energy-surrogate losses.
  • Add identity, fixed-diagonal, untrained, regret-trained, and regret-plus-Fokker--Planck ablations with held-out paired confidence intervals.
  • Preserve negative results: learned BAOAB geometry does not beat the fixed diagonal baseline, and Fokker--Planck transfer to BAOAB is inconclusive.

PR #4 · release notes

• Add opt-in overdamped Euler--Maruyama and underdamped BAOAB candidate trajectories with identity or learned diagonal-plus-low-rank geometry.
  • Add exact small-dimensional Itô mobility divergence, weak Fokker--Planck diagnostics, and an analytic Gaussian free-energy reference.
  • Add a periodic Gaussian reference and mesh-normalized Fourier reconstruction experiment across four resolutions.
  • Add an optional Diffrax reference extra and retain negative learned-geometry smoke results with explicit objective, gradient, integration, and timing costs.
  • Record the gate status: distributional training and learned function-space transfer partial, certification injection blocked; certification lower bounds unchanged.

PR #3 · release notes

• Add evaluation-neutral trajectory diagnostics and correct stale state after rejection.
  • Add normalized coordinate transforms, differentiable multi-horizon regret unrolling, finite meta-gradient tests, and a matched-input MLP ablation.
  • Add deterministic certification scheduling controls and strengthen independent replay with pruned-leaf domain coverage and non-overlap checks.
  • Preserve a negative outcome-training smoke checkpoint without promoting it.
  • Add opt-in native JAX Hamiltonian proposals with transformed box constraints, fixed or learned mass geometry, separate exploration/incumbent state, explicit cost accounting, correctness tests, and matched-budget smoke evidence.

PR #2 · release notes

• Add direct transformer optimization policy, deterministic synthetic training, portable checkpoints, bounded problem API, and restricted interval certificates.
  • Add model-independent certificate replay, tests, research audit, honest smoke benchmark, and packaging metadata.

PR #1 · release notes

items.title: Citing NeuralOpt
items.text:
If you use NeuralOpt, please cite the exact version or commit you used. NeuralOpt is an alpha research package; it makes no performance claims, and several of its research results are negative (see the release notes).

The machine-readable source is CITATION.cff; GitHub's "Cite this repository" button renders it.

NeuralOpt is archived on Zenodo from v0.7.0 on. The concept DOI 10.5281/zenodo.24444016 always resolves to the latest archived version. Each release also has its own version DOI, listed on its Zenodo record; cite that one to pin an exact version.

Field Value Title NeuralOpt: a JAX research package for learned optimization, with replayable interval certification Version 0.7.0 DOI (concept, all versions) 10.5281/zenodo.24444016 Author Mishra, Abhinav (Independent Researcher), ORCID 0009-0005-3179-7408 Repository https://github.com/bibymaths/neuralopt Documentation https://bibymaths.github.io/neuralopt/ License MIT

items.title: Installation
items.text:
NeuralOpt needs Python 3.11 or newer. It depends on JAX and NumPy only.

pip install neuralopt

Optional extras:

Extra Adds Needed for neuralopt[train] Optax training checkpoints (neuralopt train-demo, train_batched) neuralopt[benchmark] SciPy, Optimistix the benchmark scripts' reference solvers (never used in inference) neuralopt[sde] Diffrax the optional SDE reference checks

JAX installs its CPU build by default. For GPU support, follow the JAX installation guide.

items.title: From source
items.text:
git clone https://github.com/bibymaths/neuralopt
cd neuralopt
uv sync --extra dev            # tests, lint, type checks
uv sync --extra dev --group docs   # plus the documentation toolchain
uv run pytest -q

Versions before 0.7.0 are not on PyPI. To use one, install from its git tag, for example pip install "git+https://github.com/bibymaths/neuralopt@v0.6.0".

items.title: Limitations
items.text: NeuralOpt is an alpha research package. Read these before interpreting any result.

items.title: Learned optimization
items.text:
• No learned geometry has beaten its simple baselines. Learned BAOAB geometry did not beat a fixed diagonal (v0.4); learned geometry did not beat validation-tuned fixed geometry (v0.5); an untrained Barzilai–Borwein step beat every learned arm by about a decade (v0.6); the pre-registered Gram-space model did not beat BB (v0.7). Classical L-BFGS outperforms the learned optimizer on the reported benchmarks.
  • The bundled demo-v0.1.0 checkpoint is a smoke artifact.
  • Learned mode needs gradients and supports box constraints only; residuals and nonlinear constraints are metadata, not implemented constrained optimization.
  • The compiled engine needs JAX-traceable objectives; host gradients run on the Python loop only.

items.title: Certification
items.text:
• Certified mode supports an explicit expression language, not JAXPR or arbitrary JAX.
  • The nextafter backend assumes correctly rounded binary64 host operations and libm; it is not IEEE 1788 conformant and is not a formal proof across platforms.
  • Replay checks the retained bounds and domain accounting; it does not prove the implementation or hardware.
  • Neural or stochastic predictions never certify global optimality.

items.title: Detailed records
items.text:
• Limitations as recorded in v0.1–v0.2
  • Stochastic research limitations and gate record (v0.3–v0.4)
  • Per-version limitations: the "Known limitations" section of each release note.

items.title: Learned mode
items.text:
import jax.numpy as jnp
from neuralopt import Problem, minimize

problem = Problem(lambda x: jnp.sum((x - 2) ** 2), (-5.0, 5.0), 10)
result = minimize(problem, max_evaluations=100, seed=42)
print(result.status, result.fun, result.evaluations)

The default call loads the bundled demo-v0.1.0 checkpoint, trained for 100 updates on synthetic quadratics. It is a smoke artifact, not a validated general optimizer: on this problem it stops at f ≈ 0.37 after 100 evaluations, where the minimum is 0. Pass params= and config= to run another checkpoint.

items.title: The preconditioned loop (compiled)
items.text:
result = minimize(problem, max_evaluations=100, candidate_method="preconditioned",
                  record_diagnostics=True)
d = result.diagnostics
print(d["engine"], result.fun, d["objective_evaluations"], d["gradient_evaluations"])

This runs the v0.6 step-acceptance loop as one compiled XLA program (the default engine since v0.7.0). See Compiled engine.

items.title: Certified mode
items.text:
from neuralopt import Problem, Variable, minimize, verify_certificate

x = Variable()
expr = (x[0] - 0.25) ** 2
p = Problem(lambda z: (z[0] - 0.25) ** 2, (-1.0, 1.0), 1, certified_expression=expr)
r = minimize(p, mode="certified", absolute_gap=1e-4, max_evaluations=10000)
assert verify_certificate(r.certificate)
print(r.status, r.lower_bound, r.upper_bound)

Certified mode accepts only the package's expression subset. See Certified mode.

items.title: Train a demo checkpoint
items.text:
pip install "neuralopt[train]"
neuralopt train-demo --steps 100 --output model.npz

items.title: When to use NeuralOpt
items.text: Short answer: to solve an optimization problem, use a classical solver. Use NeuralOpt to study learned optimizers, or for its restricted certified mode.

items.title: Use SciPy or Optimistix when you want a good answer
items.text:
• SciPy minimize(method="L-BFGS-B") for bounded, smooth problems on the CPU.
  • Optimistix (LBFGS, BFGS, …) for JAX-native, jit/vmap-able solves.

In the v0.7 equal-work benchmark (32 rotated κ = 100 quadratics, d = 16, 100 units of objective plus gradient work each), SciPy L-BFGS-B and Optimistix LBFGS reached a regret of 1e-6 on 32 of 32 tasks. NeuralOpt's learned geometry reached 1e-3 on 10 of 32 and 1e-6 on none (engine-speed report). Across v0.4–v0.7 the learned geometries did not beat validation-tuned fixed-diagonal or Barzilai–Borwein steps (release notes).

items.title: Use NeuralOpt when you want to
items.text:
• Research learned optimizers with honest accounting: a shared evaluation budget, masked histories built only from evaluated states, versioned checkpoint schemas, frozen pre-registrations and paired comparisons against fixed and classical references.
  • Run a learned update rule fast: the compiled engine runs the loop as one XLA program and vmaps over task families.
  • Get a replayable global certificate for a small expression in the supported subset (+, -, *, square, sin, exp) on a box, with certified mode. For general global optimization, use a dedicated deterministic global solver.

items.title: Do not use NeuralOpt for
items.text:
• Production optimization, or any claim that a learned step is better than L-BFGS.
  • Certifying arbitrary JAX programs: certified mode is restricted to its expression language, and neural or stochastic outputs never certify optimality.
  • Constrained problems beyond box bounds.

items.title: Held-out quadratic smoke result
items.text:
On 15 November 2026, the 100-step demo checkpoint was evaluated on three held-out four-dimensional quadratic instances (seed 42, budget 100). Median final objective was 13.0525 for the trained policy, 195.745 for random policy weights, and 2.14e-12 for SciPy L-BFGS-B with analytic JAX gradients. Median end-to-end times were 0.635 s, 0.652 s, and 0.0329 s respectively on the onboarding CPU environment. Compilation was included.

The trained policy improved on random initialization but lost decisively to the conventional baseline. This rejects H2 for this small task distribution and checkpoint. Three instances are a smoke check, not statistical evidence for H1. Raw measurements are in results/heldout-smoke.json; training loss fell from 0.260531 to 0.00994861 in 100 updates (about 12 seconds).

items.title: Certified mode
items.text: minimize(problem, mode="certified", absolute_gap=..., max_evaluations=...) proves a global lower bound by interval branch-and-bound. No learned component affects the bounds: interval evaluation with outward rounding is the only source of the certificate.

items.title: Supported expressions
items.text:
Build the objective with Variable and the operators +, -, *, square (**2), sin and exp, and pass it as certified_expression. Arbitrary JAX code cannot enter certified mode; division, logarithms, arbitrary powers and constraints are unsupported and fail closed.

from neuralopt import Problem, Variable, minimize, verify_certificate

x = Variable()
expr = (x[0] - 0.25) ** 2
p = Problem(lambda z: (z[0] - 0.25) ** 2, (-1.0, 1.0), 1, certified_expression=expr)
r = minimize(p, mode="certified", absolute_gap=1e-4, max_evaluations=10000)
print(r.status, r.lower_bound, r.upper_bound)
assert verify_certificate(r.certificate)

items.title: Independent replay
items.text: verify_certificate re-evaluates every retained interval bound, checks that the leaf boxes lie inside the domain and cover it without positive-volume overlap, and checks the final gap. It does not use the search code's state.

items.title: Assumptions
items.text: Outward rounding uses numpy.nextafter in binary64 and assumes correctly rounded host operations and libm. It is not IEEE 1788 conformant and is not a formal proof across arbitrary platforms. See certified scheduling and the limitations.

items.title: Compiled engine
items.text:
Since v0.7.0, minimize(..., candidate_method="preconditioned") runs on the compiled engine by default (preconditioned_engine="compiled"): the whole loop is one lax.while_loop inside one jit. It computes the same rule as the Python loop (float64 parity to 1e-10) and is much faster; it does not change what the optimizer achieves.

result = minimize(problem, max_evaluations=100, candidate_method="preconditioned")

items.title: Requirements
items.text:
• The objective must be JAX-traceable. A problem with a host/NumPy gradient= raises a ValueError; pass preconditioned_engine="python" for it.
  • Reuse the same objective function object to reuse the compilation.

items.title: Batched solves
items.text: neuralopt.compiled.preconditioned_solve_batch vmaps the loop over tasks objective(x, theta_i) of one family and dimension; neuralopt.task_families provides parametric families. Under vmap, both branches of the acceptance lax.cond are computed, but gradients are charged only on acceptance.

items.title: Speed (v0.7 benchmark)
items.text: One warm learned (tf-h8) solve took 296.1 ms on the Python loop and 4.00 ms compiled (about 74×). See the engine-speed report for the equal-work benchmark against SciPy and Optimistix, cold and batched timings, and the caveats.

items.title: Learned mode
items.text: minimize(problem, mode="learned", ...) (the default mode) runs a learned policy on a box-bounded problem. Learned mode requires a JAX-differentiable objective or an explicit gradient=.

items.title: Problems
items.text:
from neuralopt import Problem

problem = Problem(
    objective,            # f(x) -> scalar
    (lower, upper),       # scalars or arrays, finite, lower < upper
    dimension,
    x0=None,              # default: the box centre
    gradient=None,        # optional host gradient (Python engine only, see below)
    max_evaluations=1000,
    dtype=jnp.float32,    # use jnp.float64 (with x64 enabled) for research runs
)

items.title: Candidate methods
items.text:
candidate_method What proposes the next point "direct" (default) the transformer emits the step directly (v0.1 policy) "preconditioned" step u' = clip(u − σ L P ĝ, −1, 1) with a learned, fixed or identity metric; one objective call per candidate, a gradient only on acceptance, σ halves after a rejection (v0.6) "hamiltonian" Hamiltonian proposals with identity, fixed or learned mass (v0.2) "langevin", "underdamped" overdamped Euler–Maruyama or BAOAB trajectories (v0.3–v0.4)

For "preconditioned", hamiltonian_metric selects "learned", "fixed" (with fixed_metric_diag and preconditioned_step) or "identity" geometry.

items.title: Checkpoints
items.text:
• params=None loads the bundled demo-v0.1.0 smoke checkpoint (legacy 5-feature model).
  • History models (ModelConfig(feature_set="history-v1", history_length=K)) need candidate_method="preconditioned" and carry a versioned schema; unknown or inconsistent schemas fail closed. v0.1–v0.5 checkpoints load identically.
  • model_kind="mlp" and model_kind="gram" need caller-provided parameters; the Gram model (v0.7) runs on the compiled engine only.

items.title: Accounting
items.text:
With record_diagnostics=True, result.diagnostics reports objective, gradient and HVP evaluations, accepted and rejected steps, and per-step records. result.evaluations is the total charged to the budget.

See the research reports for what these models do and do not achieve.

items.title: NeuralOpt v0.6 onward — trajectory-aware curvature plan
items.text: Status (2026-11-21): G0–G2 implemented (opt-in history-v1, shared preconditioned loop); first pre-registered round run: H1 supported, H2 and H3 not supported, so G3 attention, G5 and G6 are not started — see docs/research/trajectory-curvature-v0.6.md. Original status: research proposal / Claude Code handoff. Repo main inspected 2026-11-21, version 0.5.0. Frozen v0.5 negative result remains canonical.
path: NeuralOpt v0.6 onward — trajectory-aware curvature plan

items.title: Objective and novelty test
items.text:
Can a small sequence-aware learned optimizer infer useful cross-coordinate curvature from past evaluated states and transfer that geometry to unseen rotated, ill-conditioned, noisy and higher-dimensional landscapes, beating a validation-tuned fixed-diagonal baseline on best-feasible regret per objective/gradient cost and time?

Candidate contribution is not 'transformer + BFGS': Optimus (2023) and L-SR1 (2026) already learn curvature updates. The hypothesis is observation-efficient, uncertainty-aware curvature encoding with rigorous cross-task generalization and precision/cost accounting, integrated into NeuralOpt's existing learned direct and stochastic trajectories.
path: NeuralOpt v0.6 onward — trajectory-aware curvature plan

items.title: Architectural contract
items.text:
• Reuse features.py, model.py, optimizer.py, training.py, stochastic_geometry.py.
  • Keep parameter_features with 5 features per coordinate and legacy ModelConfig checkpoint path intact. Use opt-in versioned history_mode/schema; no silent shape-based migration.
  • Minimal bounded ring buffer K = 4 then K = 8 of actually evaluated normalized (u, g_u, f, mask) observations. Stable JAX PyTree shapes and bounded O(Kd) memory.
  • Derived: s = Δu, y = Δg_u, reliable s^T y, norms, gradient alignment, objective difference, reliability/conditioning, optional low-rank sketch. Initial 'history summary' model should be non-attention; only later permit cross-attention.
  • P = diag(d) + U U^T stays SPD; negative secant curvature is diagnostic and masks/learned uncertainty, not an illegal inverse Hessian assertion.
  • For optimization, incumbent must be verified; stochastic search state may move uphill. No classical optimizer dispatch in production inference.

path: NeuralOpt v0.6 onward — trajectory-aware curvature plan

items.title: G1 — Synthetic secant truth
items.text: Build deterministic test fixtures, not a new solver: known diagonal/rotated SPD Hessians, indefinite quadratics, noisy gradients and mismatched coordinate scales. Verify y = H_u s with measured pairs and the correct normalization Jacobian. Measure rank(span(S)), unbiased/noisy sample behaviour. Stop if source states or gradients are incoherent.
path: NeuralOpt v0.6 onward — trajectory-aware curvature plan

items.title: G2 — Minimal masked history feature
items.text: Add fixed-shape ring buffer and no-attention secant statistics, versioned checkpoint schema, and cost-aware inference. Tests: rejected candidate, repeated point, noisy pair, no-history identity, dimensions 2/4/8/10, JIT/VMAP/grad. Stop if legacy regressions fail or memory/time cost dominates without improved information.
path: NeuralOpt v0.6 onward — trajectory-aware curvature plan

items.title: G3 — Trajectory-aware neural representation
items.text: Only after G2 evidence: small temporal attention / Set Transformer-style cross-attention over K valid pairs and per-coordinate tokens, with explicit time order and permutation equivariance of coordinates. Compare against matched MLP history summary. No model-width scale-up as first step.
path: NeuralOpt v0.6 onward — trajectory-aware curvature plan

items.title: G4 — Curvature-regularized meta-training
items.text: Multi-horizon regret plus optional soft inverse-secant consistency, HVP identification/probe ablation and reliability-aware masking. Test correct low-rank geometry in normalized coordinates, stabilization, true gradients and held-out performance. Do not incorporate PINN collocation or self-scaled Broyden solver as an inference engine.
path: NeuralOpt v0.6 onward — trajectory-aware curvature plan

items.title: G5 — Stochastic reuse (only if G3/G4 outperform fixed diagonal)
items.text: Feed trajectory curvature into learned mass/mobility for HMC, overdamped and BAOAB. Keep fluctuation–dissipation, metric convention and sampling/inference correctness; compare to fixed diagonal with matched gradient/integration cost. Keep FP weak-form as optional regularizer; don't claim exact Gibbs invariance under online adaptation.
path: NeuralOpt v0.6 onward — trajectory-aware curvature plan

items.title: G6 — Function-space and certified-search compatibility
items.text: Existing field covariance and Fourier Nyquist tests remain. Apply resolution-aware secant features only in a small compatible field experiment, then test optional feasible-incumbent candidate injection. Interval lower bounds, pruning and independent replay remain authoritative. Do not attempt a new PDE solver.
path: NeuralOpt v0.6 onward — trajectory-aware curvature plan

items.title: G7 — Publication-grade decision
items.text: Run pre-registered multi-seed held-out family/dimension comparisons; compute paired confidence intervals and total cost. Publish negative results and select simplest supported model. If no benefit, retain fixed diagonal, archive experimental trajectory model, and stop expansion.
path: NeuralOpt v0.6 onward — trajectory-aware curvature plan

items.title: Suggested research hypotheses
items.text:
• H1: history improves rotated/ill-conditioned regret over no-history matched model at same evaluation budget.
  • H2: attention adds value beyond hand-computed secant statistics and an MLP.
  • H3: learned geometry beats validation-tuned fixed diagonal on unseen families/dimensions under cost accounting.
  • H4: curvature transfer to BAOAB or function spaces improves downstream best feasible objective without sacrificing correctness.
path: NeuralOpt v0.6 onward — trajectory-aware curvature plan

items.title: Prohibited shortcuts
items.text: No PINNs; no benchmark leakage; no new BFGS inference fallback; no unreplayable certificate; no uncounted HVP/gradient calls; no overwriting existing artifacts; no oversized architecture first; no default API break; no sweeping release claims.
path: NeuralOpt v0.6 onward — trajectory-aware curvature plan

items.title: NeuralOpt v0.8 plan: amortized optimization over problem families
items.text:
Status: approved direction (Option A, 2026-11-22); this revision awaits approval. Nothing in it has been built. The claims it tests are listed, with their decision criteria, in docs/research/v0.8-claims.md.

Release freeze. - There is no v0.8.0 tag, PyPI upload or GitHub release until every claim in the register has a pre-registered result and the user has approved the release. - Until a claim's status is "supported", the README, docs, CHANGELOG and release notes call it "under test".
path: NeuralOpt v0.8 plan: amortized optimization over problem families

items.title: 1. Goal
items.text:
Many problems come as a family f(θ; c): - θ is the parameter vector to estimate, for example kinetic rate constants; - c is the instance's context: its observed data and its conditions, such as dose.

Members of a family share structure, and their solutions move with c.

Question. Can a model trained on one family supply starting points from which a local optimizer lands in the right basin more often and more cheaply than generic strategies? The generic strategies are a default start, multistart, and a nearest-neighbour lookup. And does any advantage survive distribution shift and pay back its offline cost?

What is learned and what is not: - Learned: the start predictor g_φ(c). - Not learned: the refinement, which is NeuralOpt's own classical, pure-JAX L-BFGS. This differs from v0.4–v0.7, where the learned part was the step rule and every learned geometry lost to a fixed diagonal or the BB step. - Kept: the learned-step transformer stays in the package as a documented research mode. Those negative results remain authoritative for it.

Prior expectation, stated honestly: - A nearest-neighbour start is often strong for smooth families. - Multistart may already be cheap for small, well-identified problems. - Gate F0 measures this before anything is learned.
path: NeuralOpt v0.8 plan: amortized optimization over problem families

items.title: 2. Pipeline at inference
items.text:
c ──► g_φ(c) ──► θ̂ (or K candidates + confidence) ──► owned L-BFGS ──► θ̂*
                                                          │
             low confidence or poor refined fit ──► fallback: owned multistart L-BFGS
  • Every objective and gradient call goes through one counted budget, including fallback calls.
  • The g_φ forward pass is not an objective evaluation. Its cold and warm time is measured and reported (claim C10).
  • No SciPy, Optimistix or other external solver runs at inference.
path: NeuralOpt v0.8 plan: amortized optimization over problem families

items.title: 3. Component 1: owned L-BFGS (classical, not learned)
items.text: Purpose: the refinement for every NeuralOpt arm, and the local solver inside NeuralOpt multistart and fallback. It is documented as a classical method.
path: NeuralOpt v0.8 plan: amortized optimization over problem families

items.title: Design (neuralopt.lbfgs, opt-in, pure JAX)
items.text:
• Memory and direction: limited memory m (default 10). The two-loop recursion runs only on curvature pairs with sᵀy > ε‖s‖‖y‖; other pairs are skipped and the skip is counted.
  • Initial scaling γ = sᵀy / yᵀy from the newest pair.
  • Box bounds, by projection:
  • The free set is the variables not at a bound whose gradient would not push them out of the box.
  • The direction is the L-BFGS direction restricted to the free set; bound variables take the projected-gradient component.
  • Trial points are P_box(x + α d).
  • A backtracking Armijo condition is checked along the projection arc, with sufficient decrease measured against gᵀ(P_box(x + α d) − x).
  • The direction is reset to the projected gradient when it is not a descent direction.
  • Stopping:
  • the projected-gradient norm ‖P_box(x − g) − x‖_∞ falls below a tolerance;
  • the relative change in f falls below a tolerance;
  • or the budget is exhausted.
  • Accounting (the same convention as the NeuralOpt loop):
  • each line-search trial costs one objective call;
  • the gradient is computed only at the accepted point (one gradient call);
  • a trial is proposed only while used + 2 ≤ budget;
  • nonfinite values reject the trial and are counted;
  • counters are returned per solve.
  • Execution:
  • one lax.while_loop inside one jit;
  • vmap over a batch of (c, x0), and over K starts for multistart;
  • under vmap, both lax.cond branches are computed, but calls are charged only when taken, as in neuralopt.compiled.
  • Precision: float64 for all v0.8 work.
path: NeuralOpt v0.8 plan: amortized optimization over problem families

items.title: Tests (written first)
items.text:
1. Quadratics:
  2. Unconstrained SPD quadratics, d ∈ {2, 8, 32}, κ ∈ {1, 1e2, 1e4}: converge to the analytic minimizer, with projected-gradient norm ≤ 1e-8 within the budget.
  3. On a quadratic, the stored pairs satisfy y = H s to 1e-10.
  4. SciPy reference at matched budget, on the v0.7 engine-benchmark set (32 rotated κ = 100 quadratics, d = 16, 100 units each, results/engine-benchmark-v0.7.0.json protocol) and on the v0.7 rotated curvature tasks:
  5. the owned L-BFGS reaches regret ≤ 1e-6 on at least as many tasks as SciPy L-BFGS-B minus one;
  6. its median log10 regret is within 1.0 decade of SciPy's;
  7. its median units to 1e-6 are within 1.5× SciPy's.
  8. SciPy's counts use the existing harness accounting: every SciPy call is one objective plus one gradient.
  9. Bounded problems:
  10. quadratics whose minimizer lies outside the box, on a face, an edge or a corner;
  11. Rosenbrock in a box that clips the optimum.
  12. Each must reach the projected KKT point: projected-gradient norm ≤ 1e-8, with active bounds identified correctly. Iterates never leave the box.
  13. Accounting:
  14. counted objective and gradient calls equal wrapped-callback counts;
  15. the budget is never exceeded;
  16. nonfinite trials are rejected and counted.
  17. Parity:
  18. float64 single versus batched (vmap) solves give identical trajectories and counts to 1e-12;
  19. repeated solves with a new context of the same shape do not recompile.
path: NeuralOpt v0.8 plan: amortized optimization over problem families

items.title: 4. Component 2: start predictor g_φ (the learned part)
items.text:
• Input: the context as a set of observation tokens. Each token holds (time, measured value, species/channel id, condition features such as dose, observation-noise level if known).
  • Instances may have different numbers and spacings of time points.
  • Masked self-attention runs over the tokens, then masked mean and attention pooling.
  • Condition variables shared by the instance enter as an extra token.
  • Output:
  • θ̂ in log-parameter space, mapped into the box with a scaled tanh (always inside the bounds);
  • option K: K candidate starts plus a confidence score: a calibrated probability that refinement from the top candidate reaches success.
  • Training data:
  • simulated instances: parameters sampled from the family prior, model simulated, realistic noise added;
  • solved instances: the reference optimum θ* of each training instance, from a harness-only reference multistart. Training uses no test instance.
  • Losses compared (pre-registered; the comparison is claim C7):
  • regression to the reference optimum: ‖ĝ − log θ*‖² in normalized coordinates;
  • objective-based: minimize f(θ̂; c), optionally after k unrolled L-BFGS steps;
  • for K starts, a best-of-K loss min_k ℓ(θ̂_k), with a diversity check so the candidates do not collapse.
  • The confidence head is trained with a binary loss on "refinement from this start reached success", from training-split solves only.
  • Inference:
  • one forward pass;
  • L-BFGS from the top candidate, or from all K candidates batched;
  • fallback to owned multistart L-BFGS when the confidence is below a threshold τ_c or the refined fit fails a fit check.
  • The fit check is the refined objective above a family-specific threshold derived from the noise model, for example a reduced-χ² bound.
  • τ_c and the fit threshold are tuned on validation only. The fallback calls count in the same budget.
  • Checkpoints: a versioned schema, neuralopt-start/v0.8-v1, that fails closed. Earlier checkpoint formats are unaffected.
path: NeuralOpt v0.8 plan: amortized optimization over problem families

items.title: 5. Arms
items.text:
All arms use the same instances, matched objective + gradient units, float64 and CPU. Wall time is reported cold, warm and batched.

# Arm Start Refinement Role A0 default start + owned L-BFGS family default θ_d owned L-BFGS no amortization (C1 comparator) A1 default start + SciPy L-BFGS-B θ_d SciPy harness reference A2 multistart SciPy L-BFGS-B Sobol starts, count and split validation-tuned SciPy generic reference (C2 with A2o, C5) A2o multistart owned L-BFGS K Sobol/random starts owned L-BFGS C2 uses the better of A2 and A2o on each axis; K-random comparator (C6); also the fallback A3 nearest-neighbour start + owned L-BFGS θ* of the nearest training context owned L-BFGS lookup bar (C3) A4 learned start + owned L-BFGS g_φ(c) owned L-BFGS primary (C1–C4, C9, C10) A4K learned K starts + owned L-BFGS (batched) top-K of g_φ owned L-BFGS C6 A4F A4 with confidence check and fallback g_φ(c) owned L-BFGS + fallback C5, C8 A5 learned start + SciPy L-BFGS-B g_φ(c) SciPy harness only: separates the start from the refinement

Nearest neighbour: - Distance is measured on a context representation fixed before any test data is seen: - observations interpolated to a common time grid per species; - each time point standardized with training-split statistics; - condition features appended. - Lookup time is reported. Lookups use no objective units.
path: NeuralOpt v0.8 plan: amortized optimization over problem families

items.title: 6. Metrics
items.text:
• Reference optimum f*: harness-only multistart L-BFGS-B with 64 Sobol starts × 2,000 units, plus the true-parameter start when it is known.
  • It must be reproduced by a second Sobol seed within ε on ≥ 99% of validation instances. If not, the budget is raised.
  • If any arm beats it, it is updated and that fact is reported.
  • Success: f(θ̂) − f* ≤ ε_abs + ε_rel·|f*|, with ε fixed per family before F0. Success is measured on the objective.
  • Parameter error: reported only together with an identifiability check: profile flatness, or the condition number and eigenvalues of the Fisher information at θ* (for least squares, JᵀJ/σ²).
  • Directions with flat profiles or tiny Fisher eigenvalues are reported as non-identified, not as errors.
  • Cost:
  • objective, gradient and HVP calls, always reported separately for every arm, because a JAX/ODE gradient costs several objective calls;
  • the measured gradient/objective cost ratio per family, from the F0 timing probe;
  • accepted steps;
  • wall time cold (including compilation), warm and batched;
  • g_φ and nearest-neighbour time, listed separately;
  • fallback rate and fallback units.
  • Time and units to success: censored at the budget. Also the success rate as a function of budget.
  • Break-even (C4): N* = T_offline / (t_generic − t_amortized).
  • T_offline = simulating the training set + solving all training targets (reference multistart) + training (compilation and updates).
  • t = mean time to success at a matched success rate.
  • Reported as a number with an interval and the measurement protocol. "No break-even" when t_amortized ≥ t_generic.
  • Statistics:
  • paired per-instance differences, positive = worse;
  • percentile-bootstrap 95% intervals over instances;
  • paired intervals for success-rate differences;
  • per-family and per-split tables with failure and nonfinite counts;
  • ≥ 5 predictor training seeds for learned arms, with each instance's outcome the mean over seeds; per-seed spread is reported;
  • every claim's criterion is applied per family/variant.
path: NeuralOpt v0.8 plan: amortized optimization over problem families

items.title: 7. Splits (fixed, hashed, written once)
items.text:
• Instance i of split s uses seed = hash(family, variant, split, i).
  • Each split has a manifest listing contexts and true parameters, with its sha256 recorded.
  • No tuning, model selection or threshold is set on a test split.
Split Purpose Size (initial) train simulated + solved instances for g_φ, the nearest-neighbour index, confidence labels 2,000 validation all tuning (baselines, τ_c, fit thresholds, early stopping) and F0 200 test (in-distribution) final comparison, opened once 200 test (OOD) final comparison, opened once 200 per shift

OOD shifts, each a separate named split: 1. a higher noise level; 2. true parameters outside the training range, but inside the optimization box; 3. different sampling times: count, spacing and sparsity; 4. Family 2 only: doses outside the training range.
path: NeuralOpt v0.8 plan: amortized optimization over problem families

items.title: 8. Families
path: NeuralOpt v0.8 plan: amortized optimization over problem families

items.title: Family 1: damped-sinusoid fitting (synthetic, known multimodality)
items.text:
• Model: y(t) = a · exp(−λt) · sin(2πωt + φ) + ε, with θ = (a, λ, ω, φ), d = 4.
  • Context: the observed series.
  • Objective: the mean squared residual.
  • Why: frequency aliasing and harmonics give local minima in ω, whose number grows with the sampling span. This multimodality is known and controllable, and the truth is known.
path: NeuralOpt v0.8 plan: amortized optimization over problem families

items.title: Family 2: two-step Michaelis–Menten cascade (ODE, d = 4–5)
items.text:
• Model: S →(E1) I →(E2) P, with θ = log(V1, K1, V2, K2), plus an optional degradation rate (d = 5).
  • Solver: float64 fixed-step RK4 in JAX. The step is chosen so the error is ≤ 1e-8 relative against a 16× finer reference over the validation box.
  • Objective: weighted least squares over the observed species, with known noise σ.
  • Variants:
  • 2a, clean: dense sampling and low noise. This is the control.
  • 2b, realistic:
    • sparse sampling times (5–8 points, irregular);
    • noise at 5–10% of the signal;
    • condition-dependent inputs: dose (initial S0, or a bolus into S at a stated time), varied per instance;
    • only P observed, plus I at a subset of the times.
  • Variant 2b is intended to produce real local minima and near-flat directions. F0 checks whether it actually does, by counting the distinct converged optima per instance across reference starts.
path: NeuralOpt v0.8 plan: amortized optimization over problem families

items.title: Family 3: real dataset from the user's kinetic modelling work (later)
items.text: Only after Families 1 and 2 pass their gates, and under its own addendum: provenance, the split by experiment or condition, noise model, and licence.
path: NeuralOpt v0.8 plan: amortized optimization over problem families

items.title: 9. Gate F0: headroom, with no learning
items.text:
What runs: - Arms A0, A1, A2, A2o and A3 and the reference; - on the validation split of each family and variant; - at budgets of {25, 50, 100, 200, 400, 800} units.

Headroom on two axes, per family and variant: - B95_multi: the smallest budget at which multistart L-BFGS-B (A2) reaches 95% success. The owned version, A2o, is reported alongside. - B95_NN: the same for the nearest-neighbour start + owned L-BFGS (A3). - c_local: the median units of a single local solve from the default start (A0) to its own stopping criterion.

Stop rule (pre-registered before F0 runs): - A family or variant stops only if B95_multi ≤ 2 · c_local. Then multistart is essentially as cheap as one local solve, and there is no headroom to amortize. - If B95_NN ≤ 2 · c_local, a lookup already amortizes the family. This is recorded, and claim C3 becomes the decisive test for that family. - Also reported: the share of instances that no generic arm solves at 800 units (the hard set), and the number of distinct converged optima per instance.

Timing probe first: - It measures warm, batched µs per objective and per gradient call for each family. - The full F0 compute is projected from it. - Cap: 6 CPU-hours through F0. If the projection exceeds it, I stop and report before running.
path: NeuralOpt v0.8 plan: amortized optimization over problem families

items.title: 10. Training targets and offline cost
items.text:
• Evaluation reference: 128k units per instance.
  • Training targets: a cheaper reference, 16 starts × 1,000 units. It must match the evaluation reference within ε on ≥ 98% of validation instances; if not, its budget is raised.
  • All of this cost is part of T_offline (C4).
path: NeuralOpt v0.8 plan: amortized optimization over problem families

items.title: 11. Gates and stop points
items.text:
Stop After Content 1 this plan, CLAUDE.md update and claims register committed (all claims "unverified") approval 2 owned L-BFGS + tests, families + splits, gate F0 headroom report per family 3 the v0.8 pre-registration, frozen and hashed, with every claim's criterion approval before any training 4 the study (training, in-distribution test, OOD test) claims register updated; every outcome reported as found; release decision is the user's

Track v0.8-B (§15) starts only after stop point 2. It has its own plan approval and pre-registration stops before any implementation or training.

Exploratory results may be reported but cannot change a claim's status. Each stop is preceded by the full local quality gate.
path: NeuralOpt v0.8 plan: amortized optimization over problem families

items.title: 12. Rules
items.text:
• Test first; float64; no uncounted evaluations; never form secants from un-evaluated states.
  • Frozen artifacts are never overwritten. v0.8 results are versioned (results/*-v0.8.0.json).
  • External solvers are references only. No PINNs or PDE collocation. Certification stays independent and model-free.
  • Squash merges with conventional PR titles. Research PRs may be merged only when every CI check passes. No tags or releases.
path: NeuralOpt v0.8 plan: amortized optimization over problem families

items.title: 13. Prior work (verified; no novelty claim over it)
items.text:
• Amos, B. Tutorial on Amortized Optimization. Foundations and Trends in Machine Learning, 2023. arXiv:2202.00665.
  • The taxonomy used here: regression-based versus objective-based amortization, and fully amortized versus semi-amortized models.
  • Sambharya, R., Hall, G., Amos, B., Stellato, B. Learning to Warm-Start Fixed-Point Optimization Algorithms. Journal of Machine Learning Research 25(166):1–46, 2024. arXiv:2309.07835.
  • A learned warm start followed by a fixed iteration scheme. v0.8's pipeline follows this pattern, using L-BFGS on small nonconvex parameter-estimation families. It is not a new method.
  • Zammit-Mangion, A., Sainsbury-Dale, M., Huser, R. Neural Methods for Amortized Inference. Annual Review of Statistics and Its Application, 2025. doi:10.1146/annurev-statistics-112723-034123.
  • A survey of amortized parameter estimation with neural networks: the comparison point for g_φ as an amortized point estimator.
  • Chosen over Cranmer, Brehmer and Louppe (PNAS 2020), which is broader.

All three were checked against OpenAlex; the JMLR volume was checked on jmlr.org.
path: NeuralOpt v0.8 plan: amortized optimization over problem families

items.title: 14. Risks
items.text: Risk Mitigation No headroom (multistart is cheap) F0 stop rule B95_multi ≤ 2·c_local; report plainly A lookup does as well A3 is a required bar; C3 says so plainly if it holds Regression averages over modes objective-based and best-of-K losses (C7, C6) Overconfident starts silently miss optima confidence + fit-check fallback, evaluated as C5 The owned L-BFGS is weaker than SciPy its acceptance tests (§3) precede F0; A5 separates start from refinement The reference optimum is not global two-seed reproduction; updated when beaten Non-identifiable parameters success on the objective; parameter error only with identifiability checks ODE solver error fine-step reference check Leakage validation-only tuning; hashed splits; tests opened once Unfair wall time cold, warm and batched times separate; compilation in cold; same float64 CPU
path: NeuralOpt v0.8 plan: amortized optimization over problem families

items.title: 15. Parallel track v0.8-B: a learned step policy in its plausible regime
items.text:
Detailed plan: docs/plans/neuralopt-v08b-step-policy.md (approved 2026-11-22; implementation waits for stop point 2 and the user's go-ahead). It fixes the metric definitions, decision rules, cost matching, compute cap and dependencies; where it is more specific than this section, it governs.

Status: recorded here; no implementation until the user approves its own plan. It has its own pre-registration, the same release freeze, and the same families, splits and baselines as F0. It starts only after F0 (stop point 2), so that it uses the verified families and baselines.

Question. v0.4–v0.7 tested learned steps on precision at moderate budgets and lost to fixed or BB steps. v0.8-B asks whether a learned step policy can win where such policies are most plausible: - multimodal and valley-shaped families: Rastrigin, Ackley, shifted Rosenbrock, Family 1 and Family 2b; - small budgets of 20–100 evaluations; - judged on anytime best-so-far progress and reaching the global basin, not on final precision.

Metrics: - anytime regret, the area under the best-so-far regret curve (claim C11); - the probability of reaching the global basin, measured by a measurement-only local polish (claim C12); - objective and gradient calls reported separately; - warm and cold wall time.

Baselines, matched on units and, separately, on warm wall-clock, each tuned on validation only: - owned multistart L-BFGS; - SciPy multistart L-BFGS-B; - CMA-ES; - TPE; - BB.

CMA-ES and TPE are harness-only references, from packages added to the benchmark extra. Gradient-free arms receive their whole unit budget as objective calls. The gradient-to-objective cost ratio is reported, so unit matching does not hide the price of gradients.

Policy (design space for its plan): - a transformer over the trajectory that outputs per-coordinate step sizes, as in POP (Kobiolka et al. 2026). POP runs a per-coordinate trajectory history through a transformer and samples coordinate-wise log step sizes from a Gaussian. - Optionally, Optimus-style low-rank updates (Gärtner et al. 2023). - Stochastic outputs for exploration, as in OPEN (Goldie et al. 2024). - It may read the instance context, as the start predictor does. - Checkpoints use a new versioned schema. The existing history-v1 and Gram schemas are untouched.

Training: - RL (for example PPO) or evolution strategies, on a clipped best-so-far improvement reward max(0, f_best(t−1) − f(x_t)), the form POP uses; - on the target families' training splits only, with the OOD splits held out; - no second-order unrolls. - A compute cap is set in its plan. POP reports about 56 H100-hours of training, which is far beyond this project's CPU budget. That scale gap is a stated risk to C11 and C12.

Claims: C11 (anytime regret) and C12 (global-basin probability) are in the register as unverified.

Prior work (verified; no novelty claim over it): - Gärtner, E., Metz, L., Andriluka, M., Freeman, C. D., Sminchisescu, C. Transformer-Based Learned Optimization (Optimus). CVPR 2023. doi:10.1109/CVPR52729.2023.01152. - Kobiolka, J., Frey, C., Shala, G., Kadra, A., Bedalli, E., Grabocka, J. POP: Prior-Fitted First-Order Optimization Policies. arXiv:2602.15473, 2026. - A preprint marked "Under Review", not peer-reviewed. - A transformer actor-critic trained with PPO; coordinate-wise step sizes; a 43-function benchmark including multimodal functions; 50- to 100-step budgets. - Goldie, A. D., Lu, C., Jackson, M. T., Whiteson, S., Foerster, J. Can Learned Optimization Make Reinforcement Learning Less Difficult? (OPEN). NeurIPS 2024. arXiv:2407.07082. - Moudgil, A., Knyazev, B., Lajoie, G., Belilovsky, E. Celo: Training Versatile Learned Optimizers on a Compute Diet. TMLR 2025. arXiv:2501.12670. - Meta-generalization caveats: - Metz, L., Freeman, C. D., Harrison, J., Maheswaranathan, N., Sohl-Dickstein, J. Practical tradeoffs between memory, compute, and performance in learned optimizers. arXiv:2203.11860, 2022. The arXiv page names no venue, so none is cited. - Rezk, F., Antoniou, A., Gouk, H., Hospedales, T. M. Is Scaling Learned Optimizers Worth It? Evaluating The Value of VeLO's 4000 TPU Months. arXiv:2310.18191, 2023. It has four authors, not two.

All except POP were checked against OpenAlex. POP was checked on arxiv.org, abstract and HTML v2.
path: NeuralOpt v0.8 plan: amortized optimization over problem families

items.title: NeuralOpt v0.8-B: a learned step policy in its plausible regime (plan)
items.text:
Status: approved on 2026-11-22, with the decisions in §14. Implementation still waits for the main track's gate F0 (stop point 2) to be reported and for the user's go-ahead, so v0.8-B builds on the verified families, owned L-BFGS and baselines. No training or heavy compute happens before then.

This plan expands section 15 of neuralopt-v08-amortized-families.md. It keeps the v0.8 release freeze (CLAUDE.md rule 8), the same Families 1 and 2b with their hashed splits, the same accounting conventions (§6 of the main plan), and has its own pre-registration. Claims C11 and C12 are in docs/research/v0.8-claims.md as unverified; their criteria below are proposed and are frozen only at this track's pre-registration.
path: NeuralOpt v0.8-B: a learned step policy in its plausible regime (plan)

items.title: 1. Question and hypotheses
items.text:
v0.4–v0.7 tested learned steps on final precision at moderate budgets; fixed diagonal or BB steps won. v0.8-B asks whether a learned step policy wins where such policies are most plausible: multimodal or valley-shaped problems, at 20–100 evaluations, judged on anytime progress and on reaching the global basin, not on final precision.

  • H11 (C11): on a family, the policy's anytime regret (§5.1) is lower than every baseline's at every pre-registered budget, under unit matching and under wall-clock matching.
  • H12 (C12): on a family, the policy reaches the global basin (§5.2) with a higher probability than every baseline, at every pre-registered budget, under both matchings.

Both are falsifiable per family: either can come out supported, not supported or inconclusive (§6), and every outcome is reported.
path: NeuralOpt v0.8-B: a learned step policy in its plausible regime (plan)

items.title: 2. Families and splits
items.text:
All families are f(x; c) on a box, float64, d = 4 in distribution.

Family Definition Box Instance distribution Global optimum Rastrigin (rotated, shifted) z = R(x − o); f = A·d + Σ (z_j² − A cos 2π z_j) [−5.12, 5.12]^d o ~ U[−2.5, 2.5]^d, R Haar-orthogonal, A ~ U[5, 15] x = o, f* = 0 Ackley (rotated, shifted) z = R(x − o); standard Ackley with a = 20, b = 0.2, c = 2π [−32.768, 32.768]^d o ~ U[−16, 16]^d, R Haar-orthogonal x = o, f* = 0 Shifted Rosenbrock z = x − o + 1; f = Σ 100 (z_{j+1} − z_j²)² + (1 − z_j)² [−5, 5]^d o ~ U[−2.5, 2.5]^d x = o, f* = 0 (a second local minimum exists for 4 ≤ d ≤ 7) Family 1 (damped sinusoid) main plan §8, neuralopt.families "sinusoid" as defined there as defined there reference optimum f* (main plan §6) Family 2b (realistic cascade) main plan §8, "cascade-realistic" as defined there as defined there reference optimum f*
  • Rotations are in distribution on purpose. Unrotated Rastrigin and Ackley are separable, which favours per-coordinate step policies; a rotated test removes that advantage.
  • Splits: train 2,000, validation 200, test 200, and 200 per OOD shift. Instance i of split s is seeded by sha256(family|split|i), as in neuralopt.families; every split has a sha256 manifest. Families 1 and 2b reuse their existing splits and hashes.
  • OOD shifts (reported, not part of the C11/C12 criteria):
  • synthetic families: d = 8; shifts outside the training range (still inside the box); Rastrigin A ∈ [15, 25];
  • Families 1 and 2b: their existing OOD splits.
  • First evaluation point. Every arm's first evaluation on instance i is the same point x0_i: drawn uniformly in the box (instance-seeded) for the synthetic families, and the family default for Families 1 and 2b (as F0's A0). Multistart arms take their further starts from a fixed Sobol sequence.
path: NeuralOpt v0.8-B: a learned step policy in its plausible regime (plan)

items.title: 3. Arms
path: NeuralOpt v0.8-B: a learned step policy in its plausible regime (plan)

items.title: 3.1 The policy (the learned arm)
items.text:
• Inputs, all in box-normalized coordinates u = 2(x − lo)/(hi − lo) − 1, with gradients mapped as g_u = Jᵀ g_x, J = diag((hi − lo)/2):
  • per coordinate and per step, over a window of the last H = 16 evaluated states: u_j, g_u,j divided by the window's RMS gradient, and the secant differences Δu_j, Δg_j, masked when invalid or rejected (never filled with zeros);
  • per step: the normalized objective relative to the best so far, the step index and the remaining budget fraction;
  • Families 1 and 2b only: an instance-context embedding from the start predictor's masked set encoder. The synthetic families get no context, because their only context (shift and rotation) would reveal the optimum.
  • Architecture: POP-style (Kobiolka et al. 2026). A small transformer attends over time per coordinate (weights shared across coordinates), followed by one cross-coordinate mixing layer so that rotated problems can be represented. Target size 20k–50k parameters.
  • Outputs: per-coordinate mean and log standard deviation of a log step size, η_t ~ N(μ_t, σ_t²), sampled for exploration (as in OPEN; Goldie et al. 2024). The update is u_{t+1} = Π_box(u_t − exp(η_t) ⊙ g̃_t).
  • Optional ablation: an Optimus-style low-rank term (rank 2) added to the update (Gärtner et al. 2023). It is off in the primary arm.
  • Evaluation randomness: the sampling RNG is seeded per instance, so evaluation is reproducible.
  • Cost: one objective and one gradient call at each new point (2 units).
  • Checkpoints use a new versioned schema (step-policy-v1); the history-v1 and Gram schemas and all v0.1–v0.7 checkpoints are untouched.
  • Every step at inference comes from NeuralOpt's own code (CLAUDE.md).
path: NeuralOpt v0.8-B: a learned step policy in its plausible regime (plan)

items.title: 3.2 Baselines
items.text:
Each is tuned on validation only, per family and per budget, over the grid below; the chosen configuration is frozen in the pre-registration.

Baseline Implementation Tuning grid (validation) Owned multistart L-BFGS neuralopt.lbfgs (pure JAX) K ∈ {1, 2, 4, 8} starts, B/K units each SciPy multistart L-BFGS-B SciPy, harness only K ∈ CMA-ES cma (pycma), harness only; mean at x0_i, in u coordinates, box bounds σ0 ∈ {0.1, 0.2, 0.3} of the u box width; popsize ∈ TPE optuna.samplers.TPESampler, in-memory storage, harness only; first trial enqueued at x0_i n_startup_trials ∈ {5, 10}; multivariate ∈ {False, True} BB NeuralOpt's compiled-loop BB step, projected onto the box initial step ∈ {1e-3, 1e-2, 1e-1}; step clip ∈ {1, 10} Quasi-random search scrambled Sobol points in the box, the first at x0_i; harness only none

Quasi-random search is in the "every baseline" set (decision 1). At 20–100 evaluations it is the natural floor; a policy that beat the other baselines but lost to sampling would not support C11 or C12.

Stochastic baselines (CMA-ES, TPE, quasi-random search with its scramble seed) are run with 5 seeds; each instance's outcome is the mean over seeds, as for the policy.
path: NeuralOpt v0.8-B: a learned step policy in its plausible regime (plan)

items.title: 4. Cost accounting and matching
items.text:
• Units. One objective call = 1 unit; one gradient call = 1 unit; HVPs are not used. Objective and gradient calls are reported separately for every arm.
  • Owned L-BFGS: an objective per line-search trial and a gradient on acceptance (§3 of the main plan).
  • SciPy, BB and the policy: a joint value-and-gradient call costs 2 units. Its value becomes available at the second unit.
  • CMA-ES, TPE and random search use no gradients. At budget B they make B objective calls, and their gradient count is zero.
  • Unit matching undercharges gradients. F0's probe measured the gradient at 2.5× an objective call for Family 1 and about 12× for Family 2. Unit matching therefore favours gradient-based arms. This is why every claim must also hold under wall-clock matching. A cost-weighted count n_f + r·n_g, with the measured ratio r, is reported as an exploratory column.
  • Wall-clock matching (warm).
  • Each arm's median warm cumulative-time curve C_a(t) (seconds after t units) is measured per family on 50 validation instances. Measurement is one instance at a time (the deployment case), after compilation, on the same CPU, float64, with XLA single-threaded. The policy's forward passes are included. The curves are frozen in the pre-registration.
  • The wall budget for budget B is T(B) = C_policy(B). Baseline k gets B_k = max{t : C_k(t) ≤ T(B)} units and is tuned on validation at B_k.
  • Wall-matched anytime regret integrates L (§5.1) over time [0, T(B)], mapping each arm's units to time through its frozen C_a. This keeps the comparison deterministic.
  • Actual test timings are recorded too. A deviation from the frozen curves above 25% is reported.
  • Cold time (including compilation) and batched throughput are reported separately and are not part of the criteria.
  • Not charged to any arm: the global-basin polish (§5.2) and the regret normalization scale s_i (§5.1). Both are measurement only and never feed back into an arm.
  • Charged as offline cost and reported: training (all generations, including compilation) and the training-split references.
path: NeuralOpt v0.8-B: a learned step policy in its plausible regime (plan)

items.title: 5. Metric definitions
path: NeuralOpt v0.8-B: a learned step policy in its plausible regime (plan)

items.title: 5.1 Anytime regret: the area under the regret curve
items.text:
For instance i:

  • f_best(t) is the lowest objective value among the arm's objective evaluations completed within the first t units. It is undefined before the first value.
  • Floor: τ_i = ε_abs + ε_rel·|f*_i|, the success tolerance, with ε as in F0 (ε_abs = 1e-6, ε_rel = 1e-3). Precision below the success tolerance earns nothing, so the metric does not reward final precision.
  • Normalization: s_i is the median of f(x) − f*_i over 64 fixed Sobol points in the box (harness only, uncharged). It is the regret of a typical uninformed point. Instances with s_i ≤ τ_i are excluded and counted.
  • Clipped log regret: L_i(t) = log10( min(max(f_best(t) − f*_i, τ_i), 10·s_i) / s_i ), and L_i(t) = 1 before the first value.
  • Its range is [log10(τ_i/s_i), 1].
  • If any arm finds a value below f*_i − τ_i, then f*_i is updated for all arms and the update is reported, as in F0.
  • Anytime regret at budget B: AUC_i(B) = (1/B) Σ_{t=1..B} L_i(t). Lower is better. The wall-matched version is (1/T) ∫_0^T L_i(τ) dτ, as in §4.
  • Budget grid: B ∈ {20, 50, 100} units.
  • Baselines are run separately at each B, with their B-tuned configuration.
  • The policy takes the remaining budget as an input and is also run separately at each B.
  • Full curves for t = 1..100 are reported for every arm.
path: NeuralOpt v0.8-B: a learned step policy in its plausible regime (plan)

items.title: 5.2 Global basin
items.text:
• Definition (operational): an arm reached the global basin at budget B if a measurement-only polish started from its best point x_best(B) converges to within the success tolerance of the global optimum: f(polish(x_best)) − f*_i ≤ τ_i.
  • The polish is NeuralOpt's owned L-BFGS, capped at 2,000 units with gtol 1e-8 (the reference cap), with no restarts. It is uncharged and never fed back.
  • The global basin is thus the basin of attraction of a fixed local polish, not a geometric object.
  • Per family:
  • Rastrigin, Ackley, shifted Rosenbrock: f* = 0 at x = o (known).
  • Families 1 and 2b: f* is the reference optimum from the main plan's §6 protocol (SciPy multistart, 64 Sobol starts plus the truth, two seeds, ≥ 99% two-seed reproduction on validation), updated if any arm beats it.
  • Sanity rows (reported): the rate from polishing x0_i directly (zero search), and the rate from polishing the best of B Sobol points.
path: NeuralOpt v0.8-B: a learned step policy in its plausible regime (plan)

items.title: 6. How C11 and C12 are decided
items.text:
• Unit of analysis: test instances, paired across arms. The policy's outcome for an instance is the mean over ≥ 5 training seeds. Stochastic baselines are averaged over 5 run seeds.
  • Differences:
  • C11: d_i = AUC_i(policy) − AUC_i(baseline); negative is better for the policy.
  • C12: d_i = p_i(policy) − p_i(baseline), where p_i is the share of seeds reaching the global basin; positive is better for the policy.
  • Intervals: a two-level percentile bootstrap resamples training seeds, then instances (paired). It uses 10,000 resamples and a fixed RNG seed.
  • Each comparison uses a two-sided 95% interval.
  • "Beats all baselines" is an intersection-union test (Berger 1982), decided per family. The claim holds for a family only if every comparison is individually significant: 6 baselines × 3 budgets × 2 matchings = 36 comparisons.
  • Because the claim is a conjunction, its error rate is at most the level of each comparison: a one-sided 2.5% chance of a false "supported" for the family.
  • No multiplicity correction is applied within a family, and none to the per-family statuses in the register.
  • Joint claims across families need a multiplicity correction. Any statement made jointly about several families must apply Holm–Bonferroni over the families it covers, at a family-wise one-sided level of 2.5%. Examples: "C11 holds on the multimodal families", "on k of 5 families", or a pooled summary.
  • Each family's IUT p-value is the largest one-sided bootstrap p-value among its 36 comparisons.
  • A family counts toward the joint statement only if it passes at its Holm-adjusted level.
  • Without that correction, the per-family statuses are reported side by side and no joint claim is made.
  • C11 status per family:
  • Supported: for every baseline, budget and matching, the 95% interval of d lies entirely below 0.
  • Not supported: for some baseline, budget and matching, the interval lies entirely above 0 (that baseline is better).
  • Inconclusive: otherwise.
  • C12 status per family: the same rules with the sign reversed. Supported requires every lower bound > 0; not supported requires some upper bound < 0. Degenerate cases (all rates 0 or all 1) are inconclusive.
  • Each family's status is recorded separately. OOD results are reported (C8 conventions) and do not change the status.
  • Power (meaningful effects approved: 0.25 decades of AUC; 10 percentage points of basin rate):
  • Rule: each comparison is powered at 80% for the threshold effect at the 95% two-sided level. Required paired instances n = ((z_0.975 + z_0.8)·SD_d / δ)², with z_0.975 + z_0.8 = 2.80.
  • Under the IUT, the claim's power is at most the weakest comparison's, so n is set by the comparison with the largest SD_d. That is usually the closest baseline.

  • A priori (normal approximation, assumed SDs; no data yet). At n = 200 the minimal detectable effect is 0.198·SD_d. The 99% rule of the first draft needed 0.242·SD_d.

    Effect δ SD_d n needed (95%) n needed (99%, superseded) MDE at n = 200 (95%) 0.25 decades 0.5 32 47 0.099 0.25 decades 1.0 126 187 0.198 0.25 decades 1.5 283 421 0.297 0.25 decades 2.0 503 748 0.396 10 points 0.2 32 47 0.040 10 points 0.3 71 106 0.059 10 points 0.5 197 292 0.099 10 points 0.7 385 573 0.139

    So 200 test instances suffice when SD_d ≤ 1.26 decades (C11) or SD_d ≤ 0.50 (C12). - The binding check uses data: at B-S2/B-S3, SD_d is estimated per family, comparison and budget from validation (baselines plus a pilot policy where available). The pre-registration sets each family's test size to the largest required n. Test sizes are raised, never the criteria loosened. If a family needs more than 1,000 instances, that is reported before freezing. - Also reported, not criteria: per-seed results, including the worst seed; failure and nonfinite counts; the table of all 36 per-family intervals.
path: NeuralOpt v0.8-B: a learned step policy in its plausible regime (plan)

items.title: 7. Training
items.text:
• Method: antithetic evolution strategies (Salimans et al. 2017) with centred-rank fitness shaping and Adam (optax, already in the train extra) on the ES gradient estimate.
  • ES needs no backpropagation through unrolls, so there are no second-order unrolls. It also accepts the non-differentiable, clipped metric directly.
  • PPO is a pre-declared fallback (decision 2), triggered only by the validation rule below.
  • Reward: clipped best-so-far regret at every unit.
  • Per unit, r_t = −L_i(t) (§5.1), so an episode's mean reward is −AUC_i(B), the evaluation metric itself.
  • POP's per-step form max(0, f_best(t−1) − f(x_t)) telescopes to the total improvement and ignores when progress happens. The per-unit clipped regret keeps the anytime character and is clipped at the same floor and cap.
  • Data: each target family's training split only.
  • Synthetic f* = 0 is known.
  • Families 1 and 2b use the training-target references of the main plan (§10: 16 starts × 1,000 units, owned).
  • Validation is used only for selection (best checkpoint every 25 generations) and early stopping. Test and OOD splits stay closed until the single final evaluation.
  • Settings:
  • population P = 64 (32 antithetic pairs), ES noise 0.02;
  • M = 16 training instances per generation, common to the population;
  • budget sampled per episode from {20, 50, 100};
  • G ≤ 500 generations;
  • one policy per family; 5 seeds.
path: NeuralOpt v0.8-B: a learned step policy in its plausible regime (plan)

items.title: 7.1 Pre-registered PPO fallback (validation only)
items.text:
• Validation checkpoints: every 25 generations, each ES seed's current policy is evaluated on the family's validation split. The tracked score is the mean AUC(B) over B ∈ {20, 50, 100} under unit matching.
  • Plateau: a seed has plateaued when either
  • at least 200 generations have run, and its best validation score improved by less than 0.02 decades over the last 4 checkpoints (100 generations); or
  • it reaches G = 500.

A family's ES training has plateaued when at least 3 of its 5 seeds have. - "Beats quasi-random search and BB on validation": the seed-mean policy (best validation checkpoint per seed) has a lower mean validation AUC(B) than both quasi-random search and BB at every B ∈ {20, 50, 100}, under unit and wall-clock matching. These are point estimates on validation; no intervals are used for this switch. - Trigger: PPO runs for a family if its ES training has plateaued and the ES policy does not beat quasi-random search and BB on validation. The trigger is evaluated once, when the family's ES runs stop. - PPO arm (pre-declared now): - the same policy network as actor, plus a value head; - clipped surrogate 0.2, GAE λ = 0.95, γ = 1 (finite horizon); - the same per-unit reward −L_i(t), the same training split and validation selection; - 5 seeds; - no new dependencies (JAX and optax). - It differentiates through the policy network per step, never through the optimization trajectory, so there are no second-order unrolls. - Which arm goes to test: exactly one policy arm per family. It is ES if PPO was not triggered, PPO if it was, fixed before any test data is opened. The other arm's validation results are reported. Test data never informs this choice. - Compute: PPO counts against the same 24 CPU-hour cap. If the projection exceeds the cap, PPO's update count is cut first; seeds are never cut.
path: NeuralOpt v0.8-B: a learned step policy in its plausible regime (plan)

items.title: 8. Compute estimate and cap
items.text:
The per-unit costs below come from F0's probe (results/f0-probe-v0.8.0.json). The policy forward cost is an estimate that the B0 probe must measure.

  • Per generation: 1,024 episodes × up to 50 policy steps = 51,200 steps.
  • Synthetic families and Family 1:
  • about 26 µs per step (about 20 µs policy forward plus 2 cheap evaluations);
  • ≈ 1.3 s per generation, ≈ 11 min per run, plus validation checks;
  • 4 families × 5 seeds ≈ 4 CPU-hours.
  • Family 2b:
  • about 220 µs per step (≈ 100 µs per unit for batched owned evaluation, × 2, plus the forward pass);
  • ≈ 11 s per generation, ≈ 1.6 h per run;
  • 5 seeds ≈ 8 CPU-hours.
  • Baseline tuning, references for the new synthetic splits, wall-clock calibration and the single test evaluation: ≈ 4 CPU-hours. Synthetic references are free (f* known). Family 2b references dominate.
  • Total ≈ 16 CPU-hours. Proposed cap: 24 CPU-hours.
  • If the B0 probe projects more than the cap, the pre-registered reduction order is: G 500 → 300, then M 16 → 8, then dropping the d = 8 OOD split.
  • Seeds (≥ 5) and test sizes are never reduced.
  • For scale, POP reports about 56 H100-hours of training. A CPU budget three orders of magnitude smaller is a stated risk to C11 and C12; a negative result under this budget is reported as such and not generalized to learned policies at scale.
path: NeuralOpt v0.8-B: a learned step policy in its plausible regime (plan)

items.title: 9. Long runs
items.text: Every run expected to exceed 10 minutes follows CLAUDE.md rule 9: - a named tmux session (for example neuralopt-v08b-train); - a git-ignored runs/v08b-<stage>-<UTC stamp>/ directory holding: - command.txt: command, git SHA, uv.lock hash, UTC start; - log.txt; - an atomic progress.json: units (family × seed) done/total, generation, ETA; - checkpoints: one per finished unit via scripts/run_checkpoint.py, plus ES state every 25 generations, so a resume loses at most 25 generations; - exit_code, and DONE only on success. - HANDOFF.md is updated before and after each run. - Versioned results go to results/v0.8-b-*.json. Frozen files are never overwritten.
path: NeuralOpt v0.8-B: a learned step policy in its plausible regime (plan)

items.title: 12. Risks
items.text: Risk Mitigation Training scale far below POP stated; negative results are scoped to this budget Separability exploited rotated Rastrigin and Ackley in distribution Gradient price hidden by unit matching wall-clock matching is a required condition Python overhead (TPE, CMA-ES) dominates wall matching reported per arm; unit matching is also required, so neither matching alone decides Overfitting to a family OOD splits reported; per-family claims only; no pooling ES variance across seeds ≥ 5 seeds; seeds resampled in the bootstrap; worst seed reported Many comparisons intersection-union within a family (95% per comparison); Holm–Bonferroni for any joint claim across families ES fails to train pre-declared PPO fallback on a validation-only trigger (§7.1) f* not global (Families 1, 2b) two-seed reproduction; updated when beaten Context leaks the optimum synthetic families get no context The polish defines the basin operational definition stated; zero-search sanity rows

items.title: 13. Prior work (verified; no novelty claim over it)
items.text:
All of the following resolved exactly on OpenAlex on 2026-11-22. POP was also checked on arxiv.org earlier.

  • Gärtner, E., Metz, L., Andriluka, M., Freeman, C. D., Sminchisescu, C. Transformer-Based Learned Optimization (Optimus). CVPR 2023. doi:10.1109/CVPR52729.2023.01152.
  • Kobiolka, J., Frey, C., Shala, G., Kadra, A., Bedalli, E., Grabocka, J. POP: Prior-Fitted First-Order Optimization Policies. arXiv:2602.15473, 2026. A preprint ("Under Review"), not peer-reviewed.
  • Goldie, A. D., Lu, C., Jackson, M. T., Whiteson, S., Foerster, J. Can Learned Optimization Make Reinforcement Learning Less Difficult? (OPEN). NeurIPS 2024. doi:10.52202/079017-0177; arXiv:2407.07082.

  • Metz, L., Freeman, C. D., Harrison, J., Maheswaranathan, N., Sohl-Dickstein, J. Practical tradeoffs between memory, compute, and performance in learned optimizers. arXiv:2203.11860, 2022 (arXiv only).
  • Rezk, F., Antoniou, A., Gouk, H., Hospedales, T. M. Is Scaling Learned Optimizers Worth It? Evaluating The Value of VeLO's 4000 TPU Months. arXiv:2310.18191, 2023.

  • Salimans, T., Ho, J., Chen, X., Sidor, S., Sutskever, I. Evolution Strategies as a Scalable Alternative to Reinforcement Learning. arXiv:1703.03864, 2017.

items.title: 14. Decisions (approved 2026-11-22)
items.text:
1. Quasi-random search is in the "every baseline" set (§3.2).
  2. ES first, PPO deferred, with a pre-registered PPO fallback triggered on validation only (§7.1).
  3. A 24 CPU-hour cap with the stated reduction order (§8).
  4. optuna for TPE, in the benchmark extra only (§10).
  5. Power thresholds: 0.25 decades of AUC; 10 percentage points of basin rate (§6).
  6. Change: C11 and C12 are decided per family as intersection-union tests with two-sided 95% intervals per comparison. A multiplicity correction (Holm–Bonferroni over families) applies only to claims made jointly across families. The power check was redone under this rule (§6).

items.title: Disagreements and notes
items.text:
1. Dates depend on the time zone.
  2. The dates you supplied are the merge commits' local dates (+05:30).
  3. GitHub shows merge times in UTC, and on that basis four versions merged one day earlier:
    • v0.1.0: 11-14, not 11-15;
    • v0.4.0: 11-15, not 11-16;
    • v0.5.0: 11-20, not 11-21;
    • v0.6.0: 11-21, not 11-22.
  4. D1, decided: UTC dates everywhere (GitHub's merge dates). These go in the CHANGELOG, the release notes and the tag messages. Each tag message also gives the +05:30 local merge time.
  5. The dates are therefore:
    • v0.1.0: 2026-11-14;
    • v0.2.0: 2026-11-15;
    • v0.3.0: 2026-11-15;
    • v0.4.0: 2026-11-15;
    • v0.5.0: 2026-11-20;
    • v0.6.0: 2026-11-21.
  6. The version number at the v0.6.0 commit is wrong. At bef56bc, pyproject.toml, __init__.__version__ and CITATION.cff all say 0.5.0.
  7. The tag is still correct: the CHANGELOG and the PR both describe v0.6.
  8. However, a wheel built from it would be named neuralopt-0.5.0. See D2 in item 6.
  9. Every old tag carries a zensical.toml. That makes the docs backfill (item 7) feasible for all six old versions.
  10. Other notes.
  11. .bumpversion.toml is stale at 0.4.0, and __init__.py hard-codes __version__. Both are handled in item 5.
  12. v0.1.0, v0.2.0 and v0.3.0 were merged from the same branch (feature/research-grade-neuralopt). That is consistent with the mapping.
