items.title: 2. Release notes (docs/release-notes/)
items.text:
• vX.Y.Z.md for 0.1.0 through 0.7.0, plus an index.md table with one row per version: version, date, one-line summary, and result type (infrastructure / positive / negative).
  • Sources: CHANGELOG entries, the version's research reports (mapped below) and the PR commit lists. Reports are linked, not rewritten.
  • Sections: Highlights, Features, Research results, Fixes, Documentation, Build and CI, Breaking changes, and Known limitations. Empty sections are written as "None."
  • Research results state the outcome in the first sentence. For example: "Negative: learned geometry did not beat the validation-tuned fixed diagonal."
Version Research reports first added in that version 0.1 theory, experiment-plan, literature, novelty, limitations, benchmarks/smoke 0.2 training, benchmarks, certification, generalization, trajectory-diagnostics, hamiltonian-{theory,correctness,related-work} 0.3 langevin-theory, fokker-planck, gibbs-measures, function-spaces, stochastic-{novelty,limitations} 0.4 distribution-aware-training (negative: learned BAOAB geometry does not beat fixed diagonal) 0.5 transferable-geometry (negative: learned geometry does not beat tuned fixed geometry) 0.6 trajectory-curvature-v0.6, -experiments, -literature (negative main result: BB beats every learned arm) 0.7 engine-speed-v0.7 (speed only), gram-space-v0.7 (pre-registered negative: H1 fails)

Breaking changes in 0.7.0: - preconditioned_engine now defaults to "compiled". Callers that use candidate_method="preconditioned" with a host/NumPy gradient= now get a ValueError that names preconditioned_engine="python". Before, they ran on the Python loop silently. - __version__ now comes from the package metadata.

items.title: 3. CHANGELOG.md
items.text:
• One section per version, in the form ## [0.N.0] - YYYY-MM-DD, with UTC merge dates (D1).
  • An ## [Unreleased] section at the top.
  • Each section is a short version of the curated release notes, with bullets kept consistent with them. It ends with a link to docs/release-notes/v0.N.0.md.
  • Comparison links go at the bottom, for example [0.2.0]: https://github.com/bibymaths/neuralopt/compare/v0.1.0...v0.2.0.

items.title: 4. git-cliff and conventional commits
items.text:
• cliff.toml will be replaced with a copy of the globax configuration:
  • conventional_commits = true and filter_unconventional = false;
  • the same emoji groups and commit preprocessors;
  • tag_pattern = "v[0-9].*";
  • links rewritten to bibymaths/neuralopt.
  • git-cliff only drafts. A new scripts/draft_release_notes.sh vX.Y.Z runs git cliff --unreleased --tag vX.Y.Z and writes to stdout or a scratch file. It never writes CHANGELOG.md or a docs/release-notes/ file. Unlike globax, there is no changelog workflow that rewrites CHANGELOG.md.
  • Release procedure (in CONTRIBUTING.md):
  • Draft the notes with git-cliff.
  • Curate them into docs/release-notes/vX.Y.Z.md.
  • Prepend a CHANGELOG section.
  • Bump the version.
  • Open a PR, then merge it.
  • Tag the merge commit.
  • CONTRIBUTING.md gains:
  • the commit types (feat fix docs perf refactor test build ci chore revert, plus research → grouped under "Research", a NeuralOpt addition);
  • the scope convention;
  • a ! / BREAKING CHANGE: footer for breaking changes;
  • the release procedure.
  • PR-title check: .github/workflows/pr-title.yml, using amannn/action-semantic-pull-request pinned to a release tag, with pull-requests: read only. It runs on pull_request (not pull_request_target), so fork code never gets elevated permissions.
  • History is not rewritten. Old commits stay unconventional; git-cliff groups them under "Other".
  • D3, decided: squash-merge with the PR title as the commit message. You set it in Settings. With that setting, the PR-title check guarantees conventional commits on main. CONTRIBUTING.md documents this.

items.title: 5. Version metadata: a single source
items.text:
• pyproject.toml is the source of truth (version = "0.7.0").
  • neuralopt.__version__ = importlib.metadata.version("neuralopt").
  • .bumpversion.toml is deleted: it is stale, and nothing uses it.
  • CITATION.cff (version and date-released) is set in the release PR, as step 4 of the release procedure (item 4).
  • .zenodo.json omits version, so Zenodo takes it from the release tag. That leaves one less field to keep in sync.
  • scripts/check_release.py vX.Y.Z verifies that:
  • the tag, pyproject.toml's version and CITATION.cff's version are all equal;
  • if .zenodo.json ever gains a version, it must equal the tag too;
  • CITATION.cff's date-released equals the date of this version's CHANGELOG heading;
  • CITATION.cff passes cffconvert --validate, run in CI as uvx cffconvert==2.0.0 --validate. It stays out of the project's dependencies, because it pins old jsonschema versions;
  • .zenodo.json is valid JSON with the required keys: title, upload_type, description, creators, license, access_right and related_identifiers;
  • docs/release-notes/vX.Y.Z.md exists;
  • CHANGELOG.md has a ## [X.Y.Z] - heading.
  • The metadata checks also run in ci.yml, on every PR: cffconvert --validate, plus check_release.py --metadata-only for the JSON and the version agreement.
  • With --backfill, it skips the three-way version check (D2) and checks only that the notes and the CHANGELOG entry exist on main.
  • Tests:
  • __version__ matches pyproject.toml;
  • the release checker passes on 0.7.0;
  • the release checker fails when a version mismatches, a notes file is missing, the date-released disagrees with the CHANGELOG, or .zenodo.json is invalid.

items.title: 6. .github/workflows/release.yml
items.text:
Triggers: - push: tags: ['v*']; - workflow_dispatch with inputs tag (string) and publish_pypi (boolean, default false), used for backfill.

Workflow-level settings: - permissions: contents: read; - concurrency: release-${{ tag }} with cancel-in-progress: false.

Jobs:

  1. verify checks out ref: <tag> and runs check_release.py. For tags below v0.7.0, it runs --backfill against main's files.
  2. Outputs: version, is_backfill, and pypi_ok. pypi_ok is true when Version(tag) >= 0.7.0 and either the run was a tag push or publish_pypi is true. The comparison uses packaging.version.
  3. test runs the full quality gate at the tag: uv sync --extra dev --extra docs, ruff check ., pyright, pytest -q, zensical build --strict, uv build, and twine check dist/*.
  4. It is skipped for backfill, because those commits passed CI in their own PRs and old tags lack the current tooling. The release notes say so.
  5. build runs uv build at the tag and uploads dist/ with actions/upload-artifact and retention-days: 3.
  6. D2, decided: v0.6.0 gets no build files. Its sdist and wheel would be named 0.5.0, so build is skipped for v0.6.0. Its release notes explain why. All other versions get both an sdist and a wheel.
  7. pypi has needs: [verify, test, build] and if: pypi_ok.
  8. environment: pypi, and permissions: id-token: write in this job only.
  9. It uses pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish pinned to a release tag. That is trusted publishing, with no tokens.
  10. github-release has permissions: contents: write.
  11. It uses gh release create vX.Y.Z --title "NeuralOpt vX.Y.Z" --notes-file docs/release-notes/vX.Y.Z.md --prerelease --verify-tag, then attaches the dist files.
  12. The notes file is read from main for backfill. All 0.x releases are marked as pre-releases.
  13. For backfill it waits for nothing on PyPI. For v0.7.0 it runs after pypi succeeds.
  14. docs calls the reusable deploy steps from item 7 for the tag's minor version.
  15. It runs in concurrency: gh-pages (shared with docs.yml, cancel-in-progress: false), so deploys never overlap.

Common to all jobs: - Actions are pinned to full release tags: actions/checkout@v4.x.y, astral-sh/setup-uv@v6.x.y, and so on, with exact values resolved in Phase 2. - Option: pin to commit SHAs instead. That is safer but noisier, so say if you want it. - No other workflow uploads artifacts. Release files live only on the GitHub release.
path: Release engineering plan: tags, releases, PyPI, versioned docs

items.title: 7. Versioned docs (Zensical plus its mike fork)
items.text:
Tooling: - Zensical's versioning is a temporary fork of mike 2.2.0 (squidfunk/mike). It is not on PyPI. - It is installed from git, pinned to a commit hash: mike @ git+https://github.com/squidfunk/mike@2d4ad799442f4592db8ad53b179bfb33db8c69ac. - That is the head of master on 2026-04-17. The fork of jimporter/mike was last pushed on 2026-10-11. - It is used in the docs extra and in the workflows. - The zensical.toml setting is [project.extra.version] provider = "mike", with alias = true and default = "latest". - What I read in the fork at that commit: - Zensical version: it requires zensical >= 0.0.30. The installed 0.1.1 satisfies that, so Zensical is not upgraded. If Phase 2 nonetheless shows an incompatibility, Zensical is upgraded and zensical build --strict is run again. - How it builds: mike deploy runs zensical build --clean, without --strict. Strictness is therefore a separate zensical build --strict step, run before every deploy. - Config file: mike reads zensical.toml, or the file given with -F/--config-file. It resolves site_dir relative to that file's directory. - Commands: mike 2.2.0's (deploy --push --update-aliases, set-default, list, -b gh-pages). - The Zensical versioning page (zensical.org/docs/setup/versioning/) currently redirects to a 404. The fork's README points to the upstream mike documentation.

Layout on gh-pages: - one folder per minor version, 0.1/ … 0.7/, each titled with its full version (for example "0.7.0"); - aliases latest (the newest release) and dev (main); - mike set-default latest; - site_url = https://bibymaths.github.io/neuralopt/.

.github/workflows/docs.yml: - On PRs it runs zensical build --strict only, with no deploy. - On pushes to main it runs mike deploy --push --update-aliases dev. - It runs in concurrency group gh-pages, with permissions: contents: write only in the deploy job.

Backfill (scripts/backfill_docs.py): for each old tag it: 1. runs git worktree add <tmp> vX.Y.0; 2. writes an untracked overlay config at the worktree root: the tag's zensical.toml plus site_url and the version provider. It is named .zensical-versioned.toml and passed with -F. It has to sit at the root, because docs_dir and site_dir resolve relative to the config file. It is never committed, and the worktree is deleted afterwards. 3. runs mike deploy --config-file <overlay> 0.N with --title 0.N.0; 4. runs zensical build --strict -f <overlay> first. If that fails, it records the failure and deploys anyway, since mike's own build is non-strict; 5. removes the worktree.

The script: - writes a report to artifacts/docs-backfill-report.json (gitignored scratch, not a workflow artifact) listing strict, non-strict and failed builds; - defaults to --no-push (a local gh-pages commit only). Pushing needs --push and happens only in Phase 3, after you approve.

Phase 2 local check: build two versions (0.6 and 0.7) into a local gh-pages with mike deploy (no push), then mike serve and check the version selector. The result is reported.

items.title: 8. Docs site structure (current version)
items.text:
The zensical.toml nav will be (new pages marked ★, existing pages reused):

  • Home (index.md, rewritten to a landing page ★)
  • Getting started: Installation ★, Quickstart ★, When to use NeuralOpt ★
  • User guide: Learned mode ★, Certified mode ★ (built from research/certification.md usage parts plus the README), Compiled engine ★ (the usage parts of research/engine-speed-v0.7.md; the report itself is linked, not moved)
  • Research reports by version: 0.1 … 0.7 groups pointing at the existing docs/research/*.md files, with no rewrites
  • Release notes: release-notes/index.md and each version
  • Changelog: changelog.md ★, which includes the root CHANGELOG.md via the pymdownx.snippets include
  • Limitations: research/limitations.md plus research/stochastic-limitations.md
  • API reference ★: mkdocstrings for neuralopt.__all__ (as in globax; mkdocstrings-python is added to the docs group)
  • Citing NeuralOpt ★ (citing.md):
  • the CITATION.cff details: title, version, author with ORCID, license, repository;
  • "cite the exact version or commit";
  • a BibTeX @software entry generated by cffconvert -f bibtex;
  • (later) the concept DOI.
  • A test checks that the page's version, title and ORCID match CITATION.cff.
  • docs/superpowers/ and docs/plans/ stay out of the nav. They are internal working documents, built but not listed.

"When to use NeuralOpt" says it plainly: - For solving problems, use SciPy L-BFGS-B or Optimistix LBFGS. On the v0.7 equal-work benchmark they reach 1e-6 on 32/32 tasks, where learned NeuralOpt geometry reaches it on 0/32. - NeuralOpt is for research on learned optimizers, and for its restricted certified mode on the supported expression subset.

items.title: 9. README
items.text: The README will contain, in order: - the logo; - a one-line description; - badges: CI, Docs, PyPI version, Python versions, License MIT, Ruff, uv (downloads only after the first PyPI release); - "Status: alpha research package; learned components do not outperform classical optimizers in our benchmarks (see release notes)."; - install (pip install neuralopt once on PyPI; uv sync for development); - the quickstart (the learned and certified examples, both checked by a doctest-style test); - when to use NeuralOpt; - links to docs, release notes and the changelog; - citation: a short BibTeX block and a link to the Citing NeuralOpt docs page and CITATION.cff (a DOI badge after the first Zenodo archive); - license.
path: Release engineering plan: tags, releases, PyPI, versioned docs

items.title: 10. Logo
items.text:
• Original SVG, written by hand, in the globax palette:
  • deep navy #0B1B3F for the wordmark;
  • gradient cyan #22D3EE → blue #2563EB → purple #8B5CF6.
  • Icon: a contour basin, three or four nested elliptical level sets, with a short chain of connected nodes (a descent path) running from the rim into the minimum. The final node is highlighted. There is no globe and no cubes.
  • Wordmark: lowercase geometric "neuralopt" in navy, with "opt" in the gradient, mirroring globax's accented "x". Letterforms are drawn as paths, so no font is needed at render time.
  • Files in docs/assets/images/:
  • logo.svg (source) and logo.png (1448×1086, matching the globax canvas);
  • logo-dark.svg and logo-dark.png, with a light wordmark for dark backgrounds;
  • favicon/: favicon.ico, 16/32 PNGs, apple-touch-icon.png, android 192/512 and site.webmanifest, made from the icon alone.
  • PNGs are rendered with rsvg-convert or cairosvg, whichever is available, and the command used is recorded.
  • Usage:
  • the README uses <picture> with light and dark sources;
  • zensical.toml sets favicon and theme.logo;
  • the palette is navy/indigo plus deep-purple accent, as in globax.
  • You review the rendered PNGs before the PR.

items.title: 11. Manual steps for you (I cannot do these)
items.text:
1. ✅ Check that neuralopt is free on PyPI (it is now reserved by your pending publisher).
  2. ✅ The PyPI pending trusted publisher is created. Check it matches exactly:
Field Value PyPI project name neuralopt Owner bibymaths Repository name neuralopt Workflow name release.yml (the file name only, no path) Environment name pypi
  • The plan uses exactly .github/workflows/release.yml, and a pypi job with environment: pypi.
  • The publish step runs directly in that file, not in a reusable workflow that it calls. Otherwise PyPI's OIDC claim would name the other file.
  • A pending publisher does not reserve the name. If someone else registers neuralopt before v0.7.0 is published, it lapses.
  • Create the GitHub environment pypi (Settings → Environments), with yourself as required reviewer. Optionally restrict deployment to tags v*.
  • Set Pages to "Deploy from a branch", branch gh-pages, folder /, after the branch exists. The branch is created by the first mike push in Phase 3.
  • ✅ D4: the repository is public (gh repo view confirms it).
  • D3: in Settings → General, allow squash merging and set the default commit message to "Pull request title". You said you will do this.
  • Zenodo, after the backfill only. Enable the Zenodo GitHub integration for bibymaths/neuralopt only after the v0.1.0–v0.6.0 GitHub releases exist and before v0.7.0 is tagged.
  • Zenodo archives on "release published" events, so v0.7.0 becomes the first archived version.
  • Phase 3 has a hard stop between the backfill and the v0.7.0 tag for this step.
  • After the first archive, send me the concept DOI. A follow-up PR (docs: or chore:) adds it to:
  • CITATION.cff (doi: and identifiers);
  • .zenodo.json related_identifiers;
  • a DOI badge in the README and the Citing page.
  • Optional: set the repository's website field to https://bibymaths.github.io/neuralopt/, so it shows on GitHub.
path: Release engineering plan: tags, releases, PyPI, versioned docs

items.title: 12. Scope
items.text:
• v0.1.0–v0.6.0 get annotated tags, GitHub pre-releases (with assets except v0.6.0, per D2) and versioned docs.
  • They are never published to PyPI: pypi_ok is false below 0.7.0, and the backfill runs with publish_pypi=false.
  • v0.7.0 is the first PyPI release.
path: Release engineering plan: tags, releases, PyPI, versioned docs

items.title: 13. Actions storage
items.text:
• Artifacts are kept only between the jobs of one release run, with retention-days: 3.
  • CI and docs workflows upload no artifacts. Docs deploy by pushing gh-pages, not by Pages artifacts.
  • Release files are kept on the GitHub release.

items.title: 14. Also in Phase 2: the compiled-engine default flip
items.text:
This is already implemented test-first on a local stash, and is still uncommitted:

  • Default changed: minimize(..., preconditioned_engine=...) now defaults to "compiled".
  • v0.6 pinned: scripts/run_trajectory_curvature_v0_6.py passes preconditioned_engine="python" explicitly at both preconditioned call sites. A new test, which parses the script's syntax tree, enforces this.
  • Script hash recorded, results untouched: the script's sha256 changes from 35c1e401…50d1. The new hash goes in the release notes and engine-speed-v0.7.md. results/trajectory-curvature-v0.6.0.json is not touched.
  • Host-gradient tests pinned: three tests in tests/test_trajectory.py use host gradients that are deliberately inconsistent with the objective. They test the Python loop, so they are now pinned to "python".
  • New tests: the default is compiled; and with a host gradient, the default fails closed with a message naming preconditioned_engine='python'.
  • v0.7 scripts: they all pass "compiled" explicitly, so they are unaffected.
  • Measured: full pytest gives 196 passed and 1 skipped (diffrax not installed). The legacy golden tests pass.

D5, decided: this PR adds a dated note (2026-11-22) to gram-space-v0.7.md → "Decision and next work". It says the user chose amortized optimization over problem families as the next direction, and that learned guidance for certified search is deferred, not cancelled. The note is added below the existing bullet, which stays as written for the record.

items.title: Phase 3 order (each push needs your go-ahead)
items.text:
1. Push the annotated tags v0.1.0–v0.6.0. Ask first.
  2. Backfill the GitHub releases: release.yml via workflow_dispatch, one tag at a time, with publish_pypi=false. v0.6.0 gets no files.
  3. Backfill the docs: scripts/backfill_docs.py --push (0.1–0.6). Then deploy dev from main, and report the strict/non-strict list. Ask before pushing gh-pages.
  4. STOP: you set Pages to the gh-pages branch and enable Zenodo (manual steps 4 and 7).
  5. Tag v0.7.0 on main. Ask first. release.yml then does the following:
  6. verify, test and build;
  7. publish to PyPI (after your approval in the pypi environment);
  8. create the GitHub release;
  9. deploy docs 0.7 with aliases latest and default.
  10. Zenodo archives the release.
  11. Report the release URLs, the docs URL and the PyPI page, then open the DOI follow-up PR once you send me the DOI.

items.title: Release notes
items.text:
Every NeuralOpt release is an alpha research release. Versions before 0.7.0 were tagged retroactively on 2026-11-22 and are not on PyPI.

Version Date (UTC) Summary Result 0.7.0 2026-11-22 Compiled engine (speed only); pre-registered Gram-space history model does not beat the untrained BB step; first PyPI release. negative 0.6.0 2026-11-21 Secant-history features and a shared preconditioned loop; an untrained BB step beats every learned arm by about one decade. negative 0.5.0 2026-11-20 Scale-aware bounded geometry; learned geometry does not beat validation-tuned fixed geometry. negative 0.4.0 2026-11-15 Trained stochastic mobility and mass geometry; learned BAOAB geometry does not beat a fixed diagonal. negative 0.3.0 2026-11-15 Langevin and BAOAB candidates, Fokker–Planck diagnostics and a function-space reference. infrastructure 0.2.0 2026-11-15 Outcome-driven training, trajectory diagnostics, certified scheduling and Hamiltonian proposals. infrastructure 0.1.0 2026-11-14 Transformer optimization policy with restricted, independently replayed interval certificates. infrastructure

For a condensed list of changes, see the changelog.

items.title: NeuralOpt v0.1.0
items.text:
Released 2026-11-14 (UTC merge date) · PR #1 · commits

First research prototype: a small transformer optimization policy for box-bounded problems, plus a restricted interval certificate system that does not depend on the model. Result type: infrastructure.

This release was tagged retroactively on 2026-11-22; it was not published to PyPI.

items.title: Highlights
items.text:
• A transformer policy that proposes optimization steps directly, for objectives of any dimension.
  • Restricted interval branch-and-bound certificates with independent replay. The learned model cannot affect whether a certificate is valid.
  • A held-out smoke check in which the trained policy loses decisively to SciPy L-BFGS-B.

items.title: Features
items.text:
• Direct transformer policy: normalized coordinate tokens, two task tokens, and heads for direction, independent proposal, step length, a positive diagonal D and a low-rank U. The update applies D + U Uᵀ without forming a dense matrix.
  • A fixed reject-and-contract rule, so worse or nonfinite candidates are not propagated.
  • Bounded Problem API (box constraints, gradients required).
  • Deterministic synthetic training on quadratics and portable .npz checkpoints; the bundled demo checkpoint is demo-v0.1.0.npz.
  • Interval certification over a small serializable expression language, with one-ULP outward rounding after every supported operation; unsupported operations fail closed.
  • Model-independent certificate replay that re-evaluates retained terminal boxes.
  • A neuralopt command-line interface (train-demo).

items.title: Research results
items.text:
Infrastructure only; the one smoke check rejects H2 (competitiveness with a classical solver) for this checkpoint and task distribution.

  • On three held-out four-dimensional quadratics (budget 100), the median final objective was 13.0525 for the trained policy, 195.745 for random weights and 2.14e-12 for SciPy L-BFGS-B. Median end-to-end times, compilation included, were 0.635 s, 0.652 s and 0.0329 s.
  • Three instances are a smoke check, not statistical evidence for H1.
  • Raw measurements: results/heldout-smoke.json.

Reports: smoke benchmark, mathematical specification, experiment plan, literature audit, novelty and falsification, limitations.

items.title: Fixes
items.text: • Certificate verification was hardened before merge (commit 8b89604).

items.title: Documentation
items.text:
• Docs site (Zensical) with the theory, experiment plan, literature, novelty, limitations and smoke-benchmark pages.
  • README, CONTRIBUTING, CODE_OF_CONDUCT, SECURITY and artifacts/README.md.
  • Example: examples/kinetic_inverse.py.

items.title: Build and CI
items.text:
• CI on Python 3.11 and 3.12: ruff, pyright, pytest with coverage, uv build and twine check.
  • A scheduled and manual "Research smoke" workflow that trains a 20-step demo model.
  • pre-commit, pixi.toml, CITATION.cff, .zenodo.json, cliff.toml and .bumpversion.toml.

items.title: Breaking changes
items.text: None.

items.title: Known limitations
items.text:
• No claim of superiority or production maturity. The training curriculum is small and supervised and does not establish transfer beyond its sampled quadratics.
  • Gradients are required; only box constraints are supported. Residuals and nonlinear constraints are metadata only.
  • Certification supports an explicit expression language, not JAXPR. It assumes correctly rounded host operations and libm, is not IEEE 1788 conformant, and is a validated numerical result, not a machine-checked proof.
  • The v0.1.0 verifier did not check domain coverage of retained boxes; v0.2.0 added it.
  • The random-weight smoke median (195.745) cannot be reproduced because its seed was not recorded; v0.2.0 reports 27.4117 with seed 123.
  • The retroactive release workflow does not rerun the test suite at this tag.

items.title: NeuralOpt v0.2.0
items.text:
Released 2026-11-15 (UTC merge date) · PR #2 · commits

Research foundation for outcome-driven training, trajectory diagnostics, certified scheduling and opt-in Hamiltonian proposals, with smoke-scale evidence only. Result type: infrastructure.

This release was tagged retroactively on 2026-11-22; it was not published to PyPI.

items.title: Highlights
items.text:
• Differentiable multi-horizon regret training through unrolled updates.
  • Trajectory diagnostics that diagnose the v0.1 policy's failure: good directions, but steps that are too long and a proposal head that is never accepted.
  • Opt-in native JAX Hamiltonian (HMC) proposals with explicit cost accounting.
  • Certificate replay now checks domain coverage and non-overlap of retained boxes.

items.title: Features
items.text:
• unrolled_regret_loss: lax.scan unrolling with robust normalized best-so-far regret; requires an explicit known optimum.
  • Normalized box-coordinate transforms for positions and gradients, round-trip tested.
  • A matched-input MLP policy as an architecture ablation (no attention).
  • Evaluation-neutral trajectory diagnostics: one row per objective evaluation, no extra calls.
  • Certification scheduling controls (lower-bound or width priority, widest or round-robin splitting) and callbacks for learned ranking. Callbacks affect only the order of work, never bounds, pruning or termination.
  • candidate_method="hamiltonian": leapfrog with Metropolis correction, logistic box transform with its Jacobian, fixed or learned diagonal-plus-low-rank mass, and a separate feasible incumbent.

items.title: Research results
items.text:
Infrastructure with smoke-scale evidence only; the outcome-trained smoke checkpoint is a negative result and is not promoted.

  • Outcome-training smoke (12 meta-updates): the checkpoint worsened an unseen 8D rotated quadratic from 89.41 to 164.71. It is kept as neuralopt-v0.2.0-smoke.npz.
  • A fixed normalized-gradient control beats v0.1.0 on every recorded smoke family. Each family is a single instance, so this is not a superiority claim.
  • Diagnostics: v0.1 directions have median descent cosine 0.833–0.999, yet acceptance is 0–4.1%; the proposal head uses 24 of 49 evaluations and is never accepted.
  • HMC smoke (15 instances, three seeds): identity HMC beats direct on 8/15 pairs and learned-metric HMC on 9/15, but learned beats identity on only 7/15. Learned mass geometry is not supported (H2).
  • Certification: no learned scheduling policy was trained, so no speedup is claimed.

Reports: training, benchmarks, certification, generalization, trajectory diagnostics, Hamiltonian theory, Hamiltonian correctness, Hamiltonian related work.

items.title: Fixes
items.text:
• After a rejected candidate, x moved without being evaluated, so its stored value no longer matched its gradient. The current state now stays unchanged after rejection.
  • Certificate replay closes the v0.1.0 domain-accounting omission (volume and overlap checks).
  • Benchmarks enforce evaluation budgets strictly and handle nonfinite samples without replacing a valid incumbent.
  • Training regularizers compare directions and gradients in the same normalized coordinates.
  • Regret-training numerics hardened; learned-policy architecture parameters validated; HMC chain state preserved exactly between transitions.

items.title: Documentation
items.text: • New reports listed under Research results.

items.title: Build and CI
items.text: • Version 0.2.0 in pyproject.toml, neuralopt.__version__ and CITATION.cff.

items.title: Breaking changes
items.text: None.

items.title: Known limitations
items.text:
• All evidence is smoke-scale (single instances or 15 instances, three seeds).
  • Hamiltonian proposals are opt-in. History-adaptive learned metrics have no stationary-distribution claim.
  • Hamiltonian incumbents are not injected into certified search.
  • The retroactive release workflow does not rerun the test suite at this tag.

items.title: NeuralOpt v0.3.0
items.text:
Released 2026-11-15 (UTC merge date) · PR #3 · commits

Opt-in overdamped and underdamped Langevin candidates, Fokker–Planck diagnostics and a periodic function-space reference, with negative smoke evidence for learned geometry. Result type: infrastructure.

This release was tagged retroactively on 2026-11-22; it was not published to PyPI.

items.title: Highlights
items.text:
• Opt-in overdamped Euler–Maruyama and underdamped BAOAB candidate trajectories with identity or learned diagonal-plus-low-rank geometry.
  • Exact small-dimensional mobility divergence and weak Fokker–Planck diagnostics.
  • A periodic Gaussian function-space reference that refines consistently across four resolutions.

items.title: Features
items.text:
• Overdamped Langevin (Euler–Maruyama) and BAOAB integrators with episode-frozen geometry, explicit PRNG keys and the same logistic box transform as HMC.
  • mobility_divergence: exact Itô divergence term via jacfwd, for small dimensions.
  • Weak-form Fokker–Planck generator residual and an analytic Gaussian free-energy reference.
  • Periodic Gaussian reference measure with mesh-normalized Fourier reconstruction at 32, 64, 128 and 256 points.
  • Objective, gradient, integration and timing costs reported separately.

items.title: Research results
items.text:
Infrastructure; the smoke evidence for learned stochastic geometry is negative.

  • 15 instances, three seeds, nominal budget 100 (results/stochastic-smoke-v0.3.0.json).
  • Overdamped identity and learned mobility beat direct on only 5/15 and 4/15 pairs. Identity and learned BAOAB each beat direct on 11/15.
  • Learned geometry has not established a consistent advantage over identity.
  • Gates: distribution-aware training and function-space transfer are partial; certification injection is blocked. Certification lower bounds are unchanged.

Reports: Langevin theory, Fokker–Planck, Gibbs measures, function spaces, stochastic research status, stochastic limitations and gates.

items.title: Fixes
items.text:
• Nonfinite Langevin coordinates are rejected.
  • Fourier refinement and optional-import checks corrected.

items.title: Documentation
items.text: • New reports listed under Research results.

items.title: Build and CI
items.text:
• New optional extra sde (diffrax>=0.7.2) for an independent identity-mobility Euler reference; the base package does not import it.
  • Version 0.3.0 in pyproject.toml, neuralopt.__version__ and CITATION.cff.

items.title: Breaking changes
items.text: None.

items.title: Known limitations
items.text:
• Euler–Maruyama and BAOAB have finite-step bias; history-adaptive geometry has no fixed invariant measure. No exact Gibbs sampling is claimed.
  • No Langevin-specific checkpoint exists; the v0.1 transformer was not trained for mobility.
  • The function-space experiment validates a discretized reference problem only; no mesh-independent transformer claim is made.
  • The smoke study is too small for publication-level intervals, and hyperparameters were not tuned on a separate validation set.
  • The retroactive release workflow does not rerun the test suite at this tag.

items.title: NeuralOpt v0.4.0
items.text:
Released 2026-11-15 (UTC merge date) · PR #4 · commits

Trains transformer mobility and mass geometry through differentiable overdamped and BAOAB trajectories; learned BAOAB geometry does not beat a fixed diagonal. Result type: negative.

This release was tagged retroactively on 2026-11-22; it was not published to PyPI.

items.title: Highlights
items.text:
• Transformer diagonal-plus-low-rank mobility and mass heads trained end to end through stochastic trajectories.
  • A held-out ablation against identity, fixed-diagonal and untrained geometry with paired bootstrap intervals.
  • The simple fixed diagonal remains the strongest supported BAOAB result.

items.title: Features
items.text:
• stochastic_geometry_loss: pathwise differentiation through explicit-noise overdamped Euler or BAOAB trajectories with episode-frozen geometry.
  • Losses: multi-horizon log1p regret, a stability penalty, a fixed compute-cost term, a weak-generator (Fokker–Planck) term and an optional Gaussian free-energy surrogate (disabled in the reported run).
  • Ablation arms: identity, fixed diagonal, untrained, regret-trained and regret-plus-Fokker–Planck.
  • Reproduction script scripts/run_geometry_training_v0_4.py (with --reuse-checkpoints) and checkpoints artifacts/neuralopt-v0.4.0-*.npz.

items.title: Research results
items.text:
Negative: learned BAOAB geometry does not beat the fixed diagonal, and Fokker–Planck transfer to BAOAB is inconclusive.

  • Ten held-out pairs, budget 80; paired mean log1p(regret) against identity, negative is better (results/geometry-training-v0.4.0.json).
  • BAOAB fixed diagonal: −0.441 [−0.878, −0.078]. BAOAB regret-trained: −0.028 [−0.259, 0.207]. BAOAB transferred regret + FP: −0.247 [−0.752, 0.072].
  • Overdamped: every learned interval crosses zero against identity.
  • Overdamped FP − regret: −0.048 [−0.105, −0.006] on the ten pairs. This is a small effect on a small prespecified set, not a general advantage.
  • At budget 40, transferred FP geometry was worse for BAOAB at both unseen temperatures.

Report: distribution-aware training.

items.title: Fixes
items.text:
• The weak-generator loss evaluates the Gaussian noise term analytically; sampling it added a variance term that rewarded shrinking the mobility.
  • BAOAB training samples its initial momentum from N(0, T M), matching inference.
  • fixed_metric_diag is cast to the problem's floating dtype (an integer array kept an integer dtype before).

items.title: Documentation
items.text: • New report: distribution-aware-training.md; training.md gained a stochastic geometry section.

items.title: Build and CI
items.text: • Version 0.4.0 in pyproject.toml, neuralopt.__version__ and CITATION.cff.

items.title: Breaking changes
items.text: None.

items.title: Known limitations
items.text:
• Small study: six training tasks, ten primary held-out pairs, one training seed, no BBOB or scientific inverse problem.
  • The FP weight was not selected on a separate validation sweep.
  • Transfer evaluations use four instances; their intervals are descriptive.
  • v0.5.0 found that the v0.4 feature map discarded the gradient norm, so the model could not adapt to objective scale.
  • The retroactive release workflow does not rerun the test suite at this tag.

items.title: NeuralOpt v0.5.0
items.text:
Released 2026-11-20 (UTC merge date) · PR #5 · commits

Scale-aware, bounded learned geometry evaluated on 30 held-out instances; it did not beat a validation-tuned fixed geometry. Result type: negative.

This release was tagged retroactively on 2026-11-22; it was not published to PyPI.

items.title: Highlights
items.text:
• Exact reproduction of every deterministic v0.4 metric (timings excluded), and reconciliation of its two reported FP results.
  • A diagnosis: the v0.4 features discarded the gradient norm, so geometry could not adapt to objective scale.
  • A held-out comparison with disjoint validation tuning, at unseen dimensions 7, 8 and 10.

items.title: Features
items.text:
• Opt-in bounded log gradient-scale feature in place of the constant feature, using the same input width.
  • Bounded geometry for new checkpoints: diagonal bounded in log space; low-rank factor normalized by dimension and rank and bounded with tanh. Legacy checkpoints behave as before.
  • Diagonal-only, low-rank-only and full geometry heads as explicit ablations.
  • Temperature and friction sampled from their inference ranges during training; optional multi-key pathwise meta-gradients.
  • Scripts: scripts/run_transfer_geometry_v0_5.py and scripts/run_geometry_diagnostics_v0_5.py.

items.title: Research results
items.text:
Negative: learned geometry did not beat the validation-tuned fixed geometry overall.

  • 30 held-out instances, budget 100; paired mean log1p(regret) against tuned fixed geometry, positive is worse (results/transfer-geometry-v0.5.0.json).
  • Overdamped learned diagonal: +0.075 [−0.064, 0.246]; learned full: +0.088 [0.021, 0.164]; learned FP: +0.079 [0.009, 0.178]; learned low rank: +0.315 [0.065, 0.609].
  • BAOAB learned diagonal +0.053 [−0.247, 0.353] and full +0.058 [−0.204, 0.322].
  • Learned geometry helped isotropic tasks but regressed on ill-conditioned and rotated quadratics (and, for BAOAB, Rastrigin).
  • A 36-update full checkpoint also had a worse point estimate, +0.103 [−0.058, 0.329]; 144 updates narrowed the interval but stayed worse, so training budget alone does not explain the result. FP regularization did not establish an improvement.
  • Diagnosis: a single gradient cannot identify rotated curvature; the limitation is information, not positive definiteness.

Report: transferable geometry.

items.title: Fixes
items.text: • v0.4 reproduced exactly (results/geometry-diagnostics-v0.5.0.json). Its two overdamped FP − regret values came from two checkpoint generations; the corrected −0.048 [−0.105, −0.006] supersedes the pre-review −0.089 [−0.181, −0.008].

items.title: Documentation
items.text: • New report: transferable-geometry.md.

items.title: Build and CI
items.text: • Version 0.5.0 in pyproject.toml, neuralopt.__version__ and CITATION.cff.

items.title: Breaking changes
items.text: None. Legacy checkpoint behavior is preserved.

items.title: Known limitations
items.text:
• One meta-training seed and 30 final instances; six instances per family, so family means are diagnostic only.
  • Objective closures are compiled independently, and transformer overhead remains material.
  • Timings are single-host and descriptive.
  • The retroactive release workflow does not rerun the test suite at this tag.

items.title: NeuralOpt v0.6.0
items.text:
Released 2026-11-21 (UTC merge date) · PR #6 · commits

Opt-in secant-history features and a shared preconditioned loop, tested in a pre-registered multi-seed study; an untrained Barzilai–Borwein step beats every learned arm by about one decade. Result type: negative.

This release was tagged retroactively on 2026-11-22; it was not published to PyPI.

No sdist or wheel. At this commit pyproject.toml, neuralopt.__version__ and CITATION.cff still read 0.5.0, so a build would be mislabelled. This GitHub release has no build files; use the git tag or the source archive.

items.title: Highlights
items.text:
• history-v1 trajectory features built only from actually evaluated states.
  • One preconditioned loop shared by every arm, with objective and gradient calls charged to one budget.
  • A golden regression test pins v0.1–v0.5 checkpoints and inference outputs.
  • A pre-registered study: three training seeds per arm, 84 final-test tasks at unseen dimensions 7/10/16.

items.title: Features
items.text:
• neuralopt.trajectory: a fixed-shape buffer of normalized (u, g_u, f) records. Rejected candidates only increment a counter. Masked secant pairs and twelve scale-invariant, permutation-equivariant curvature and reliability features.
  • ModelConfig(feature_set="history-v1", history_length=K) with checkpoint schema neuralopt-policy/v0.6-history-v1. Unknown, stripped or inconsistent schemas fail closed; legacy files are written byte-compatibly.
  • minimize(..., candidate_method="preconditioned"): hard acceptance, step halving after rejection, no Hessian-vector products. Negative sᵀy is reported, never inverted.
  • train(..., objective="history"): a lax.scan mirror of the loop, tested equal to inference.

items.title: Research results
items.text:
Negative: an untrained Barzilai–Borwein (BB) step beats every learned arm by about one decade, and attention adds nothing over an MLP.

  • tf-h8 − BB on the curvature domain: +0.92 [+0.59, +1.25] (positive means BB is better). L-BFGS-B leads by about six decades.
  • H1 supported: history plus a rejection signal beats a matched no-history control, −0.54 [−0.80, −0.32]. The control also drops the rejection counter, so the value of secant pairs alone is not isolated.
  • H2 not supported: tf-h8 − mlp-h8 = −0.08 [−0.20, +0.06].
  • H3 not supported under the 3.5× anisotropy cap: tf-h8 beats the tuned fixed step on the curvature domain (−0.22 [−0.43, −0.03]) but fails the reliability guard on Rastrigin (+2.39) and Ackley (+0.82). Fixed geometry stays the default.
  • Results: results/trajectory-curvature-v0.6.0.json (6,300 rows, reproduced exactly).

Reports: v0.6 results, experiment protocol, literature.

items.title: Fixes
items.text: • Legacy golden-test tolerances set from measured cross-host float32 drift; the test reports every mismatch and per-case drift.

items.title: Documentation
items.text:
• Project instructions, research rules, domain skills, reviewer agents, the v0.6+ roadmap and the frozen v0.6 design.
  • New reports listed under Research results.

items.title: Build and CI
items.text:
• No version bump (see the note above).
  • CI runs the legacy golden regression test.

items.title: Breaking changes
items.text: None. v0.1–v0.5 checkpoints and outputs are pinned by the golden test.

items.title: Known limitations
items.text:
• The geometry parameterization caps off-axis anisotropy at about 3.5×; rotated κ=100–1000 needs 100–1000×, so H3 is a weaker test than the research question.
  • Training used a 50-unit budget feature and evaluation used 100; the bias on H3 and the BB comparison was not measured.
  • Three training seeds make the seed level of the bootstrap coarse.
  • Rosenbrock replicates are near-duplicates, and Rastrigin and Ackley start inside the global basin, so global search is not tested.
  • Stochastic methods reject history configurations; stochastic history geometry was not started.
  • The retroactive release workflow does not rerun the test suite at this tag.

items.title: NeuralOpt v0.7.0
items.text:
Released 2026-11-22 (UTC merge date) · PRs #7, #8 and the release-engineering PR · commits

A compiled engine makes the v0.6 loop much faster without changing its results, and a pre-registered Gram-space history model fails to beat the untrained BB step; this is also the first release on PyPI. Result type: negative.

items.title: Highlights
items.text:
• Track A (speed only, PR #7): the preconditioned loop runs as one compiled lax.while_loop, about 74× faster per warm solve than the Python loop, with the same results.
  • Track B (research, PR #8): a pre-registered Gram-space history model. Negative: it does not beat the untrained Barzilai–Borwein (BB) step, which stays the bar.
  • Release engineering: first PyPI release, tag-driven releases, versioned docs and curated release notes for every version.

items.title: Features
items.text:
• minimize(..., preconditioned_engine="compiled") and neuralopt.compiled.preconditioned_solve / preconditioned_solve_batch (vmapped over tasks of one family and dimension). Float64 parity with the Python loop to 1e-10.
  • neuralopt.task_families: parametric objectives f(x, theta) reproducing the v0.6 generator; one compilation per family and dimension.
  • neuralopt.fast_training.train_batched: compiled, batched training step with a NaN guard; skipped updates are counted in TrainingReport.skipped_steps.
  • Opt-in Gram-space history model (model_kind="gram", compiled engine only), schemas neuralopt-policy/v0.7-gram-v1 and -v2, with history-v2 masks.
  • Opt-in step-acceptance rules on the compiled engine: loop_rule="halving" (default), "armijo" and "wolfe".
  • neuralopt.gram_training: a training unroll matched to the evaluation loop, and train_batched(model_kind="gram").

items.title: Research results
items.text:
Negative: the pre-registered primary hypothesis (H1) fails, and Track A changes speed only, not quality.

  • Track A: warm tf-h8 solve 296.1 ms (Python) → 4.00 ms (compiled). Under equal work, learned geometry reaches 1e-3 on 10 of 32 tasks and 1e-6 on none; L-BFGS-B and Optimistix LBFGS reach 1e-6 on all 32.
  • Track B, H1 fails: gram-full − BB on the curvature domain is −0.224 [−0.510, +0.115]; the interval is not entirely below zero. BB stays the bar.
  • The reliability guard is also violated: Rastrigin +2.14 [+0.36, +4.34], Ackley +0.89 [+0.10, +2.08].
  • gram-full − oracle-BFGS is +4.69 [+3.76, +5.68] decades; the learned model is far from relearning L-BFGS. H2 and H3 are exploratory, with no claim.
  • An exploratory post-mortem (training and validation tasks only, no claims): wider models imitate the oracle better but none performs well in the loop; A/C gradients reach the heads without a saddle. The cause is undetermined.
  • Next direction: amortized optimization over problem families. Learned guidance for certified search is deferred, not cancelled.

Reports: engine speed (Track A), Gram-space model (Track B).

items.title: Fixes
items.text:
• The compiled engine casts the budget fraction to the parameters' dtype, as the Python loop does (float32 checkpoints on float64 problems).
  • τ and σ for Gram runs are recorded in their own fields; they were mislabelled.

items.title: Documentation
items.text:
• Docs restructured: installation, quickstart, when to use NeuralOpt, user guide, research reports by version, release notes, changelog, citing and API reference.
  • Release notes for v0.1.0–v0.7.0.

items.title: Build and CI
items.text:
• First PyPI release, by trusted publishing.
  • Tag-driven release workflow; GitHub releases use these notes.
  • Versioned docs (Zensical with its mike fork).
  • git-cliff with conventional commits, and a PR-title check.
  • Release-metadata consistency checks on every PR: pyproject.toml, CITATION.cff, .zenodo.json, CHANGELOG.md and the release notes.
  • New logo and a Citing page.
  • Optimistix added to the benchmark extra only; it never runs inside inference.

items.title: Breaking changes
items.text:
• minimize(..., preconditioned_engine=...) now defaults to "compiled". candidate_method="preconditioned" with a host/NumPy gradient= now raises a ValueError that names preconditioned_engine="python". Pass that to keep the previous behavior.
  • neuralopt.__version__ now comes from the package metadata.
  • The v0.6 reproduction script scripts/run_trajectory_curvature_v0_6.py now pins preconditioned_engine="python". Its sha256 changed from 35c1e401e6bc8bccfaecbb9168708335e9a7d4fbd6498e35d635ed54da5e50d1 to f80e8acc6bda802d65a00ea73e80e179ffcf7f8d0ddd9e23492220581b27e9f3. results/trajectory-curvature-v0.6.0.json is unchanged.

items.title: Known limitations
items.text:
• Alpha research release: learned components do not beat BB or classical quasi-Newton methods in these benchmarks.
  • In float32 the compiled engine matches the Python loop only to rounding level, not bit for bit.
  • Track B: five training seeds, float64 and exact gradients only; test dimensions 7, 16 and 32 for a model trained at 4, 8 and 12. Why A and C were not learned is not established.
  • Optimistix solvers have no box bounds; they are benchmark references only.

items.title: Benchmark protocol
items.text:
Machine-readable rows must separate objective calls, gradient calls, derivative products, compilation, warm execution, loading, and total time. Compilation is not silently amortized. Comparisons are paired by instance and seed and report medians, intervals, success, and anytime regret. Objective wrappers enforce the requested budget even when a third-party solver would finish an over-budget line search. Regret is null, rather than zero, when a task has no known optimum. All baselines return the tracked best finite in-budget observation. Nonfinite samples cannot replace a valid incumbent; a run with no finite observation fails explicitly instead of emitting a misleading NaN result. Solver state remains NumPy-compatible, but objective and gradient callbacks receive JAX arrays in the problem's declared dtype. Benchmarks therefore support the same array-specific objective operations as native NeuralOpt inference.

The current v0.2 artifact is only a smoke experiment. A fixed normalized-gradient control beats v0.1.0 on every recorded family; for example, its final values are 0.0286 versus 0.4685 (isotropic), 24.61 versus 293.0 (ill-conditioned), and 5.918 versus 71.46 (rotated). These are single instances and do not support a superiority claim. SciPy, Adam, Optimistix, differential evolution, quasi-random search, trained MLP, and BBOB performance profiles remain an uncompleted M4 milestone.

items.title: Development performance profile
items.text:
Single-run CPU timings from the development environment (November 2026) are diagnostic, not publication benchmarks. Compiling the policy, objective, and gradient once per run reduced warm learned-inference cost as follows:

Dimension Before Current Evaluations 4 7.80 ms/eval 1.18 ms/eval 100 32 8.32 ms/eval 1.70 ms/eval 100

Cold 100-evaluation runs remain about 1.1--1.2 seconds because JAX compilation dominates. Warm execution still synchronizes once per candidate and uses a Python optimization loop; batching or a compiled loop is the next runtime bottleneck. Independently, the measured 0--4.1% v0.1 acceptance rate remains a larger algorithmic efficiency problem than kernel dispatch.

items.title: Certified scheduling
items.text:
Certification now exposes deterministic lower-bound or width region priority, widest or round-robin legal splitting, and callbacks for learned ranking and split selection. Callbacks affect scheduling only: interval lower bounds, incumbents, pruning, and termination remain native and rigorous under the stated floating-point assumptions. Default lower-bound scheduling reads the global bound from the scheduling heap root. Alternative and learned priorities maintain a second lower-bound heap with lazy deletion, avoiding a full active-set scan after every processed node.

Every terminal pruned box is serialized. Independent replay re-evaluates each interval bound, checks that boxes lie inside the original domain, compares total leaf and domain volume, rejects positive-volume overlap, and checks the final gap. Partition replay follows shared bisection boundaries recursively, avoiding quadratic all-pairs overlap checks. This closes the v0.1.0 verifier's domain-accounting omission while remaining practical for thousands of leaves.

On the dependency-stress expression x[0] - x[0], 8,191 processed nodes and 8,192 retained leaves took about 0.89 seconds for search and 0.68 seconds for replay after the current fixes. Scaling from 2,048 to 16,384 leaves was close to linear. Search time is dominated by interval-expression evaluation and Interval object validation; replay is dominated by recursive partition reconstruction, followed by re-evaluating every retained interval bound.

No learned certification policy has yet been trained or benchmarked. Therefore there is no supported node-count or wall-time speedup claim.

items.title: Equations and gradient path
items.text:
The transformer predicts A = diag(d) + U U^T, where d is produced by a softplus plus 1e-4. Overdamped training uses

\[z_{n+1}=z_n-hA abla U(z_n)+\sqrt{2Th}\,(D^{1/2}\xi+U\eta),\]

with the bounded transformed potential U(z) = f(x(z)) - T log|dx/dz|. BAOAB uses the same factor as a mass matrix, its Woodbury inverse in the drift, and exact Ornstein--Uhlenbeck momentum covariance T(1-exp(-2 gamma h)) M. Explicit PRNG keys make trajectories reproducible and pathwise differentiation carries gradients through both drift geometry and noise scale. The BAOAB rollout also samples its initial momentum from N(0, T M) using the first predicted mass, matching the inference transition rather than beginning from an artificial zero-momentum state.

The weak Fokker--Planck term compares the conditional expected one-step change of phi(z)=mean(z^2) with

\[L\phi=b^T abla\phi+ frac12\operatorname{tr}(a abla^2\phi), \qquad a=2TA.\]

Mobility is frozen only within an episode. Updating it from trajectory history makes the optimizer nonstationary. Euler and BAOAB retain finite-step bias; the experiment makes no exact Gibbs or finite-step stationarity claim. The quadratic Gaussian noise contribution is evaluated analytically rather than sampled, avoiding a variance term that would reward shrinking mobility.

items.title: Protocol
items.text:
• Model: width 16, four heads, rank two, one transformer layer.
  • Training: 36 Adam updates at 3e-4, global gradient clipping, seed 17.
  • Trajectory: six episodes, two integration steps per episode, horizons 2/4/6, step size 0.008, temperature 0.5.
  • Training set: shifted, rotated, condition-10 to condition-1000 quadratics, Rastrigin, Ackley, and Rosenbrock in dimensions two through four.
  • Held out: ten paired instances spanning rotated and ill-conditioned quadratics, Rosenbrock, Ackley, and Rastrigin in unseen dimensions three to six and seeds 40/41.
  • Primary evaluation: objective budget 80 and temperature 0.5. Paired percentile bootstrap intervals use 10,000 resamples.
  • Transfer evaluation: temperatures 0.25/1.0 and budgets 40/120 on four held-out instances. These small four-instance intervals are descriptive.

The machine-readable record is results/geometry-training-v0.4.0.json. The three portable checkpoints are in artifacts/neuralopt-v0.4.0-*.npz. Reproduce with uv run python scripts/run_geometry_training_v0_4.py; use --reuse-checkpoints to repeat evaluation without retraining.

items.title: Primary held-out results
items.text:
Differences are paired mean log1p(regret) relative to identity; negative is better. All variants used the same objective budgets. Overdamped runs used 78 gradient evaluations and 52 integration steps; BAOAB used 75 and 30.

Integrator and geometry Mean log regret Difference vs identity (95% CI) Wins/10 Overdamped identity 2.854 0.000 -- Overdamped fixed diagonal 2.804 -0.050 [-0.282, 0.143] 3 Overdamped untrained transformer 2.661 -0.193 [-0.553, 0.075] 5 Overdamped regret trained 2.678 -0.177 [-0.452, 0.056] 6 Overdamped regret + FP 2.630 -0.224 [-0.552, 0.039] 6 BAOAB identity 1.712 0.000 -- BAOAB fixed diagonal 1.272 -0.441 [-0.878, -0.078] 6 BAOAB untrained transformer 1.460 -0.253 [-0.790, 0.091] 4 BAOAB regret trained 1.685 -0.028 [-0.259, 0.207] 3 BAOAB transferred regret + FP 1.465 -0.247 [-0.752, 0.072] 4

The direct paired FP-minus-regret comparison is -0.048 with 95% interval [-0.105, -0.006] for overdamped dynamics (5/10 wins). This is evidence on the small prespecified held-out set, not a universal advantage. For BAOAB transfer the difference is -0.220 [-0.570, 0.022], so no improvement is established.

At unseen temperatures and budgets the overdamped FP-minus-regret point estimate remained negative in all four settings, but every four-instance interval touched or crossed zero. At budget 40, transferred FP geometry was worse for BAOAB at both temperatures (+0.377 at 0.25 and +0.357 at 1.0). The simple fixed diagonal remains the strongest supported BAOAB result.

Training took 22.9 seconds for overdamped regret, 28.9 seconds for BAOAB regret, and 17.3 seconds for regret plus FP on the recorded CPU run. Median warm inference was about 0.08--0.12 seconds. First-call timings in the shared process are cache- and order-sensitive and are retained in the artifact rather than interpreted as isolated compilation measurements.

items.title: Correctness and remaining gaps
items.text:
Tests verify positive diagonals, diagonal-plus-low-rank covariance, exact OU fluctuation--dissipation scaling, reproducibility, Gaussian moments, finite nonzero gradients into both geometry heads, weak generator identities, and nonfinite-coordinate rejection. Certification code and independent replay are unchanged.

The experiment is still small: six training tasks, ten primary held-out pairs, one training seed, and no BBOB or scientific inverse problem. FP weighting was not selected on a separate validation sweep, free-energy regularization remains disabled, and objective closures compile independently. Stronger claims require multiple training seeds, larger held-out suites, family-level uncertainty, and batched parameterized task generators.

items.title: v0.7 Track A: compiled inference and training (speed only)
items.text:
Track A changes how the v0.6 preconditioned rule runs, not what it computes. All new paths are opt-in.

  • minimize(..., preconditioned_engine="compiled") and neuralopt.compiled.preconditioned_solve(_batch) give the same results as the Python loop: identical to 1e-10 in float64, and statistically equivalent in float32.
  • Since the v0.7.0 release the default is "compiled" (see "Default engine" below). The v0.6 reproduction script pins "python", so the frozen v0.6 results remain reproducible bit for bit.

items.title: A1. Where the time went (profile)
items.text:
One warm tf-h8 solve: frozen v0.6 checkpoint, rotated κ=100, d=16, budget 100, float32.

Component ms per solve push_history (38 eager calls, 1.9 ms each) 71 objective + gradient, including 2 recompilations per call (minimize rebuilds jit(grad(f)) every time) 64 eager coordinate transforms (normalize, candidate, gradient→u, denormalize) 59 jitted features + model (120 dispatch-bound calls, ~140 µs each) 17 remaining Python, eager ops and host syncs 43 total (instrumented; 241 ms uninstrumented) 256 estimated compiled compute, vmap-amortized 0.8 (0.3%)

Host dispatch and per-call recompilation account for more than 99% of the wall time.

items.title: A2–A4. Compiled engine
items.text:
• Loop. A single jit runs a lax.while_loop. The gradient is evaluated under lax.cond only when a candidate improves, so budget accounting is unchanged. Errors come back as status codes and are raised after the loop. Diagnostics go into preallocated length-budget arrays.
  • Batching. preconditioned_solve_batch vmaps over tasks objective(x, theta) of one family and dimension. Under vmap, lax.cond evaluates both branches, but gradients are still charged only on acceptance; this is tested.
  • Parity. Float64 parity is tested on rotated and Rastrigin problems across five arms: history transformer, history MLP, legacy transformer, fixed and identity. Trajectory, stored history, records and counts match to 1e-10.
  • float32. On 12 rotated tasks with the frozen tf-h8 checkpoint:
  • accepted-step counts were identical on all 12;
  • final log10 regret differed by a mean of +0.0000 decades (median |D| 3.4e-5, maximum 0.001);
  • trajectories differ only at float32 rounding level.
  • Recompilation. Repeated solves with new weights of the same shapes do not recompile.
path: v0.7: compiled engine and Gram-space model

items.title: A5. Training
items.text:
• One compilation per family and dimension. neuralopt.task_families reproduces the v0.6 generator exactly (tested to 1e-10), with parametric objectives f(x, theta).
  • One compiled training step. neuralopt.fast_training.train_batched compiles the loss, the meta-gradient and the Optax update together, vmapped over a batch of tasks.
  • NaN guard. A step with a nonfinite loss or meta-gradient leaves parameters and optimizer state unchanged. It is counted in TrainingReport.skipped_steps, never dropped silently. This is tested with f(x) = Σ√(1+x), which is singular at the lower box edge.

items.text:
• NeuralOpt loop: it proposes a candidate only while used + 2 ≤ 100.

items.title: Why Optimistix BFGS reaches only −1.21
items.text: It is not a tolerance problem. - With rtol = atol = 1e-14 (the A6 run) and again with 1e-8, every one of the 32 tasks used all 50 steps and ended with result code 7, "maximum number of steps reached". The median regret was −1.21 both times. - On task 0 the iterate moved on only 8 of the 50 steps. The other 42 were backtracking line-search trials, each charged one evaluation. - Its default initial inverse Hessian is the identity, which overshoots badly on these κ=100 problems. LBFGS scales its initial Hessian from the secant pair and reaches −9.25. - Neither solver was tuned beyond these two tolerance settings.

items.text:
• Speed. The compiled engine makes the learned policy about 74× faster per solve than the Python loop. Per solve it is about 2.4× faster than SciPy L-BFGS-B, and still about 18× slower than Optimistix LBFGS.

items.title: Hypothesis experiment plan
items.text:
All comparisons use paired task instances, seeds, dimensions, and evaluation budgets. H1 compares trained and untrained policies on held-out families and dimensions. H2 compares final and anytime regret, evaluations, failures, and wall time against an appropriate classical solver and available faithful learned baselines. H3 compares fixed widest-first branch ordering with model priority while replaying identical certificate rules. H4 records compilation, steady-state policy time, objective calls, parameter count, memory, and training cost. Ablations remove attention, history compression, gradients, low-rank factors, independent proposals, normalization augmentation, pretraining, and learned spatial guidance one factor at a time.

The bundled smoke experiment is insufficient for accepting any hypothesis: it verifies training and serialization on synthetic quadratics only.

items.title: v0.8 gate F0: headroom per family, with no learning

Status: gate F0 of the v0.8 plan (docs/plans/neuralopt-v08-amortized-families.md, §9). Nothing here is learned, and no claim in docs/research/v0.8-claims.md changes status: all remain unverified (under test). F0 only decides whether each family has enough headroom to be worth testing a learned start predictor on.

1. The CPU cap was exceeded on process CPU time.

  7. A1 and A2 use SciPy's default stopping tolerances; the reference uses tight ones.
  8. An exploratory diagnostic (not part of the F0 protocol) re-ran A1 with tight tolerances.

items.title: Fokker–Planck foundations
items.text:
For Itô drift b and covariance a = sigma sigma^T, the generator is

\[\mathcal L\varphi=b^T abla\varphi+ frac12\operatorname{tr}(a abla^2\varphi).\]

The forward Kolmogorov equation is the adjoint evolution of this generator. For fixed mobility Langevin dynamics it becomes

\[\partial_t ho= abla\cdot[A( ho abla f+T abla ho)].\]

NeuralOpt implements the small-dimensional generator and Monte Carlo weak-form residual

\[(E[\varphi(X_{n+1})]-E[\varphi(X_n)])/h-E[\mathcal L\varphi(X_n)].\]

Tests validate the Ornstein–Uhlenbeck identity with antithetic noise. This is a diagnostic primitive, not yet a transformer training result. A low residual can coexist with poor optimization regret and is not itself evidence for the central learned-optimizer hypothesis.

The free energy E[f] + T int rho log rho is implemented exactly only for a Gaussian distribution and quadratic objective. The test confirms its minimum at the analytic Gibbs covariance. No arbitrary particle entropy estimator is labelled exact free energy.

Jordan, Kinderlehrer, and Otto (1998) interpret Fokker–Planck evolution as a Wasserstein gradient flow through a minimizing-movement scheme. That continuous-time/variational result is not transferred to finite-step Euler or history-adaptive transformer coefficients.

items.title: Periodic function-space reference experiment
items.text:
There is no infinite-dimensional Lebesgue measure. Function-space probability is formulated relative to a Gaussian reference measure, following Beskos et al. (2011) and Cotter et al. (2013). NeuralOpt's initial periodic reference uses the spectral covariance

\[C_k=(\alpha+|k|^2)^{-p},\qquad p>1/2,\]

and real Fourier synthesis. The compact reconstruction problem minimizes a mesh-normalized L2 data fit plus periodic H1 regularization. Its Fourier solution is analytic, providing an independent refinement reference.

Tests at 32, 64, 128, and 256 points recover the same continuous sine/cosine solution and verify a near-zero discrete gradient. This establishes spectral operator correctness and discretization consistency only. It does not show that the transformer transfers across resolutions, that a learned operator is mesh independent, or that the finite discretization converges as a probability measure in function space.

Dense learned matrices are deliberately absent. A future learned geometry must act relative to the reference covariance through Fourier multipliers or resolution-stable low-rank corrections.

items.title: Generalization
items.text:
Coordinate inputs and gradients are explicitly transformed into normalized box coordinates. If u = 2(x-l)/(h-l)-1, then df/du = (h-l) df/dx / 2. Round-trip behavior is regression tested.

The transformer and the new shared-coordinate MLP baseline have parameter counts independent of objective dimension. The MLP consumes the same coordinate features plus budget and dimension signals, but has no attention; it is smaller than the configured transformer and provides an executable architecture ablation. The bundled checkpoint is transformer-specific. MLP inference therefore requires caller-provided MLP parameters; architecture-specific parameter keys are validated before optimization begins.

Unrotated quadratic tasks retain an elementwise weighted objective with linear storage and evaluation cost. A dense matrix is constructed only when rotation is requested; a 10,000-dimensional regression guards against accidental dense materialization in the default task curriculum.

Only one unseen-dimension smoke result is currently executed: the 12-update regret model worsened an unseen 8D rotated, condition-100 quadratic (164.71 versus 89.41 for v0.1.0). There is not yet enough evidence for interpolation or extrapolation claims. Unseen-family and multi-seed studies are outstanding.

items.title: Gibbs measures and optimization
items.text:
At temperature T, the artificial finite-dimensional Gibbs density is pi_T(x) proportional to exp(-f(x)/T). It is a distribution over feasible states, not an optimizer certificate. Lower temperature concentrates mass near low objective values under suitable assumptions but does not guarantee that a finite trajectory finds a global minimizer.

The logistic bounded transform includes its determinant so fixed-geometry continuous-time dynamics target the mapped bounded Gibbs measure. Euler, BAOAB, and adaptive learned geometry introduce distinct qualifications:

  • Euler–Maruyama and BAOAB have finite-step bias.
  • Episode-frozen learned geometry is fixed only during one episode.
  • Updating geometry from history makes the overall process nonstationary.
  • Changing temperature creates a sequence of targets, not one invariant Gibbs distribution.

Optimization therefore reports the best feasible incumbent separately from the stochastic state. Distributional accuracy, candidate improvement, and incumbent updates are independent measurements.

items.title: Result
items.text:
The claim the frozen outcome-to-claim table permits: learned geometry did not beat BB on the curvature domain; BB stays the bar. H2 and H3 are exploratory, with no claim.

This is a negative result. Read off the frozen outcome-to-claim table (pre-registration sha256 6d5489da…3cad3f), the row that applies is: Stage 1 passes, H1 fails, so:

Learned geometry did not beat BB on the curvature domain; BB stays the bar. H2 and H3 are exploratory, with no claim.

  • Primary, H1, fails. gram-full − BB on the curvature domain (diagonal κ1000, rotated κ100 and κ1000 at unseen d = 7/16/32, budget 100) is −0.224 [−0.510, +0.115]. The interval is not entirely below 0.
  • The reliability guard is also violated.
  • Rastrigin: +2.14 [+0.36, +4.34].
  • Ackley: +0.89 [+0.10, +2.08].
  • Shifted Rosenbrock: −0.06 [−0.11, −0.03].
  • Under the table, the guard changes nothing once H1 has failed. It is reported because it confirms the Stage 1 warning.
  • The learned model is far from relearning L-BFGS.
  • gram-full − oracle-BFGS is +4.69 [+3.76, +5.68] decades.
  • Its step directions have a median cosine of 0.48 with the oracle's on 200 probe states.
  • Per family it is almost identical to the learned scalar step (gram-scalar): A and C added essentially nothing.
  • BB stays the bar, and no claim is made for the Gram model. The headroom the oracle shows (A and C set to BFGS values) exists but was not learned.

items.title: 3. Conclusion (exploratory)
items.text:
Depth and width are not the binding limit. - Width improves imitation fit: relative A error falls from 0.70 to 0.33–0.35, and the direction cosine rises from 0.92 to 0.96–0.97. Depth adds little. - But no fitted configuration performs well in the shared loop. Every one is worse than BB on validation (−1.79 to −2.70, against −3.32), and worse than the frozen meta-trained model (−3.3 to −3.9). - Even direction cosines of 0.96–0.97 with the oracle do not reproduce the oracle's −15.99. That points to the loop's sensitivity to small metric errors and to the shift between oracle-visited and self-visited states. Neither cause was isolated.

There is no head saddle. - Gradients reach the A and C heads from the frozen init, and A/C magnitudes grow 3–30× in 200 updates. - They stay 20–150× below the oracle's median ‖A*‖_F of 4.5. - The A/C gradient is only about 0.14–0.19 of the δ/σ gradient, and every update is dominated by δ: total norms of 135–370 are clipped to 1.0. - With init scale 1.0, A and C do not collapse, but their share stays at 0.44–0.57, and δ moves most (|δ| 0.3 to 1.1–1.6).

Overall, the failure is undetermined, leaning towards optimization and objective signal rather than representation. The meta-gradient mostly drives the scalar step (δ/σ). Larger networks fit the oracle better without performing better in the loop. Which change would let A and C be learned (the loss, the gradient balance or clipping, on-policy imitation, or more updates) was not tested. Any such change belongs to a future v0.8 pre-registration, not to v0.7.

items.title: The model (B1; opt-in, schema neuralopt-policy/v0.7-gram-v1)
items.text:
Source: neuralopt.gram. It runs only through minimize(..., model_kind="gram", candidate_method="preconditioned", preconditioned_engine="compiled").

  • Tokens. There is one token per stored secant pair plus one for the current gradient: K+1 tokens, independent of the dimension d. Every input is a normalized inner product among the columns of S, Y and g_u, or a log norm ratio, mask, pair age, rejection count, last rejected step length, or observed/predicted change ratio of the last rejected trial. Rejected trials never form secant pairs.
  • Outputs. Masked attention produces A and C (K×K), δ and σ. They define P = τ[e^δ (I − ŜAŶᵀ)(I − ŶAᵀŜᵀ) + ŜCCᵀŜᵀ] + ετI, applied without forming the matrix in O(Kd).
  • τ = sᵀs/sᵀy of the newest valid pair when sᵀy > 0, otherwise fallback_length/‖g_u‖.
  • The step is u' = clip(u − shrink·σ·P g_u, −1, 1), with the same acceptance and accounting as the shared loop.
  • What P is. P is symmetric positive definite for every A and C, and it is an inverse metric (P y ≈ s). Its directional structure is confined to span(Ŝ, Ŷ); on the complement it is isotropic.
path: v0.7: compiled engine and Gram-space model

items.title: Gate 1: algebraic, float64 (tests/test_gram.py)
items.text:
All checks pass.

  • (a) The model can express L-BFGS. With every valid pair having sᵀy > 0, set
  • τe^δ = γ = sᵀy/yᵀy of the newest pair,
  • A = R⁻ᵀ and C = R⁻ᵀD^{1/2}/√τ, with Rᵢⱼ = sᵢᵀyⱼ for i ≤ j (chronological) and D = diag(sᵢᵀyᵢ),
  • converted to normalized columns as Â = D_s A D_y and Ĉ = D_s C.

Then P g equals the L-BFGS two-loop direction with H₀ = γI to within 1e-10. This holds for d/K = 10/4, 10/6, 16/8 and 5/5, and P y = s holds on the newest pair. The coefficients lie inside the model's output ranges. This is the compact representation of Byrd, Nocedal & Schnabel (1994); the independent derivation review found no error. - (b) SPD. P is symmetric positive definite for random A and C (minimum eigenvalue at least ετ). The matrix-free product equals the dense matrix. Masked pairs, rows and columns, contribute nothing. - (c) Invariance. Tokens are invariant to rotation of u and to positive rescaling of the objective. Whole trajectories rotate with a rotated quadratic: a ±1000 cube at the origin with an interior optimum, so clipping is never active. Trajectories are unchanged by rescaling the objective, which rescales τ, while σ is dimensionless.
path: v0.7: compiled engine and Gram-space model

items.title: Gate 2: capacity, no training (results/gram-gates-v0.7.0.json)
items.text:
Criterion, stated before the first run: for both rotated κ = 100 and κ = 1000, the oracle-BFGS arm's median log10 regret must be within one decade of SciPy L-BFGS-B on the same tasks.

Conditions: d ∈ {7, 10, 16}, 4 tasks per d, gate-only seeds 6000+, budget 100 objective+gradient units, float64. The oracle sets A, C and δ to the BFGS values and σ = 1. It lives only in the harness, scripts/gram_reference.py and scripts/run_gram_gates_v0_7.py. The harness copy of the loop reproduces the package's compiled Gram loop to 1e-10 over 37 iterations; this is checked before any oracle number is reported.

oracle-BFGS oracle clipped to the model's ranges τ only (A=C=0, δ=0, σ=1) L-BFGS-B oracle − L-BFGS-B Pass rotated κ=100, median log10 regret −13.80 −13.80 −5.23 −15.96 +2.16 no rotated κ=1000, median log10 regret −5.49 −5.49 −2.72 −8.79 +3.30 no

Further measurements: - Reached 1e-6 regret: at κ=100, oracle 12/12 and L-BFGS-B 12/12; at κ=1000, oracle 5/12 and L-BFGS-B 8/12. - Acceptance: the oracle accepted 89% of trials at κ=100 and 93% at κ=1000, so rejections are rare. - Conditioning: the oracle's P reached a median maximum condition number of 149 at κ=100 and 1,363 at κ=1000. The Gram parameterization therefore expresses at least 100× anisotropy. - Coefficient sizes: the oracle coefficients never left the model's output ranges. The maximum |Â| was 13.4 and |Ĉ| 7.8, against a bound of 100; |δ| reached 4.84, against a bound of 5. Clipping to the model's ranges changes nothing.

items.title: Reading
items.text:
• κ=100. Both arms reach 1e-6 on every task. The 2.2-decade gap lies at relative regret around 1e-14 to 1e-16, the float64 roundoff zone. Under the pre-stated rule this still counts as a failure, and it is reported as one.
  • κ=1000. The 3.3-decade gap is substantive.
  • Where the limit is. The same BFGS directions, run through this loop rule, fall well short of L-BFGS-B at equal budget. The loop accepts any decrease with a unit step and only halves after a rejection. There is no sufficient-decrease or curvature (Wolfe) condition and no step lengthening.
  • Untested explanations: the accepted steps may produce poorer secant pairs than Wolfe line-search steps do, and K = 8 against SciPy's default memory of 10 may also matter.
  • Rejection signal under clipping. With a non-diagonal P, a clipped step can ascend for every shrink factor. This is a loop-rule property, shared with v0.6, and it makes the rejection signal ambiguous near active bounds. These gate tasks have interior optima.

items.text:

  • At κ=100 both arms are at the float64 floor, and the original criterion had no regret floor.
  • For the reruns below, the user stated an amended criterion before any rerun was made:
  • per task, log10 regret below −12 counts as −12, so regrets below 1e-12 are equal;
  • an arm passes iff its floored median is within one decade of SciPy L-BFGS-B's floored median, at both κ=100 and κ=1000.

items.title: The three rules
items.text:
• halving (v0.6): one trial per iteration; any decrease is accepted; a rejection halves the next trial.
  • armijo: sufficient decrease with interpolating backtracking. Each trial costs 1 objective unit, and the accepted point costs 1 gradient unit.
  • wolfe: strong Wolfe conditions with bracketing and zoom, lengthening up to 10×. Each trial costs 2 units.

items.title: Reading
items.text:
• The step-acceptance rule is not the bottleneck for good directions.
  • Under all three rules the oracle's own step is accepted unchanged 86–93% of the time at κ=1000.
  • Changing the rule moves the oracle by at most 0.5 decades.
  • For the no-learning baselines the rule matters, in the other direction. At κ=100, τ-only does best under halving (−5.23, against −3.52 and −3.32).
  • History length matters a lot.
  • SciPy loses 2.8 decades at κ=1000 when its memory drops from 10 to 8.
  • At matched memory 8, every oracle loop is within 0.3–0.5 decades of SciPy.
  • At K=10, a gap of 2.1–2.6 decades to SciPy (maxcor 10) remains under every rule. The cause is not identified.
  • The amended criterion fails. Every arm is at the floor at κ=100, but at κ=1000 none comes within one decade of SciPy L-BFGS-B at its default memory.
  • Uncertainty. Medians over 12 tasks are coarse, and no paired intervals were computed for this ablation.

items.title: Mask diagnostic (oracle K=10, halving; results/mask-diagnostic-v0.7.0.json)
items.text: The decision rule was stated before running: relaxed masks count as meaningful only if they reduce the κ=1000 median gap to SciPy (maxcor 10) by at least one decade. - Masking is rare. Under the current thresholds (step 1e-7, relative gradient change 1e-6), only the step test fires: on 3.4% of filled pairs at κ=1000 and 18% at κ=100. The gradient-change and nonfinite tests never fire. On average 8.6 of 10 pairs are valid at κ=1000. - Relaxed masks change nothing at κ=1000. With float64 thresholds (1e-12 and 1e-10), or masking only nonfinite pairs and pairs with sᵀy ≤ 0, the oracle median stays at −6.19. The reduction is 0.0 decades, so not meaningful. - At κ=100 relaxed masks help, moving the median from −14.47 to −15.98, but that is at the float64 floor. - Paired over tasks at κ=1000, oracle − SciPy is mean +0.86 [+0.18, +1.60] (raw) and +0.69 [+0.08, +1.41] (floored at −12), with median +0.06. - The gap sits at d=10: the oracle reaches about −6 and SciPy −8.5 to −9.8. At d=7 both are at the floor; at d=16 both are near −5. - The cause is unexplained.

items.title: Step-acceptance rules (scope)
items.text: loop_rule is a step-acceptance rule in the sense of CLAUDE.md, not a solver. - It decides whether, and how far, to move along the model's proposed displacement. - The model's step is always the first trial. - No curvature is built: there is no BFGS update and no classical solver. - It is opt-in, on the compiled engine only (loop_rule="halving" | "armijo" | "wolfe", default "halving"). - The Python loop, the v0.6 rule and all frozen results are unchanged.
