items.title: Compute (pinned; process-CPU clock)
items.text:
• Total: 3.82 CPU-h, against a cap of 10. Wall time was about 1.3 h.
  • Per process: Rastrigin 0.61, Ackley 0.62, Rosenbrock 0.62, Family 1 0.71, Family 2b 1.27 CPU-h, all under the 3 CPU-h per-process cap. Each process used CPU ≈ wall.
  • Training projection (plan §8, re-based on the families still tested):
  • Three families (Rastrigin, Ackley, Family 1) × 5 seeds, each about 11 minutes (the plan's estimate): about 3 CPU-h.
  • Test-split baselines: about 2 CPU-h; TPE dominates.
  • Total about 5 CPU-h, against the approved cap of 24.
  • The policy forward cost is not yet measured (no policy code exists). It is timed at B-S3 before any training.

items.title: Deviations and caveats
items.text:
1. The BB tuning grid is smaller than the plan's. The plan listed an initial step of {1e-3, 1e-2, 1e-1} and a step clip of {1, 10}. NeuralOpt's compiled BB loop (the Gram loop with zero parameters, which v0.7 checked equals BB to 1e-10) has no step-clip parameter. So only the fallback (initial) length was tuned.
  2. Owned L-BFGS traces: rejected line-search trials count in the units, but the solver does not expose their values. Such a trial could be lower than the current value only by the tiny Armijo margin (c1 = 1e-4), so the arm's anytime regret is very slightly pessimistic.
  3. CMA-ES evaluates the shared start point first (1 unit), then runs its generations. The last generation is cut at the budget and not told to the optimizer.
  4. The B0 rule's "best baseline" is the maximum over all arms and configurations on the same 200 instances. That is optimistic for baselines, so it makes "no headroom" easier to declare.
  5. For Rosenbrock and Family 2b, the conclusion does not depend on it: several arms exceed 0.95, and the zero-search polish alone reaches 0.88 and 0.98.
  6. The basin metric saturates where the polish does the work. The uncharged 2,000-unit polish defines the basin operationally (plan §5.2). On Family 2b and Rosenbrock, almost every start lies in the global basin, so C12 cannot separate arms there. The B0 rule then also drops them from C11, as the plan specifies. Their anytime regret still differs between arms (owned multistart −3.9 versus BB −2.9 on Family 2b), but that is not tested.
  7. Rastrigin and Ackley may give little signal on C12. Basin rates of 0–17% for every baseline mean a policy must find the global basin among thousands of local minima within 100 evaluations. A negative or inconclusive C12 there is a plausible outcome.

items.title: What happens next
items.text: STOP. The next step, B-S3 (pre-registration: grids, chosen configurations, frozen cumulative-time curves, policy forward cost, criteria, seeds and sizes; frozen and hashed), waits for the user's go-ahead.

items.title: v0.8 claims register
items.text:
This register decides what v0.8 may claim. The plan is docs/plans/neuralopt-v08-amortized-families.md.

Rules: - Status values: unverified | supported | not supported | inconclusive. - Every claim starts unverified. - When a status changes: only through the claim's pre-registered test, on its stated split, after the study runs. - Exploratory results may be reported next to a claim, but cannot change its status. - Freezing the criteria: - The criteria below are the proposed decision rules. - They are copied verbatim into the v0.8 pre-registration and frozen there (sha256 recorded) before any training (stop point 3). - Any change before the freeze is recorded in the history table at the end. - Release freeze: - There is no v0.8.0 tag, PyPI upload or GitHub release until every claim has a pre-registered result and the user has approved the release. - Public text calls a claim "under test" until it is supported.

Shared definitions:

Term Meaning Arms A0–A5, A2o, A4K, A4F defined in plan §5 Success f(θ̂) − f* ≤ ε_abs + ε_rel·|f*| (plan §6), with ε fixed per family before F0 Units objective + gradient calls, all counted, fallback included. Objective and gradient calls are always reported separately for every arm, because one JAX/ODE gradient costs several objective calls; the measured gradient/objective cost ratio per family (F0 timing probe) is reported too. Matched budget B per family, fixed in the pre-registration from the F0 report (proposed: B = 2·c_local, rounded up to the F0 grid) Intervals paired over instances, percentile bootstrap, 95%, 10,000 resamples. Learned arms use ≥ 5 predictor training seeds: each instance's outcome is the mean over seeds; per-seed results and their spread are reported as well. Families each claim is decided per family/variant that passed F0 (1, 2a, 2b), with its criterion applied separately to each. The register lists one status per family. Cost-to-95% B95: the smallest budget on the F0 grid at which an arm reaches 95% success; its interval comes from a bootstrap of the success-versus-budget curve over instances Default split the in-distribution test split, opened once

items.title: C1. Basin landing
items.text:
• Wording: Learned start + L-BFGS reaches the reference optimum on more instances than default start + L-BFGS at the same budget.
  • Test: A4 versus A0 at budget B, owned L-BFGS in both.
  • Criterion (proposed): supported if the paired success-rate difference A4 − A0 has a 95% interval whose lower bound is > 0.
  • Not supported if the upper bound is ≤ 0.
  • Inconclusive otherwise.
  • Split: in-distribution test.
  • Status: unverified

items.title: C2. Cost versus multistart
items.text:
• Wording: At a matched success rate, learned start + L-BFGS uses fewer units and less wall time than multistart L-BFGS-B.
  • Test: A4 versus the better of SciPy multistart (A2) and owned multistart (A2o).
  • "Better" is decided separately on each axis: the lower B95 for units, the lower warm time for wall-clock.
  • The matched rate is 95% success. Compared: B95 in units, and warm wall time per instance at that budget.
  • Cold and batched times are reported as well. Objective and gradient calls are reported separately.
  • Criterion (proposed): supported only if it holds on both axes:
  • the 95% interval of B95_A4 / min(B95_A2, B95_A2o) lies entirely below 1;
  • the interval of warm time A4 / (the better arm's warm time) lies entirely below 1.
  • Not supported if A4 never reaches 95% within 800 units, or if either ratio's interval lies entirely above 1.
  • Otherwise inconclusive.
  • Split: in-distribution test.
  • Status: unverified

items.title: C3. The neural part earns its place
items.text:
• Wording: The learned start beats the nearest-neighbour warm start, on both success and cost.
  • Test: A4 versus A3, both refined with owned L-BFGS.
  • Criterion (proposed), a superiority claim: supported only if A4 is better than A3 on at least one axis (a paired interval excluding zero, in A4's favour) and non-inferior on the other.
  • Success axis:
    • better: the interval of the success difference A4 − A3 at B has lower bound > 0;
    • non-inferior: lower bound ≥ −0.02 (−2 percentage points).
  • Cost axis:
    • better: the interval of B95_A4 / B95_A3 has upper bound < 1;
    • non-inferior: upper bound ≤ 1.02. This is the −2 percentage-point margin expressed as a relative cost margin.
  • Not supported if neither axis shows A4 better (each interval includes zero or favours A3), or if A4 is inferior on either axis.
  • If not supported, this entry must state plainly: "a nearest-neighbour lookup does as well as (or better than) the learned start on this family."
  • Split: in-distribution test.
  • Status: unverified

items.title: C4. Break-even
items.text:
• Wording: The number of instances after which training plus target-solving cost is recovered.
  • Test: N* = T_offline / (t_generic − t_amortized).
  • T_offline is the measured wall time of:
    • simulating the training set;
    • solving all training targets (the reference multistart);
    • training, including compilation.
  • t is the mean warm time to success at the matched success rate of C2.
  • t_generic is the better of A2 and A2o; t_amortized is A4, with the g_φ forward pass included.
  • Batched and per-instance variants are both reported.
  • Criterion (proposed):
  • supported if t_generic − t_amortized > 0 with an interval whose lower bound is > 0. Then N* is reported with its interval and the measurement protocol: hardware, float64, timing method.
  • Not supported ("no break-even") if the interval's upper bound is ≤ 0.
  • Inconclusive otherwise.
  • Split: in-distribution test (timings); offline costs from the actual runs.
  • Status: unverified

items.title: C5. Safety: no silently missed optima
items.text:
• Wording: With the confidence check and fallback, the success rate is not worse than multistart L-BFGS-B.
  • Test: A4F (fallback included in its units) versus A2, at the larger of the two arms' B95 budgets.
  • Silent miss (definition): the fallback was not triggered, and the final fit is worse than the reference optimum by more than the success tolerance, i.e. f(θ̂) − f* > ε_abs + ε_rel·|f*|.
  • The silent-miss rate is the share of all instances that are silent misses.
  • Criterion (proposed): supported if both hold:
  • the interval of the success difference A4F − A2 has lower bound ≥ −0.01;
  • the silent-miss rate's interval has upper bound ≤ 0.01.
  • Not supported if either bound fails decisively: the success upper bound is < −0.01, or the silent-miss lower bound is > 0.01.
  • Otherwise inconclusive.
  • Split: in-distribution test; also reported on OOD (C8).
  • Status: unverified

items.title: C6. Informed versus random multistart
items.text:
• Wording: K informed starts beat K random multistarts at equal K and budget.
  • Test: A4K versus A2o at the same K and the same total units.
  • K = 4 is primary.
  • K = 1, 2 and 8 are exploratory: reported, but they do not decide the claim.
  • Criterion (proposed): supported if, at K = 4, the interval of the success difference A4K − A2o has lower bound > 0.
  • Not supported if the upper bound is ≤ 0. Otherwise inconclusive.
  • Split: in-distribution test.
  • Status: unverified

items.title: C7. Objective-based versus regression training (secondary)
items.text:
• Wording: Objective-based training beats regression on families with non-identifiable directions.
  • Test: A4 trained with the objective-based loss versus A4 trained with the regression loss: same architecture, data, seeds and budget.
  • Applies only to families/variants that F0's identifiability check marks as having non-identified directions (expected: 2b). Fisher-information conditioning above a pre-registered threshold, or flat profiles.
  • Criterion (proposed): supported if the success difference (objective − regression) at B has lower bound > 0.
  • Not supported if the upper bound is ≤ 0. Otherwise inconclusive.
  • If no family qualifies, the status is inconclusive (not applicable).
  • Split: in-distribution test.
  • Status: unverified

items.title: C8. Generalization and OOD detection
items.text:
• Wording: Performance on OOD splits is reported, and the confidence score flags OOD instances.
  • Test:
  • All arms on each OOD split (noise, parameter range, sampling times, dose), with the same metrics as the in-distribution test. This part is reported regardless of outcome.
  • The AUROC of 1 − confidence for separating OOD from in-distribution test instances.
  • The detection rate (the share of OOD instances below τ_c) at the validation-tuned threshold.
  • Criterion (proposed): supported if, on every OOD split:
  • part 1 is fully reported;
  • the AUROC interval has lower bound > 0.5;
  • the detection rate is reported.
  • Not supported if any split's AUROC upper bound is ≤ 0.5.
  • Otherwise inconclusive.
  • Split: the OOD test splits, plus the in-distribution test as the negative class.
  • Status: unverified

items.title: C9. Precision is not required
items.text:
• Wording: Basin landing does not require precise predictions. The relation between prediction error and success is reported.
  • Test:
  • Prediction error: the distance from the start to θ* in normalized log-parameter coordinates.
  • Reported: success as a function of error decile for A4, plus a logistic fit, with the NN start (A3) on the same axes.
  • Criterion (proposed): supported if the success rate in A4's highest prediction-error quartile is ≥ 0.8 × A4's overall success rate, with the interval of the ratio having lower bound ≥ 0.8.
  • Not supported if the ratio interval's upper bound is < 0.8.
  • Otherwise inconclusive.
  • Split: in-distribution test.
  • Status: unverified

items.title: C10. The forward pass is cheap
items.text:
• Wording: The forward pass costs negligible time compared with refinement.
  • Test: warm and cold g_φ time versus the warm and cold owned-L-BFGS refinement time per instance, single and batched, measured in the same process.
  • Criterion (proposed): supported if the warm ratio (forward / refinement) has an interval whose upper bound is < 0.05.
  • Cold times (first call, compilation included) are reported for both the forward pass and the refinement, single and batched, but do not decide the claim.
  • Not supported if the warm ratio's lower bound is > 0.05. Otherwise inconclusive.
  • Split: in-distribution test.
  • Status: unverified

items.title: Track v0.8-B: learned step policy in its plausible regime
items.text:
These two claims belong to the parallel track v0.8-B (plan §15). It has its own pre-registration, frozen before any v0.8-B training, and no implementation starts until the user approves its plan. Families: - Rastrigin, Ackley and shifted Rosenbrock (the task_families generators); - Family 1; - Family 2b.

Budgets are ≤ 100 units, with a pre-registered grid (proposed {20, 50, 100}). Baselines are matched on units (objective and gradient calls reported separately) and, separately, on warm wall-clock: - owned multistart L-BFGS; - SciPy multistart L-BFGS-B; - CMA-ES; - TPE; - BB (the compiled loop's BB step); - quasi-random search (scrambled Sobol points).

Each baseline is tuned on validation only.

items.title: C11. Anytime regret
items.text:
• Wording: The learned step policy beats all baselines on anytime regret on multimodal families at budgets ≤ 100.
  • Test:
  • Anytime regret (v0.8-B plan §5.1): AUC_i(B) = (1/B) Σ_{t=1..B} log10(min(max(f_best(t) − f*, τ_i), 10·s_i) / s_i), where τ_i is the success tolerance (floor) and s_i is the median regret of 64 fixed Sobol points (normalization). It is 1 before the first value.
  • Budgets: B ∈ {20, 50, 100} units.
  • Comparison: the policy (≥ 5 training seeds) is paired over instances against each baseline.
  • Criterion (proposed): supported for a family only if, at every budget, the two-sided 95% interval of the policy-minus-baseline difference lies entirely below zero for every baseline. The comparison is made under unit matching and under warm wall-clock matching (v0.8-B plan §4).
  • This is an intersection-union test: all 36 comparisons (6 baselines × 3 budgets × 2 matchings) must hold, so the family-level error is at most each comparison's.
  • The interval is a two-level bootstrap over seeds and instances.
  • Any claim made jointly across families needs Holm–Bonferroni over those families (v0.8-B plan §6). Per-family statuses get no correction.
  • Not supported if any baseline is better (interval entirely above zero) at any budget.
  • Otherwise inconclusive.
  • Split: in-distribution test of each family; OOD reported (C8 conventions).
  • Status: unverified

items.title: C12. Probability of reaching the global basin
items.text:
• Wording: The learned step policy reaches the global basin with higher probability than the baselines.
  • Test:
  • "Reached the global basin" (v0.8-B plan §5.2): a measurement-only polish (owned L-BFGS, ≤ 2,000 units, gtol 1e-8, uncharged) started from the best-so-far point converges to within the success tolerance of the global optimum f*.
    • The global optimum is known for Rastrigin, Ackley and shifted Rosenbrock, and is the reference optimum for Families 1 and 2b.
    • The polish is not charged to the arm.
  • The rate is compared at each pre-registered budget, against each baseline.
  • Criterion (proposed): supported for a family only if, at every budget (B ∈ {20, 50, 100}), the two-sided 95% interval of the paired difference in global-basin rate (policy − baseline) has lower bound > 0 for every baseline, under both unit and wall-clock matching. The statistics are the same as for C11.
  • Not supported if any baseline is better (upper bound < 0) at any budget.
  • Otherwise inconclusive.
  • Split: in-distribution test of each family; OOD reported.
  • Status: unverified

items.title: 1. Sources and decisions
items.text:
• Plan: docs/plans/neuralopt-v08-amortized-families.md, §§2–11.
  • Claims register: docs/research/v0.8-claims.md (C1–C10; the criteria are copied in §8 below, with the amendments the user approved).
  • Gate F0:
  • results/f0-v0.8.0.json and the report docs/research/f0-v0.8.md;
  • per-instance validation data, results/f0-instances-v0.8.0.json, which reproduces the frozen F0 aggregates;
  • the pinned-thread probe re-time, results/f0-probe-pinned-v0.8.0.json.
  • User decisions after F0 (2026-11-22):
  • The default start (A0) is a required bar for every cost claim, next to the nearest-neighbour lookup (A3) and the better multistart arm.
  • Per-family expectations are stated before training (§3). A win on one family is never summarized as a general result; the joint-claim rule (§7) applies.
  • Compute:
    • one thread per process, pinned with taskset;
    • XLA intra-op threads 1; OMP_NUM_THREADS, OPENBLAS_NUM_THREADS and MKL_NUM_THREADS set to 1;
    • the settings are recorded in every command.txt;
    • parallelism comes from separate processes;
    • every cap names its clock and is stated per run and in total (§10).
  • SciPy fairness: SciPy arms run with tolerances that let them use the full budget (ftol = gtol = 0, maxfun = budget/2). Default-tolerance runs are extra context only.
  • Power: checked with F0's validation spreads per family and claim (§9). Test sizes are raised where needed; criteria are never loosened.

items.title: 3. Per-family expectations (stated before any training)
items.text:
Family Role Primary claims Expectation stated in advance 1 primary test of the learned start C1, C3, C6 Headroom is large: no generic arm reached 95% success within 800 units. The nearest-neighbour lookup is the bar to beat (57% at 50 units; it levels off at 74.5%). 2a control C5 Little headroom: the default start reaches 95% success at 100 units. "No harm" (C5) is the expected main finding. C1–C4 are not expected to show an advantage, and a null result there is the expected outcome, not a failure. 2b cost test C2; C7 (the only family flagged for non-identifiability) Every arm needed 800 units for 95% success. 28% of validation instances are not identifiable (Fisher condition > 1e6). Parameter error is reported only alongside the identifiability check. Success is measured on the objective.
  • Every claim is still evaluated and reported on every family that passed F0, and each gets its own per-family status in the register.
  • The expectations above set which result is the headline for each family. They do not change any criterion.

items.title: 4. Arms (frozen settings)
items.text:
All arms share the same instances, float64, CPU, the counted unit budget (objective + gradient calls; objective and gradient reported separately) and the success tolerance f − f* ≤ 1e-6 + 1e-3·|f*|.

Arm Frozen setting A0 family default start; owned L-BFGS (neuralopt.lbfgs, memory 10, gtol 1e-8, Armijo c1 1e-4, shrink 0.5) A1 family default start; SciPy L-BFGS-B with ftol = gtol = 0, maxfun = budget/2, maxcor 10 (2 units per call) A2 SciPy multistart, same SciPy settings; starts are scrambled Sobol (seed 3); K per budget chosen on validation from {2, 4, 8, 16} (§9 lists the chosen K) A2o owned multistart; same starts; K chosen on validation from A3 nearest-neighbour start (F0's features: observations interpolated to a common grid per species, standardized with training statistics, dose appended; labels from owned multistart, 16 starts × 1,000 units); owned L-BFGS A4 the learned start g_φ (§5): the highest-confidence candidate; owned L-BFGS A4K the top-K candidates by confidence, budget split equally across starts; owned L-BFGS. K = 4 is primary; 1, 2 and 8 are exploratory A4F A4 plus fallback to A2o (K = 2, the rest of the budget) when the confidence is below τ_c or the refined fit fails the fit check; fallback units count A5 A4's start with SciPy refinement (harness only; separates start from refinement)
  • Default-tolerance SciPy (A1 and A2 with SciPy's defaults) is run and reported as context only. It decides nothing.
  • Reference optimum f*:
  • F0's protocol: SciPy L-BFGS-B multistart, 64 Sobol starts plus the truth, two seeds, 2,000 units each, ftol 1e-15 and gtol 1e-10.
  • It is updated, and the update reported, whenever any arm finds a lower value beyond tolerance.
  • Two-seed reproduction is reported. If it falls below 99% on a split, the reference budget is doubled for that split before any claim is evaluated.

items.title: 5. The start predictor g_φ and its training (frozen)
items.text:
• Input: each observation is a token (t/10, standardized y, species one-hot, log σ, dose), where y is standardized with training-split statistics per species. Padding is masked.
  • Encoder:
  • a linear embedding to width 64;
  • 2 transformer blocks with 4 heads, masked self-attention and pre-layer-norm, GELU MLP of width 128;
  • masked mean pooling concatenated with attention pooling (one learned query).
  • Heads:
  • K = 8 candidates: a 2-layer MLP (width 128) outputs 8 × 4 values. Each is mapped into the optimization box by lo + (hi − lo)·(tanh(·) + 1)/2. The box is in the family's own coordinates: log parameters for the cascades.
  • Confidence: for each candidate, a 2-layer MLP (width 64) on the pooled embedding and the candidate gives a probability that owned L-BFGS from that candidate reaches success within B.
  • Losses (two candidate heads, compared in C7):
  • (R) regression: best-of-K squared error to the training-target optimum in box-normalized coordinates, min_k ‖u(θ̂_k) − u(θ*)‖².
  • (O) objective-based: best-of-K objective, min_k f(θ̂_k; c) / f_scale, with no unrolled steps (k = 0). f_scale is the training-split median of f*.
  • Training targets: owned multistart, 16 starts × 1,000 units (the F0 label procedure; label adequacy was 100% on validation in every family).
  • Optimizer:
  • Adam (optax), learning rate 1e-3, cosine-decayed to 1e-5 over 10,000 steps;
  • batch 64 training instances; gradient-norm clip 1.0; float64.
  • Validation loss is checked every 500 steps, and the best checkpoint is kept.
  • Confidence head (stage 2):
  • The candidate heads are frozen.
  • Each training instance's 8 candidates are refined with owned L-BFGS at budget B, giving success labels.
  • The confidence MLP is trained with binary cross-entropy: Adam 1e-3, 2,000 steps, batch 256.
  • Diversity check: the median pairwise box-normalized distance between candidates on validation is reported. Below 0.05 is reported as "collapsed". This changes nothing.
  • Seeds: 5 training seeds (0–4) per family and loss. Each instance's outcome is the mean over seeds; per-seed results and their spread are reported.
  • Validation-only choices, each made per family before the test is opened:
  • A4's loss: (R) or (O), whichever has the higher validation success at B; ties go to (R).
  • Fit check: f(θ̂*) ≤ τ_fit, where τ_fit is the 99th percentile of the reference optimum f* over validation instances.
  • Confidence threshold: τ_c is the smallest threshold for which A4F's validation silent-miss rate is ≤ 0.005 (half the C5 margin). Ties go to the lower fallback rate.
  • Checkpoints: schema neuralopt-start/v0.8-v1, which fails closed. Earlier schemas are untouched.

items.title: 6. Metrics
items.text:
• Success, units and calls: as defined in the register's shared definitions. Objective and gradient calls are reported separately for every arm, along with the pinned-probe gradient/objective cost ratio.
  • B95: the smallest budget on the grid {25, 50, 100, 200, 400, 800} at which an arm reaches 95% success. Its interval comes from bootstrapping the success-versus-budget curve over instances.
  • Wall time:
  • warm, per instance, measured one instance at a time after compilation, on pinned single-thread processes on the same machine;
  • cold time (with compilation) and batched time are reported separately.
  • g_φ time is included in A4's warm time.
  • Parameter error: only on instances that the identifiability check (Fisher condition ≤ 1e6 at θ*) marks as identified. Non-identified instances are counted.

items.title: 7. Statistics and the joint-claim rule
items.text:
• Intervals:
  • paired over test instances, percentile bootstrap, 95% two-sided, 10,000 resamples, bootstrap seed 0;
  • learned arms: instance outcomes are seed means, and seeds are resampled with instances (two-level bootstrap).
  • Per-family decisions: each claim's criterion (§8) is applied separately per family. The register records one status per family. Within a family, claims that require several conditions (C2, C3, C4, C5) are intersection-union tests: every condition must hold, and no further correction is applied.
  • Joint claims across families:
  • Any statement made jointly about several families, such as "the learned start helps on the families tested", "on k of 3 families" or a pooled number, uses Holm–Bonferroni over the families it covers, at a family-wise one-sided level of 2.5%.
  • Each family's p-value is the largest one-sided bootstrap p-value among the conditions of its criterion.
  • Without that correction, results are reported side by side, and no general claim is made from a single family's win.

items.title: 8. Criteria (copied from the register; amendments marked [amended])
8.1 Amendments (decided by the user after F0; they apply where they differ from §8.2)
items.text:
• C2 [amended, decision 1]: supported only if, on both axes, A4 beats each required bar:
  • the bars are A0, A3, and the better of A2 and A2o (chosen per axis);
  • on units: the 95% interval of B95_A4 / B95_bar lies entirely below 1;
  • on wall time: the 95% interval of warm time A4 / warm time of the bar lies entirely below 1.
  • Not supported if A4 never reaches 95% within 800 units, or if any ratio's interval lies entirely above 1.
  • Otherwise inconclusive.
  • C4 [amended, decision 1]: N* is computed against each bar, with each bar's own offline cost:
  • A0: none;
  • better multistart: none;
  • A3: its label and index cost, so N* versus A3 uses the incremental offline cost.
  • Supported only if t_bar − t_A4 > 0, with an interval lower bound > 0, for every bar.
  • Not supported ("no break-even") if any bar's interval upper bound is ≤ 0.
  • Otherwise inconclusive.
  • C3: the cost axis already compares against A3. A0 is added as a reported reference on that axis; it is not part of C3's criterion, because C2 now carries the A0 bar.
  • C5: the comparator A2 runs with the full-budget SciPy settings (decision 4).
  • C5 silent-miss bound [amended at freeze; stricter than the register, so it loosens nothing]: the silent-miss rate's 95% upper bound is the exact Clopper–Pearson bound, not a percentile bootstrap. A bootstrap of a rate near zero degenerates: zero observed misses give [0, 0] at any sample size.
  • The user may revert this, by a dated amendment, before any training.
  • Matched budget B is fixed per family as in §2. Every other criterion is unchanged.

items.title: 8.2 Register text at the freeze (verbatim, C1–C10)
C1. Basin landing
items.text:
• Wording: Learned start + L-BFGS reaches the reference optimum on more instances than default start + L-BFGS at the same budget.
  • Test: A4 versus A0 at budget B, owned L-BFGS in both.
  • Criterion (proposed): supported if the paired success-rate difference A4 − A0 has a 95% interval whose lower bound is > 0.
  • Not supported if the upper bound is ≤ 0.
  • Inconclusive otherwise.
  • Split: in-distribution test.
  • Status: unverified

items.title: C2. Cost versus multistart
items.text:
• Wording: At a matched success rate, learned start + L-BFGS uses fewer units and less wall time than multistart L-BFGS-B.
  • Test: A4 versus the better of SciPy multistart (A2) and owned multistart (A2o).
  • "Better" is decided separately on each axis: the lower B95 for units, the lower warm time for wall-clock.
  • The matched rate is 95% success. Compared: B95 in units, and warm wall time per instance at that budget.
  • Cold and batched times are reported as well. Objective and gradient calls are reported separately.
  • Criterion (proposed): supported only if it holds on both axes:
  • the 95% interval of B95_A4 / min(B95_A2, B95_A2o) lies entirely below 1;
  • the interval of warm time A4 / (the better arm's warm time) lies entirely below 1.
  • Not supported if A4 never reaches 95% within 800 units, or if either ratio's interval lies entirely above 1.
  • Otherwise inconclusive.
  • Split: in-distribution test.
  • Status: unverified

items.title: C3. The neural part earns its place
items.text:
• Wording: The learned start beats the nearest-neighbour warm start, on both success and cost.
  • Test: A4 versus A3, both refined with owned L-BFGS.
  • Criterion (proposed), a superiority claim: supported only if A4 is better than A3 on at least one axis (a paired interval excluding zero, in A4's favour) and non-inferior on the other.
  • Success axis:
    • better: the interval of the success difference A4 − A3 at B has lower bound > 0;
    • non-inferior: lower bound ≥ −0.02 (−2 percentage points).
  • Cost axis:
    • better: the interval of B95_A4 / B95_A3 has upper bound < 1;
    • non-inferior: upper bound ≤ 1.02. This is the −2 percentage-point margin expressed as a relative cost margin.
  • Not supported if neither axis shows A4 better (each interval includes zero or favours A3), or if A4 is inferior on either axis.
  • If not supported, this entry must state plainly: "a nearest-neighbour lookup does as well as (or better than) the learned start on this family."
  • Split: in-distribution test.
  • Status: unverified

items.title: C4. Break-even
items.text:
• Wording: The number of instances after which training plus target-solving cost is recovered.
  • Test: N* = T_offline / (t_generic − t_amortized).
  • T_offline is the measured wall time of:
    • simulating the training set;
    • solving all training targets (the reference multistart);
    • training, including compilation.
  • t is the mean warm time to success at the matched success rate of C2.
  • t_generic is the better of A2 and A2o; t_amortized is A4, with the g_φ forward pass included.
  • Batched and per-instance variants are both reported.
  • Criterion (proposed):
  • supported if t_generic − t_amortized > 0 with an interval whose lower bound is > 0. Then N* is reported with its interval and the measurement protocol: hardware, float64, timing method.
  • Not supported ("no break-even") if the interval's upper bound is ≤ 0.
  • Inconclusive otherwise.
  • Split: in-distribution test (timings); offline costs from the actual runs.
  • Status: unverified

items.title: C5. Safety: no silently missed optima
items.text:
• Wording: With the confidence check and fallback, the success rate is not worse than multistart L-BFGS-B.
  • Test: A4F (fallback included in its units) versus A2, at the larger of the two arms' B95 budgets.
  • Silent miss (definition): the fallback was not triggered, and the final fit is worse than the reference optimum by more than the success tolerance, i.e. f(θ̂) − f* > ε_abs + ε_rel·|f*|.
  • The silent-miss rate is the share of all instances that are silent misses.
  • Criterion (proposed): supported if both hold:
  • the interval of the success difference A4F − A2 has lower bound ≥ −0.01;
  • the silent-miss rate's interval has upper bound ≤ 0.01.
  • Not supported if either bound fails decisively: the success upper bound is < −0.01, or the silent-miss lower bound is > 0.01.
  • Otherwise inconclusive.
  • Split: in-distribution test; also reported on OOD (C8).
  • Status: unverified

items.title: C6. Informed versus random multistart
items.text:
• Wording: K informed starts beat K random multistarts at equal K and budget.
  • Test: A4K versus A2o at the same K and the same total units.
  • K = 4 is primary.
  • K = 1, 2 and 8 are exploratory: reported, but they do not decide the claim.
  • Criterion (proposed): supported if, at K = 4, the interval of the success difference A4K − A2o has lower bound > 0.
  • Not supported if the upper bound is ≤ 0. Otherwise inconclusive.
  • Split: in-distribution test.
  • Status: unverified

items.title: C7. Objective-based versus regression training (secondary)
items.text:
• Wording: Objective-based training beats regression on families with non-identifiable directions.
  • Test: A4 trained with the objective-based loss versus A4 trained with the regression loss: same architecture, data, seeds and budget.
  • Applies only to families/variants that F0's identifiability check marks as having non-identified directions (expected: 2b). Fisher-information conditioning above a pre-registered threshold, or flat profiles.
  • Criterion (proposed): supported if the success difference (objective − regression) at B has lower bound > 0.
  • Not supported if the upper bound is ≤ 0. Otherwise inconclusive.
  • If no family qualifies, the status is inconclusive (not applicable).
  • Split: in-distribution test.
  • Status: unverified

items.title: C8. Generalization and OOD detection
items.text:
• Wording: Performance on OOD splits is reported, and the confidence score flags OOD instances.
  • Test:
  • All arms on each OOD split (noise, parameter range, sampling times, dose), with the same metrics as the in-distribution test. This part is reported regardless of outcome.
  • The AUROC of 1 − confidence for separating OOD from in-distribution test instances.
  • The detection rate (the share of OOD instances below τ_c) at the validation-tuned threshold.
  • Criterion (proposed): supported if, on every OOD split:
  • part 1 is fully reported;
  • the AUROC interval has lower bound > 0.5;
  • the detection rate is reported.
  • Not supported if any split's AUROC upper bound is ≤ 0.5.
  • Otherwise inconclusive.
  • Split: the OOD test splits, plus the in-distribution test as the negative class.
  • Status: unverified

items.title: C9. Precision is not required
items.text:
• Wording: Basin landing does not require precise predictions. The relation between prediction error and success is reported.
  • Test:
  • Prediction error: the distance from the start to θ* in normalized log-parameter coordinates.
  • Reported: success as a function of error decile for A4, plus a logistic fit, with the NN start (A3) on the same axes.
  • Criterion (proposed): supported if the success rate in A4's highest prediction-error quartile is ≥ 0.8 × A4's overall success rate, with the interval of the ratio having lower bound ≥ 0.8.
  • Not supported if the ratio interval's upper bound is < 0.8.
  • Otherwise inconclusive.
  • Split: in-distribution test.
  • Status: unverified

items.title: C10. The forward pass is cheap
items.text:
• Wording: The forward pass costs negligible time compared with refinement.
  • Test: warm and cold g_φ time versus the warm and cold owned-L-BFGS refinement time per instance, single and batched, measured in the same process.
  • Criterion (proposed): supported if the warm ratio (forward / refinement) has an interval whose upper bound is < 0.05.
  • Cold times (first call, compilation included) are reported for both the forward pass and the refinement, single and batched, but do not decide the claim.
  • Not supported if the warm ratio's lower bound is > 0.05. Otherwise inconclusive.
  • Split: in-distribution test.
  • Status: unverified

items.title: 9. Power check (F0 validation spreads)
items.text:
Data: - results/f0-instances-v0.8.0.json: F0 recomputed per instance with the unchanged F0 harness, under pinned single threads. It reproduces every frozen F0 success rate exactly, for all arms and families. - results/power-v0.8.0.json: written by scripts/power_v0_8.py.

Rule: - Each comparison is powered at 80% at the two-sided 95% level for its effect: n = ((z_0.975 + z_0.8)·SD/δ)². - SD is the validation spread of the paired difference between two real start strategies at the family's matched budget B: - C1, C3 and C7: A3 − A0; - C6: A3 − A2o (K = 4); - C5: A0 − A2 (full-budget SciPy). - No learned arm exists yet. A paired binary difference with true mean δ has a spread of at least sqrt(δ(1 − δ)), so the proxy SD is floored there. - Effects: - superiority: 5 percentage points (C1, C3-success, C6, C7); - the criteria's own margins at a true difference of 0: C3 non-inferiority 2 points; C5 success 1 point; - C5's silent-miss bound: the exact Clopper–Pearson upper bound ≤ 1%, at an assumed true rate of 0.25%. This is half the validation target that sets τ_c. - Test size per family: the largest requirement among the family's primary claims (§3), rounded up to 100, with a minimum of 200. Secondary claims are reported with the power they have at that size.

Required test instances (bold: primary for that family):

Claim (effect) Family 1 (SD) Family 2a (SD) Family 2b (SD) C1 (5 points) 1,119 (0.60) 150 (0.22, floor) 204 (0.25) C3 success, non-inferiority (2 points) 6,989 (0.60) 385 (0.14, floor) 1,270 (0.25) C6 (5 points) 1,007 (0.57) 150 (0.22) 330 (0.32) C7 (5 points) 1,119 150 204 C5 success, non-inferiority (1 point) 31,073 (0.63) 1,166 (0.12) 1,182 (0.12) C5 silent miss (Clopper–Pearson ≤ 1%; true rate 0.1% / 0.25% / 0.5%) 600 / 900 / 2,500 600 / 900 / 2,500 600 / 900 / 2,500 C9 (ratio ≥ 0.8; A3's success rate as proxy) 272 4 40 C8 (AUROC; 200 OOD vs test) detects AUROC ≥ 0.58 same same Frozen test size 7,000 1,200 300

Claims powered by stability rather than instance count: - C2 and the C3 cost axis (B95 ratios on the grid): a bootstrap of the bars' B95 on validation (n = 200). - Family 1: no bar reaches 95% within 800 units, so the cost axis can be "better" only if A4 reaches 95% within 800. - Family 2a: A0's B95 is 100 in 58% of resamples (otherwise 200). A3's is stable at 200 and A2o's at 400. - Family 2b: A0's and A3's B95 flip between 400, 800 and "none" (55% at 800), because A0 sits at 94.5% success at 400 units. The units axis of C2 on Family 2b may stay inconclusive at any test size. This is a property of the B95 statistic at the 95% threshold. The criterion is not changed. - C4 and C10: timing ratios from per-instance warm times, which have small relative noise. They are not powered by instance count.

Frozen test split hashes (sha256 at the frozen sizes; the first 200 instances are identical to F0's manifest): - Family 1, 7,000 instances: e9491fa8ce0c60005f1afd5ed21c954d24448c5ac504a3b58430001163635bb9 - Family 2a, 1,200 instances: 426fe2eec2c84dea04d446d8a986db28f423a8fd88dd933ed954e26553844db4 - Family 2b, 300 instances: 46a097548a250093a52a1dba3a16f7f5564f10430e97bd604286bd291b65e2be

Caveats: - The proxies stand in for a learned arm that does not exist yet. - If the learned start behaves like the lookup (A3), Family 1's spread is well estimated. - If it is closer to A0, the spread is smaller and the test is over-powered. That is conservative.

items.title: 10. Compute (pinned threads; clocks named)
items.text:
Clock and pinning: - All caps are on the process-CPU clock (time.process_time, summed over a run's processes). - Every process is pinned to one core with taskset, with every thread count set to 1 (§1). So CPU time ≤ wall time per process, and parallelism comes only from separate processes. - The settings, the CPU affinity and the cap are written to each run's command.txt.

Re-timed probe: results/f0-probe-pinned-v0.8.0.json, pinned threads. - Per-call timings match the original probe within about 10%. - Gradient/objective cost ratios: 2.5 (Family 1), 10.8 (2a), 11.0 (2b). - F0 is projected at 2.63 CPU-h, versus 2.57 multi-threaded. - The F0 per-instance extraction (pinned) actually took 0.11, 0.57 and 0.67 CPU-h.

Estimate (from the extraction's per-instance cost, all-in: references and arms A0–A3, both SciPy settings):

Work Family 1 Family 2a Family 2b Test: references + generic arms 7,000 × 2.1 s ≈ 4.0 h 1,200 × 10.2 s ≈ 3.4 h 300 × 12.0 s ≈ 1.0 h OOD splits (3 or 4 × 200): references + generic arms ≈ 0.4 h ≈ 2.3 h ≈ 2.7 h Training: 2 losses × 5 seeds (candidates, labels, confidence) ≈ 0.5 h ≈ 2.8 h ≈ 3.2 h Learned arms on test and OOD (5 seeds; A4, A4K, A4F, A5) ≈ 0.5 h ≈ 1.0 h ≈ 0.7 h

Total ≈ 22 CPU-h.

Caps (process CPU):

Scope Cap Any single process 3 CPU-h; test and OOD instances are split across processes Training, all families 10 CPU-h Evaluation, all families 20 CPU-h Study total 30 CPU-h
  • If a projection made before a stage exceeds its cap, the work stops and is reported before it runs.
  • Seeds and test sizes are never reduced to fit a cap.
  • All runs follow CLAUDE.md rule 9: tmux, a run directory, HANDOFF.md.

items.title: 11. Outcome reporting
items.text:
• Every claim gets a per-family status: supported, not supported, inconclusive, or "not tested (reason)". Each status comes with its intervals and the numbers behind them.
  • A family's results are reported against its §3 expectation. A null result on Family 2a is the expected outcome.
  • If C3 is not supported on a family, the register states: "a nearest-neighbour lookup does as well as (or better than) the learned start on this family."
  • Negative results, cost regressions and failed checks are reported as findings.

items.title: Trajectory-curvature v0.6 Implementation Plan
items.text:
For agentic workers: REQUIRED SUB-SKILL: Use superpowers:executing-plans to implement this plan task-by-task. Steps use checkbox (- [ ]) syntax for tracking.

Goal: Opt-in masked secant-history features, a shared preconditioned evaluation loop, history meta-training, and a pre-registered matched-budget ablation against tuned fixed geometry.

Architecture: New trajectory.py (history PyTree + features); ModelConfig gains a versioned feature schema; minimize gains candidate_method="preconditioned"; training.py gains history_regret_loss and checkpoint schema; one experiment script produces versioned artifacts and results.

Tech Stack: JAX 0.12 CPU, Optax, NumPy, SciPy (harness only), pytest, uv.

Spec: docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-21-trajectory-curvature-v06-design.md

items.title: Global Constraints
items.text:
• Legacy defaults (feature_set="legacy", existing candidate methods) produce outputs identical to the pre-change golden snapshot (rtol 1e-6).
  • No new keys in legacy checkpoint files; unknown schema raises ValueError.
  • No classical optimizer in src/neuralopt; BB and L-BFGS live only in scripts/.
  • History entries only from states with objective and gradient evaluated at that exact point.
  • Never write results/*v0.5* or existing artifacts/*.npz.
  • No commits/pushes unless the user asks.

items.title: Review Focus
items.text:
• Problem with all candidates rejected (flat/plateau): loop must terminate within budget, history stays one entry, no NaN features.
  • Candidate clipped to the box: secant uses the clipped (evaluated) point.
  • Explicit NumPy gradient callables: counts must match actual calls.
  • Objective returning NaN/inf at a candidate: rejected, never pushed.
  • Dimension 1 problems: features and effective-rank finite.

items.title: NeuralOpt v0.6 — trajectory-aware curvature: design and pre-registration
items.text: Status: frozen before any v0.6 training or evaluation (2026-11-21). Changes after results are seen must be listed in a dated "deviations" section of the results report, never silently edited here.
path: NeuralOpt v0.6 — trajectory-aware curvature: design and pre-registration

items.title: Question and why
items.text: v0.5 found learned stochastic geometry worse than a validation-tuned fixed scalar geometry on unseen dimensions, and diagnosed missing information: one gradient cannot identify rotated curvature. v0.6 asks whether a small variable-dimensional policy that sees 4–8 secant pairs (s, y) from actually evaluated states produces geometry that beats the tuned fixed baseline on unseen rotated / ill-conditioned objectives, under exactly matched objective+gradient counts, with runtime and training cost reported.
path: NeuralOpt v0.6 — trajectory-aware curvature: design and pre-registration

items.title: Goals / non-goals / anti-goals
items.text:
• Goal: an opt-in, versioned history feature schema and a shared deterministic evaluation loop; a pre-registered multi-seed ablation; an honest report.
  • Non-goals (this round): temporal attention over pairs, stochastic mass/mobility with history (G5), function-space or certification injection (G6), HVP probes.
  • Anti-goals: any change to legacy outputs or checkpoint loading; classical solvers in package inference; uncounted evaluations; tuning on final test tasks; claims beyond the measured evidence.
path: NeuralOpt v0.6 — trajectory-aware curvature: design and pre-registration

items.title: Approaches considered (direct-mode arena)
items.text:
• A (chosen by user): new opt-in loop candidate_method="preconditioned" shared by every arm, fixed baseline = same loop with scalar geometry, references in harness.
  • B: legacy direct loop + history features — rejected: proposal head consumes half the evaluations and rejected steps are re-proposed almost identically (v0.2 diagnosis).
  • C: stochastic arena first — rejected: contradicts "stochastic only after gates".
path: NeuralOpt v0.6 — trajectory-aware curvature: design and pre-registration

items.title: Mathematics (normalized box coordinates)
items.text: u = 2(x-lo)/(hi-lo) - 1, J = diag((hi-lo)/2), g_u = J g_x, H_u = J H_x J. For consecutive history entries k, k+1 (both actually evaluated with objective and gradient at the same point): s_k = u_{k+1}-u_k, y_k = g_{u,k+1}-g_{u,k}; on a quadratic y_k = H_u s_k exactly (up to rounding), whatever produced s_k. K pairs identify H_u only on span(S) (rank ≤ min(K, d)); two Hessians that agree on span(S) give identical histories, so no full-Hessian recovery is claimed. The geometry P = diag(d) + U Uᵀ (rank 2) stays SPD; it acts as an inverse metric (ideal P y ≈ s), cannot represent indefinite curvature, and cannot equal H_u⁻¹ for rotated Hessians in d > 3. Negative sᵀy is kept as a feature, never inverted.
path: NeuralOpt v0.6 — trajectory-aware curvature: design and pre-registration

items.title: History state (src/neuralopt/trajectory.py)
items.text:
TrajectoryHistory(u: (K+1,d), g: (K+1,d), f: (K+1,), valid: (K+1,) bool, rejections: ()) — shift buffer, index K newest, explicit chronological order, O(Kd). Entries are pushed only for accepted, evaluated states (start point included). Rejected candidates increment rejections; they have no gradient and never form pairs.

Pair mask m_k = valid_k ∧ valid_{k+1} ∧ finite(s_k,y_k) ∧ ‖s_k‖∞ > 1e-7 ∧ ‖y_k‖ > 1e-6·max(‖g_k‖,‖g_{k+1}‖) (degenerate / roundoff-level pairs are masked).
path: NeuralOpt v0.6 — trajectory-aware curvature: design and pre-registration

items.title: Feature schema history-v1 (17 per coordinate token)
items.text:
Legacy five (parameter_features(..., scale_aware=True)) followed by twelve history features. With c_k = s_kᵀy_k, σ_k = s_kᵀs_k, R_k = c_k/σ_k, cos_k = c_k/(‖s_k‖‖y_k‖), n = Σm_k, self-scaling ρ = Σ m|c_k| / Σ mσ_k:

# feature kind 6 asinh(a_i/ρ)/4, a_i = Σ m s_ki y_ki / (Σ m s_ki² + 1e-12 Σ mσ_k) (diagonal secant curvature, signed) coord 7 newest valid s_i/‖s‖ coord 8 newest valid y_i/‖y‖ coord 9 tanh(log(‖g_u‖/ρ)/4) (log Newton step length in u units) global 10 fraction of valid pairs with c_k < 0 global 11 n / K global 12 mean valid |cos_k| (reliability / conditioning) global 13 tanh(log(max|R_k| / min|R_k|)/4), 0 if n < 2 global 14 effective rank of normalized valid S divided by K global 15 1[n > 0] global 16 tanh(rejections/4) global 17 tanh(mean_k m_k clip(Δf_k / (½(g_k+g_{k+1})ᵀs_k) - 1, ±10)) (quadratic-model consistency, 0 on quadratics) global

Features 6–10, 12–14, 17 are exactly zero when n = 0, with 11 and 15 as explicit masks. All are invariant to objective scaling and to box rescaling, and coordinate-permutation equivariant (globals invariant). K = 0 gives the matched no-history control with identical width and parameter count.

items.title: Model and checkpoint schema
items.text: ModelConfig gains feature_set: "legacy" | "history-v1" = "legacy" and history_length: int = 0 (must be 0 for legacy) and property input_features (5 or 17). Init uses input_features for embed / MLP hidden. Legacy configs save byte-compatible files (no new keys). Non-legacy configs add key schema = "neuralopt-policy/v0.6-history-v1" and two extra config entries; loading an unknown schema raises. _validate_policy_params checks the embedding input width.
path: NeuralOpt v0.6 — trajectory-aware curvature: design and pre-registration

items.title: Shared evaluation loop (candidate_method="preconditioned")
items.text: State: accepted x, its f, g_x (each evaluated once), shrink σ=1, history. Each iteration: ĝ = g_u/‖g_u‖; geometry P = learned (model, structure flag honoured), fixed (fixed_metric_diag, U=0) or identity; step L = 0.5·step_head (learned) or preconditioned_step (non-learned, required). Candidate u' = clip(u − σ L P ĝ, −1, 1); one objective call; accept iff finite and f' < f, then one gradient call, push history, σ=1; else σ ← σ/2, rejections += 1. Budget counts objective plus gradient calls (start point costs 2); iterate while used + 2 ≤ budget. HVP count is 0 and reported. The direction head is unused (P SPD ⇒ descent). Legacy loops are untouched; stochastic methods reject history configs.
path: NeuralOpt v0.6 — trajectory-aware curvature: design and pre-registration

items.title: Meta-training (objective="history")
items.text: history_regret_loss mirrors the loop in lax.scan (T = 24, hard acceptance via where, gradient at the candidate computed for training only). Loss mean_h log(r_h + 1e-6) + 0.1·mean_t log(r^cand_t + 1e-6) with r = max(f − f*, 0)/(|f₀ − f*| + 1e-12), horizons (6, 12, 24), features stop_gradiented (history is treated as observed data), random start in the box, Adam 1e-3, global-norm clip 1.0. Identical for every trained arm.
path: NeuralOpt v0.6 — trajectory-aware curvature: design and pre-registration

items.title: Pre-registered protocol
items.text:
• Tasks (generator scaled_task copied from v0.5, objective scale cycle 0.2/1/5, coordinate scale 0.5/1/2): train families isotropic, diagonal κ∈{10,100,1000}, rotated κ∈{10,100}, rastrigin; dims 2/4/8; seeds 1000+ (one per variant×dim, 21 tasks). Validation: same variants, dims 3/6, seeds 2000+ (14 tasks). Final test (seeds 3000+, dims 7/10/16, 4 seeds per family×dim, 84 tasks): in-distribution isotropic, diagonal κ1000, rotated κ100, rastrigin; held-out families rotated κ1000, rosenbrock, ackley. Curvature domain = diagonal κ1000 + rotated κ100 + rotated κ1000 (36 tasks).
  • Arms (all in the shared loop, budget 100 units, start at problem.x0): fixed (step L ∈ {0.01, 0.03, 0.1, 0.3, 1} chosen on validation only); bb harness reference (L = min(‖g_u‖/R_last, 1) when the newest valid R > 0, else tuned fixed L); lbfgs SciPy L-BFGS-B harness reference (each call = 1 obj + 1 grad, maxfun = 50); trained tf-legacy (v0.5 architecture, 5 features); mlp-h0/4/8 (width 48) and tf-h0/4/8 (width 16, 4 heads, 1 layer, rank 2, geometry_bound=10, lowrank_scale=0.5, scale_aware=True); contextual zero-shot frozen v0.5 overdamped_full. Three training seeds {0, 1, 2}; final-update weights (no checkpoint selection). Updates per arm: 400 (fixed now; a timing probe may only lower it uniformly if one arm exceeds 15 min CPU).
  • Metric: D = log10(r_cand + 1e-10) − log10(r_ref + 1e-10) per task (and training seed); negative favours the candidate. Two-level bootstrap (training seeds, then tasks), 10,000 draws, 95% percentile CI.
  • Primary candidate: tf-h8. H1 (history value): tf-h8 − tf-h0 on the curvature domain, supported iff CI upper < 0. H2 (attention value): tf-h8 − mlp-h8, same rule. H3 (scientific): tf-h8 − fixed, supported iff CI upper < 0 and no test family has mean D > +0.5 with CI lower > 0. Everything else (K=4, MLP, references, budgets 50/200, per-family, held-out families) is secondary and exploratory.
  • Stop rules: H1 fails ⇒ no temporal attention, no G5; report and stop. H3 fails ⇒ fixed geometry stays the default. Temporal attention and G5 each need a new pre-registered round regardless of outcome.
  • Also reported: obj/grad/HVP counts, acceptance, nonfinite rate, first-call and warm runtime, training seconds, parameter counts, checkpoint bytes.
  • Artifacts: artifacts/trajectory-v0.6.0-<arm>-seed<s>.npz (schema, split hashes, RNG provenance in metadata), results/trajectory-curvature-v0.6.0.json. v0.5 artifacts are never written.
  • Resource budget: ≤ 3 h CPU wall-clock training, ≤ 1 h evaluation (96 cores, no GPU).

items.title: NeuralOpt v0.7 Track B: Gram-space history model, pre-registration
items.text: Status: FROZEN on 2026-11-22. The approved draft was revised as instructed. This file's sha256 is recorded in the commit that follows it and in docs/superpowers/specs/2026-11-22-gram-space-v07-preregistration.sha256. No training had been run when it was frozen. Any later deviation goes under "Corrections" in the results report (docs/research/gram-space-v0.7.md), never into this file. Literature: docs/research/trajectory-curvature-literature.md (v0.7 additions, verified against OpenAlex).
path: NeuralOpt v0.7 Track B: Gram-space history model, pre-registration

items.title: 1. Question
items.text: Can a small model that sees only rotation-invariant statistics of K = 10 actually evaluated secant pairs produce an inverse metric P that beats an untrained Barzilai–Borwein (BB) step on unseen rotated and ill-conditioned problems? The comparison uses equal objective+gradient budgets and one frozen step-acceptance rule.
path: NeuralOpt v0.7 Track B: Gram-space history model, pre-registration

items.title: 2. Evidence this design rests on (measured before freezing)
items.text:
• Gate 1, algebraic (passed). With the BFGS coefficients (A = R⁻ᵀ, C = R⁻ᵀD^{1/2}/√τ, τe^δ = γ), P g equals the L-BFGS two-loop direction to within 1e-10, and the coefficients lie inside the model's output ranges. P is SPD for every A and C, the tokens are invariant, and trajectories are rotation-equivariant and invariant to objective scale.
  • Anisotropy of at least 100× is demonstrated. In gate 2 the oracle's P reached condition numbers of 149 at κ = 100 and 1,363 at κ = 1000 (medians of per-run maxima). The frozen v0.6 tf-h8 geometry is capped at about 3.5× off-axis (at most 19.9 measured).
  • Gate 2. It FAILED as written. The amended criterion (regret floor 1e-12; within one decade of SciPy maxcor 10) also fails at κ = 1000.
  • Loop-rule ablation. The step-acceptance rule moves the oracle by at most 0.5 decades.
  • Frozen loop: halving, K = 10.
  • Halving is the strongest rule for the untrained BB-like baseline, so the bar is not weakened.
  • Mask diagnostic. The decision rule was stated before running.
  • Relaxed masks reduce the κ = 1000 median gap by 0.0 decades, so they are not meaningful for the gap.
  • Paired oracle − SciPy at κ = 1000 (d = 7/10/16): mean +0.86 [+0.18, +1.60], median +0.06.
  • The gap sits at d = 10 and is unexplained.
path: NeuralOpt v0.7 Track B: Gram-space history model, pre-registration

items.title: 3. Capacity ceiling (stated, not a target)
items.text:
The oracle uses BFGS coefficients and σ = 1 in the frozen loop with history-v2 masks (harness only). The table gives median log10 regret and the number of tasks reaching 1e-6.

Tasks κ = 100 κ = 1000 Paired oracle − SciPy maxcor 10 gate tasks, d = 7/10/16 (12 per κ) −15.98 (12/12) −6.19 (7/12) κ=1000: +0.86 [+0.18, +1.60] (gap at d = 10, unexplained) validation seeds 8000+, d = 32 (4 per κ) −9.30 (4/4) −5.07 (0/4) κ=100: −0.34 [−0.47, −0.14]; κ=1000: −0.02 [−0.23, +0.20]

The d = 32 values come from results/oracle-ceiling-d32-v0.7.0.json, measured on validation seeds, not test tasks. At d = 32 the oracle matches or beats SciPy L-BFGS-B. The learned model is not expected to exceed this ceiling.
path: NeuralOpt v0.7 Track B: Gram-space history model, pre-registration

items.title: 4. Frozen design
items.text:
• Engine and rule. Compiled engine, float64 throughout (features, training, evaluation). loop_rule="halving": one trial; any finite decrease is accepted; a rejection halves the next trial. No Armijo test, and no BB-based base step inside the model: BB enters only as the τ scale and as a reference arm.
  • Model. model_kind="gram", K = 10 pairs, width 32, 4 heads, 2 layers (14,080 parameters). Output ranges: |A|, |C| < 100; |δ| < 5; σ ∈ [1/4, 4]; ε_rel = 1e-12; fallback length 0.1.
  • history-v2 masks (approved). Schema neuralopt-policy/v0.7-gram-v2, with the thresholds stored in its config.
  • Thresholds: max|s| > 1e-12 and ‖y‖ > 1e-10·max‖g‖, plus finiteness.
  • Reasons: the protocol is float64; the masks are neutral at κ = 1000, reach the floor at κ = 100, and were chosen before training.
  • Coverage. The tokens carry ŜᵀŜ (rank and conditioning of the observed span); P is isotropic on the unobserved complement by construction.
  • Noise-aware reliability is untested: no noisy-gradient family is in this round.
  • Rejection information. The rejection count, the last rejected step length and the ratio of observed to predicted change. Rejected trials never form pairs.
  • No-history control (history_masked=True). Every pair is masked, so the model sees only the gradient token (rejection information and budget fraction) and τ uses its fallback.
  • The training unroll is matched to the evaluation budget of 100 units.
  • The training loop is the inference loop under lax.scan: the same accept_step halving rule, the same budget accounting (start costs 2 units; a trial costs 1, plus 1 if it improved), and the same stopping condition (used + 2 ≤ 100 and a nonzero gradient). Inactive scan steps are masked.
  • The scan length is the maximum number of iterations at budget 100, which is 97. The budget-fraction input is 1 − used/100, as in inference.
  • A parity test against the compiled engine is required before any training: trajectory, history and counts must match to 1e-10.
  • Training settings.
  • Starts are random in the box.
  • Loss: mean over unit horizons {25, 50, 100} of log(normalized incumbent regret + 1e-12), plus 0.1 × the mean over active steps of candidate log-regret.
  • The history buffer (S, Y, f) is treated as observed data: stop_gradient applies in both the tokens and the metric. The meta-gradient flows through the current position and ∇f, so it is second-order; this cost is reported.
  • Adam 1e-3, global-norm clip 1.0, batch 8 tasks per update from one family and dimension group, 2,000 updates, final weights. There is no checkpoint selection and no tuning on any split.
  • NaN guard: a skipped update is counted and reported.
  • Seeds and cost. Five training seeds (0–4) per trained arm.
  • The cost estimate is in the infrastructure report.
  • A 20-update timing probe runs first. It may only lower the update count, uniformly for all arms, and only if one run would exceed 45 minutes.
path: NeuralOpt v0.7 Track B: Gram-space history model, pre-registration

items.title: 5. Tasks and splits
items.text:
Hashes are recorded. Test tasks are built only after training. Everything uses the make_task generator.

  • Training. Families: isotropic, diagonal κ ∈ {10, 100, 1000}, rotated κ ∈ {10, 100, 1000}, Rastrigin. Dimensions {4, 8, 12}, 4 tasks per family and dimension, seeds 7000+ (96 tasks). Objective scale cycles 0.2/1/5 and coordinate scale 0.5/1/2.
  • Validation seeds 8000+. Used only for the d = 32 ceiling. There is no tuning and no selection.
  • Final test. Seeds 9000+, unseen dimensions {7, 16, 32}, 4 tasks per family and dimension (84 tasks).
  • Curvature domain (primary): diagonal κ = 1000, rotated κ = 100, rotated κ = 1000.
  • Equal-spectrum pairs: the same seed gives the same permuted spectrum for diagonal and rotated κ = 1000.
  • Context: isotropic.
  • Reliability-guard families: Rastrigin (in-distribution), and Ackley and shifted Rosenbrock (held out).
  • Shifted Rosenbrock (rosenbrock-shifted) replaces v0.6's seed-independent Rosenbrock. Each replicate has a seeded shift in [−0.5, 0.5]ᵈ, giving a distinct interior minimizer c(1 + shift). This is tested.
  • Budgets. Primary 100 objective+gradient units; secondary 50 and 200.
path: NeuralOpt v0.7 Track B: Gram-space history model, pre-registration

items.title: 7. Metric, statistics and decision rules
items.text:
• Per task: D = log10(r_cand) − log10(r_ref), with r = max(f − f, 0)/|f₀ − f| and log10 r floored at −12. Raw values are reported as secondary. Negative favours the candidate.
  • Intervals. Every contrast gets a 95% paired bootstrap interval with 10,000 draws.
  • Trained arm versus a reference: two-level crossed resampling of training seeds and tasks.
  • Reference versus reference: resampling over tasks only.
  • Five seeds make the seed level coarse; this is stated in the report.
  • Decision rules (all on the 95% paired interval):
  • Superiority: the whole interval is below 0.
  • Non-inferiority at margin m: the upper bound is below +m.
  • Equivalence: the whole interval lies within ±0.5 decades.
path: NeuralOpt v0.7 Track B: Gram-space history model, pre-registration

items.title: 8. Hypotheses and stop rules
path: NeuralOpt v0.7 Track B: Gram-space history model, pre-registration

items.title: Stage 1 (gram-scalar and gram-nohist only)
items.text:
• S1 (non-inferiority): gram-scalar − BB on the curvature domain at budget 100.
  • STOP before Stage 2 only if the upper bound is above +0.25 decades.
  • Reason (recorded): the oracle shows that the headroom over BB comes from the metric (A, C), not the scalar step. A tie at Stage 1 therefore should not end the round.
  • S1b (diagnostic, no stop): gram-scalar − gram-nohist, which measures what the secant τ adds beyond rejection information. Also gram-nohist − BB.
path: NeuralOpt v0.7 Track B: Gram-space history model, pre-registration

items.title: Stage 2 (only if S1 passes)
items.text:
• Primary, H1: gram-full beats BB on the curvature domain at budget 100, meaning the whole interval is below 0.
  • Reliability guard (G): H1 is void if, on any of Rastrigin, Ackley or shifted Rosenbrock, gram-full − BB has a mean above +0.5 with a lower bound above 0.
  • Secondary, H2 (rotation equivalence): for gram-full, the equal-spectrum difference rotated κ1000 − diagonal κ1000 (paired by seed) lies within ±0.5 decades over its whole interval. The same contrast is reported for BB, the oracle, L-BFGS-B and tf-h8 as context.
  • Secondary, H3 (oracle non-inferiority): the upper bound of gram-full − gram-oracle-BFGS on the curvature domain is below +0.5.
  • "Relearned L-BFGS" criterion (R, pre-stated, evaluated only if H3 holds). R is met if both hold:
  • (i) |gram-full − oracle| ≤ 0.25 decades on at least 75% of curvature-domain task × seed pairs;
  • (ii) on 200 fixed probe states (sampled from oracle trajectories on test tasks, seed 0), the median cosine between the model's and the oracle's step directions is at least 0.99.
  • Exploratory: budgets 50 and 200; per-family and per-dimension results; all arms against L-BFGS-B.
path: NeuralOpt v0.7 Track B: Gram-space history model, pre-registration

items.title: Outcome-to-claim table
items.text:
Claims are cumulative within a row. "No claim" means the result is reported but nothing is asserted. Under no outcome is a claim made of superiority over SciPy L-BFGS-B, or of novelty over L-SR1, Optimus, LODO or the v0.7 literature.

Stage 1 S1 H1 Guard G H3 R H2 What we may claim fails (upper > +0.25) — — — — — The learned scalar step is worse than BB beyond the 0.25-decade margin. The round ends; BB stays the bar; no Stage 2. passes fails any any any any Learned geometry did not beat BB on the curvature domain. BB stays the bar. H2 and H3 are reported as exploratory, with no claim. passes passes violated any any any No superiority claim: the curvature-domain gain comes with a reliability regression on a multimodal family. Both are reported as exploratory. passes passes holds fails — passes Beats BB on unseen rotated and ill-conditioned tasks at equal budget, with no measurable rotation penalty (±0.5). It remains short of the oracle-BFGS ceiling. passes passes holds fails — fails Beats BB at equal budget, short of the oracle ceiling. No rotation-invariance claim; the rotated − diagonal gap is reported. passes passes holds passes met passes Beats BB with no measurable rotation penalty, by relearning L-BFGS-like directions in this loop: no evidence of a new method. passes passes holds passes met fails Beats BB by relearning L-BFGS-like directions (no new method). No rotation-invariance claim. passes passes holds passes not met passes Beats BB with no measurable rotation penalty, and is non-inferior to oracle-BFGS (+0.5) without matching its directions. Whether it differs usefully from L-BFGS is not established. passes passes holds passes not met fails Beats BB and is non-inferior to the oracle. No rotation-invariance claim.

If the upper bound of gram-full − oracle is below 0 (better than the oracle), that is reported as "improves on L-BFGS directions in this loop". It is still reported against SciPy L-BFGS-B, with no claim over it.
